Man City found guilty of almost all financial rule breaches

A verdict over Premier League charges against Manchester City is finally set to be delivered after a bombshell report said the club have been “found guilty on almost all of the charges”.

The Independent understands that the former champions have been found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, in what would be a seminal moment for the richest football league in the world.

The landmark ruling, first reported by The Athletic, follows one of the most significant court cases in the history of sport, with the verdict also having major repercussions for City’s rivals. The Premier League have declined to comment, however.

City, currently top of the Premier League after five games, were charged with over 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules in February 2023, with the club always denying any wrongdoing throughout the process.

An independent commission was appointed following a four-year investigation. Sanctions have not yet been decided, according to The Athletic, and City are expected to appeal. A club spokesperson said the Premier League process “remains ongoing”.

City have been England’s most successful team since the club’s fortunes were transformed by Sheikh Mansour’s takeover in 2008. There are a wide range of punishments available to the top-flight’s authorities. Sanctions could include fines and/or points deductions, and even expulsion as a member of the Premier League.

The Duke of Sussex has declared it is "great" to return to Britain, stating that Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are currently "happy in school".

Speaking to Canadian broadcaster CTV following a skydive outside Toronto — performed to fulfill a promise to a 102-year-old Second World War veteran and raise awareness for military charities — Harry shared an update following the family's return on August 26.

Discussing Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, the duke remarked: "The kids are happy in school and it gives me a chance to really focus on Invictus in Birmingham. The games are in July next year."

Reflecting further on his arrival, Harry added: "It’s been great. It’s been great to be back on British soil. It’s great to be back on terra firma, actually!"

open image in gallery Harry insists his children are ‘happy in school’ in the UK ( @meghan/Instagram )

When questioned by CTV regarding the motivation behind their move back from California, where they had established a life after stepping down as working royals in 2020 for personal and financial reasons, Harry offered "lots of reasons" without expanding, explaining he did not wish to overshadow his fundraising work for Canadian veterans.

The family's return to the UK after six years in the US has been accompanied by public disagreement with Buckingham Palace over their official status, alongside logistical adjustments to their children's education.

Uncertainty remains surrounding the rationale for their unexpected move. Speculation ranges from a desire for the children to forge a closer bond with their grandfather the King, to Meghan seeking a return to acting or a move to elevate their profile.

While the King was said to be pleased to spend time with the family prior to their arrival, he reportedly maintained that a half-in, half-out arrangement was off the table, firmly ruling out a return to official royal duties.

open image in gallery Harry and Meghan have been back in the UK for around one month ( Getty )

Tensions surfaced within two weeks of their arrival. A letter, authorised by the King and issued by the Lord Chamberlain to government and military officials, reinforced that the couple are "private citizens" and outlined conduct guidelines.

The duke and duchess were reportedly "surprised" by the memo. The couple, who are awaiting a decision on whether they will receive taxpayer-funded security, reportedly prefer to be designated as "public figures" instead.

Schooling has presented an additional challenge, with Archie and Lilibet transferred to an undisclosed new institution after merely two days in class. The decision followed reports that heavy traffic and an extended commute placed their security detail under strain.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

News.title: Russell capitalises on Antonelli error to take Azerbaijan GP pole
News.content:
Russell – who begins the weekend 81 points behind the Italian – simply has to capitalise. And he really should do. Even if Antonelli hadn’t crashed out, he has looked on a different level this weekend, dominating practice and qualifying. Russell topped Q1, Q3 and Q3, securing the 12th pole of his career with a lap which was nine tenths quicker than his best lap in Q2 and eight tenths quicker than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, the next fastest driver. He could hardly believe it himself.

“That was a pretty decent lap,” he told his team over the radio on his cooldown lap. “How much was [the gap]?”

“Just over eight tenths to Leclerc.” came the response. “Woah!”

This has not been the easiest season for Russell, who began the year the overwhelming favourite for the title, having dominated his younger team-mate over the course of last season. So he could be forgiven for feeling proud of having done such a good job.

“It’s been a while so it definitely feels good,” he admitted. “This was probably the biggest pole margin of my whole career, including my F2 and F3 days.

“The lap felt really sweet, car’s been feeling really great this weekend. On a track like this where you can hug it, it feels amazing.”

News.title: Buttler injury derails England chase and sends Sri Lanka series to decider
News.content:
Enter Buttler to play a wonderful counter-attack, whacking Wellalage for four and six and dumping leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage over the rope twice as he raced to 41 off 22 balls.

Buttler was at a crossroads after the T20 World Cup in February. Despite England making the semi-finals, he averaged just 10 in the tournament to complete a third poor World Cup in a row. A break with his family, and a very good Indian Premier League, where he made a crucial technical correction, changed his fortunes.

Matthew Hayden, the batting coach at the Gujarat Titans, asked him whether he was watching the ball closely enough. Buttler discovered that, now 36, he is a right-eye dominant batsman, so with Hayden’s help he opened up his stance to give himself a better view of the ball. A summer rich in runs has followed with an average of 51 for England and a strut back in his body language. The injury has surely ended Buttler’s summer and there are worries that he could be out of the Pakistan ODI triangular tournament next month as well, just to add to the night’s woes.

This was not a vintage England performance. Atkinson made a crucial error on the boundary, dropping a straightforward chance off Kusal Mendis on 17. It kickstarted Mendis, who went on the charge smashing 51 in 24 balls. He put on 137 in 120 balls with Kuminda Mendis. Josh Tongue had an off day going at seven an over and Jofra Archer was given similar treatment, although he bowled better than figures suggest, as anything wayward with pace on the ball was hit away.

Overton was more effective with his cutters and slower balls, while Ahmed did at least bag a couple of wickets, credit for keeping his head after some early rough treatment. Kusal Mendis was given out leg before on 99 but overturned the decision and stroked a four next ball for a deserved hundred.

News.title: Oil jumps after Saudi thwarts missile attack
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. A global rout in bond markets deepened overnight as traders expect the US to keep raising interest rates.

Japan’s 10-year bond yield surged to 3.08pc on Thursday, its highest level since 1996, as markets responded to stronger than expected US economic data and higher oil prices.

It followed sharp rises in the US on Wednesday, when the yield on 10-year Treasuries – a benchmark of global borrowing costs – surged as high as 5.12pc, up from 4.96pc. It was the biggest jump since the “liberation day” tariff turmoil in April last year.

Bonds were sent into turmoil as traders bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates three times by April next year in an effort to bring down inflation. Money markets suggest there is a 70pc chance of the Fed following this month’s first rate rise in three years with a second in October.

This followed closely watched industry data on Wednesday, known as PMIs, showed US private sector activity jumped unexpectedly to a five-year high in September.

Meanwhile, oil prices spiked 3.9pc on Wednesday to move back above $100 a barrel, risking an inflationary spiral in the world economy.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The main driver was a strong batch of PMIs, along with a rebound in oil prices, which both led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes.” Here is what you need to know.

2) Diesel prices surge as Trump mulls 90-day US export ban | Pump prices could exceed £3 per litre in Britain if Washington imposes ‘catastrophic’ block on exports

5) Chinese carmaker’s new EV battery will charge in under five minutes | Geely says its latest system is fastest in industry as brands approach ‘physical limit’

What happened overnight

Debt markets were in turmoil after Japanese bond yields hit 30-year highs.

As Tokyo markets reopened after a three-day holiday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield jumped to its highest level since 1996.

This came after a steep sell-off in the US market overnight. Oil prices remained around $103 a barrel and the dollar held gains after Tehran’s leader vowed to never surrender following a warning by Donald Trump that he could “annihilate” Iran.

Japan’s benchmark stock market, the Nikkei 225 rose 1pc to 65,645.10, as some chipmakers got a boost from the recent interest in AI. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.7pc to 8,702.00.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost 0.3pc to 24,762.39, while the Shanghai Composite dipped 0.9pc to 4,545.09. Trading was closed in South Korea for the Chuseok autumn harvest holiday.

Sports.title: Defiant Man City chief insists club is INNOCENT despite rules verdict & says ‘there are many who want to undermine us’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak broke his silence with a defiant statement in response to the bombshell guilty verdicts.

News broke on Friday that the Etihad club had been found guilty of huge swathes of Premier League charges brought against them in a four-year investigation.



The ramifications of the unprecedented ruling – which covers the 2009 to 2018 period – and subsequent punishments are still to be determined.

But sanctions could include astronomical points deductions, expulsion from the Premier League, fines and even having titles stripped away.



Now, though, City’s top chief broke his silence with a public message posted on the club’s website and social media.

In it, Al Mubarak reiterated the stance that City are “innocent”.

Sports.title: Ireland’s controversial Nations League clash against Israel to go ahead as planned following vote amongst players

GAME ON Ireland’s controversial Nations League clash against Israel to go ahead as planned following vote amongst players

Credit: SPORTSFILE

IRELAND will face Israel as planned despite a player withdrawing from the squad due to not wanting to be involved in the fixture.

The fate of the game, scheduled to take place in Hungary on Sunday, was cast into doubt after a pre-match press conference and training session were postponed on Saturday morning.



But at a delayed media briefing on Saturday afternoon, FAI CEO David Courell confirmed that the game will proceed following a vote amongst the squad.

That is despite Courell acknowledging that an unnamed player had approached Heimir Hallgrimsson to say that they didn’t want to be involved.



While widespread reports claimed that goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu had expressed his unwillingness to be involved in the game, the identity of the player was not confirmed.

Courell said: “This morning, a player expressed their discomfort with fulfilling this fixture to the head coach and indicated their intent to withdraw from the squad.



“As you can understand, this new variable required time and deliberation for the rest of the squad to consider.

“It was another four hours of conversations, predominantly amongst the players themselves, but also at times with the coaching staff and at times with the executive.

“A lot of positions presented.

“I think it’s important to say that from an association perspective and for everyone involved in those conversations, we were fully respectful for everyone’s right to their respective opinion on these topics.



“Within the last maybe 90 minutes, we carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures.

“And it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.

“Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football that this fixture would continue as we have always intended to fulfill the fixtures.”

Prior to Thursday’s defeat to Kosovo, Dara O’Shea, captain in the absence of Nathan Collins, had intimated that the players would use a team meeting on Friday night to consider gestures for Sunday’s game.

And it was confirmed during Saturday’s press conference that the squad would wear black armbands “in recognition of all lives lost in the conflict.”



The squad would also not be removing themselves from media obligations for the rest of the window as well as “elements of the pre-match ceremony.”

The decision came after a chaotic morning that saw a scheduled press conference and training session postponed.



The press conference was due to take place in Debrecen in Hungary, where the game is taking place, on Saturday morning at 9:15am Irish time.

But that was pushed back, with RTE reporting that the squad was expected to issue a statement outlining its position on playing the fixture as well as the return game in Serbia next week.

It was reported that, 15 minutes before the press conference was due to start, media were told that it was delayed until after training.

UEFA were informed of a further delay with the panel still to travel from their team hotel to the Nagyerdei Stadium.

Two hours later, at 1:30pm Irish time, it was revealed that the training session would be taking place at 2:45pm Irish time, with the postponed press conference at 2:30pm Irish time.

Thomas Tuchel‘s side achieved the Three Lions’ best finish in a major men’s World Cup since 1966 with their third-place in North America.

However, that got us thinking, who are the best one-cap England stars?



SunSport have looked at the record books to come up with the best Three Lions XI of stars who have earned a single cap.

That list includes Premier League and Champions League winners as well as club icons and national heroes.

We’ll start with a pair of names who aren’t necessarily in our starting XI, but stars who are actually in the current squad looking to break the one-cap curse.

Those stars are Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha and Everton‘s Jarrad Branthwaite.

The pair both have a single cap to their names.

He only made one national team appearance due to playing in the era of the likes of Gordon Banks and Peter Bonetti.



In defence we have selected Bill Nicholson, Neil “Razor” Ruddock, Bill Foulkes and Tony Kay.

Tottenham icon Bill Nicholson was a half-back turned wing-half who scored on his international debut against Portugal in 1951 after only 19 seconds with his first touch.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll lays bare every detail of ‘absolutely horrendous’ sexual assault by ‘celeb pal’ in minute-by-minute account
Sports.content:
Next

STANDING in a courtroom facing his abuser for the first time since he was sexually assaulted, Andy Carroll was a nervous wreck.

The traumatic attack, which left him sobbing uncontrollably in the arms of his family’s nanny as he waited for the police to arrive at his home, was a secret he’d kept from almost everyone who knew him.





And getting up on the stand to relive the events of that awful night was excruciating.

“It was humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous,” Andy, 37, recalls in his book, Owning It.

He had been given the option to give his evidence from behind a screen but was urged by the judge to be visible to the jury, adding: “My testimony would be more powerful if they were able to see my face.”

In front of 12 strangers, the former Newcastle United and West Ham star, recounted the horrors of that evening minute by minute.

Andy recalled the frantic texts he sent to his then wife Billi Mucklow, admitting he did not want the man – who was a friend of hers – to be at their home, where their children were sleeping upstairs.

Not wanting to be rude, and feeling obliged by Billi to open the doors to their home, Andy recalled the man, a divorcee with kids, arriving with “two boys” who drove off after dropping the man at the door.

The upsetting events which followed saw Andy waking up in the house to find the man attempting to perform oral sex on him.

Andy reacted furiously and threw the man out of their home, but recalled that the man returned to the door and begged for forgiveness.





He wrote: “He comes back in, starts saying sorry and tries to cuddle me.

“I smack him as hard as I can and he hits the deck.

“I’m sobbing in the nanny’s arms while she’s trying to comfort me while we wait for the police to come.”

For Andy, the trauma of that night’s events were just the beginning of a two-year long battle to get justice.

Without forensics, intimate swabs taken from himself and his attacker, and the evidence police took from his phone of his messages to Billi, Andy believes the man may have gotten away with his crime.

In Owning It, he recounted how the police contacted him a number of times asking for more evidence in a bid to get justice.

And a friend said the trauma of the wait and not knowing compounded Andy’s fragility.

“Andy endured something horrendous but the police investigation and the run up to the trial was equally as difficult for him,” a friend explains.



“It appeared clear from the off that this man wasn’t going to go down without a fight.

“His version of events were wildly different to Andy’s.

“When he was arrested he claimed Andy wanted to have sex with him and then he hit him when he refused.

“At trial, he claimed they’d had consensual sex, and said Andy had struck him afterwards.

“For Andy this was immeasurably difficult and is something he still has to live with, and attempt to process, on a daily basis.”

Andy stuck with the police investigation and said he helped their enquiries as much as he could.

In Owning It, he alluded to police investigating the man for other offences, and recalled how they had urged him to keep going in a bid to help others.

“Andy couldn’t turn his back and run,” a friend adds. He is a decent man and is honourable.



“Despite the toll this took on him, he wanted justice.”

In Owning It, Andy wrote about the difficulties of the trial and revealed the man tried to fight against him.

He wrote: “My abuser denied everything and claimed we’d had consensual sex before I hit him.

“Unfortunately for him, the physical and phone forensics backed me up.

“When the police called to say he’d been found guilty, I started crying uncontrollably.”

The man was sentenced to three years behind bars, placed on the sex offenders register and was banned from entering the village where Andy lived at the time.

His marriage to Billi, 37, later ended with the couple filing for divorce in 2024.

Those close to Andy said he felt unsupported by Billi during the process, admitting: “It was one of a number of factors that led to their marriage ending.



“This was a life altering event for Andy. He felt very alone.”

Andy did not speak about the attack in the time that followed but recalled that meeting his partner Lou Teasdale changed his outlook.

And as he started to write his book, he said he decided to write about his experience.

“By owning what happened to me rather than trying to bury it, perhaps I can have some control over it,” Andy said.

“Rather than it controlling me.”

Friends close to Andy said he had been overwhelmed by the response to Owning It and the reaction to him opening up about the attack.

“Andy knew that opening up about the worst moment of his life could help others,” a friend explained.

“He didn’t rush the decision. He thought about it and talked it through with Lou.

“Ultimately, speaking about it and writing it down made him realise that his experience could help other people.

“He knows it could also inspire others who may not have sought justice to speak to the police.



“Sexual abusers should not be allowed to get away with their crimes.

“Andy wanted to share his story to tell these people they’re not alone and that help is out there.”

LIVERPOOL wonderkid Rio Ngumoha has been left out of England’s matchday squad to face Spain due to a little-known Uefa rule.

The 18-year-old is the unlucky man to miss out as Thomas Tuchel‘s Three Lions take on the world champions at Wembley tonight.



Tuchel named 27 players in his squad for the international fixtures before a numberof pull-outs but had 24 train on the eve of the Spain showdown.

But Uefa rules only allow 23 players to be named in the matchday squad.



That meant Tuchel was forced to axe one star from his group for the game.

And Uefa’s updated squad list confirmed on Saturday morning that Liverpool winger Ngumoha was the player to miss out.

It means the teenager will have to wait for another opportunity to add to his senior England appearances.

Ngumoha has enjoyed a rapid rise through the Three Lions ranks after impressing at Anfield.

He made his senior England debut during the pre-World Cup warm-up friendlies in Florida before being elevated into Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League campaign.

And the fearless winger insisted this week that he wants to prove he deserves to remain part of the manager’s plans.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Ngumoha told talkSPORT: “I don’t even know what to say about the manager, Thomas.

“He’s really helpful, and I think him picking me shows his belief in me and how exciting and explosive he thinks I am.

“All I can do now is just show him again why I should be here for the many more camps and why he thinks I should be a big part of the team and help the team.

“I’d say I’m fearless. I like to take on players, whether it’s one-v-ones, sometimes two-v-ones as well.

“But also, I want to help the team out with goals and assists because at the end of the day, it’s not just about me.”



Ngumoha should still get opportunities during England’s gruelling schedule, with Tuchel’s side facing four matches in just ten days.

The England boss is expected to rotate his squad during the run and has admitted it would be difficult for his stars to play every minute.

Captain Harry Kane, however, is pushing to start all four matches.



Asked whether any player could feature throughout the run, Tuchel said: “Maybe not all of them. It’s not happening, I think. We will use our substitutes. Harry is desperate to start all four and there is a chance he will.

“This would actually be my mindset, to not make so many changes, to keep it going and to give the players we can rely on the trust and responsibility to take the next step and carry this team.

“We have six or seven positions with regular starters but we must look at the reality.”

Tuchel also believes taking players off around the 70-minute mark can make a major difference to managing their workload.

There, he had quoted the Greek Philosopher Socrates. The quote reads: “The only thing I know is that I know nothing.”

Underneath, Maresca wrote: “Time to breathe. Time to analyse. Time to learn.”

‌



City's official response suggested the process was still ongoing. In a statement, they noted that proceedings should remain strictly confidential.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023," they said.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca quoted Socrates on Instagram on Friday (Image: Instagram/@maresca)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

The statement released by City back in February 2023 noted that the club were 'surprised' by the Premier League's decision to bring charges. They also said that "The Club welcomes the review of this matter by an independent Commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position".

‌



While City will have the opportunity to appeal, possible sanctions could be decided on a faster timeline. Punishments could range from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Premier League rivals are also investigating legal action. Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham have already preserved their right to claim compensation due the loss of earnings they suffered due to City's success.

A potential £200million claim in the offing with those clubs reported to be 'planning' to launch an action.

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher responds to Man City guilty verdict with plea to Premier League bosses
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher responds to Man City guilty verdict with plea to Premier League bosses

An independent commission is said to have found Manchester City guilty on 114 of 115 charges for breaches of financial rules, with an appeal now set to be launcged

View 2 Images Noel Gallagher on the pitch with Pep Guardiola after winning the title in 2018

Noel Gallagher has urged Premier League bosses to not punish Manchester City supporters after a landmark verdict was reached on Friday.

‌



City have been locked in a legal battle with the Premier League since 2024 over breaches of financial rules between 2009 and 2018. An independent commission has been deliberating on the 115 charges - of which City vehemently deny - for two years.

‌



But it has now emerged that the eight-time title winners have been found guilty on all but one charge, with City set to appeal the verdict.

‌



Depending on that appeal, it leaves City open to a variety of sanctions - ranging from fines and bans, all the way to points deductions and possibly expulsion from the top-flight.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



There is also the chance that City could be stripped of the titles won during the impacted years. But Oasis superstar Noel has said players and fans shouldn’t bear the brunt for what has happened off the pitch.

“A little surprised because only that the club has assured us all along that they would vehemently deny any of these charges,” he said on the Let Me Talk podcast.

“So it was a bit of a shock to find out we've been found guilty of all but one but really overall quite sad really, sad for the fans and for the players.

‌



“Our focus as fans is always on the pitch and we know what we saw: they won it on the pitch. Whatever goes on in the boardroom it's nothing to do with the supporters or the players, the players won the game and won that [2011-12] title on the pitch.

View 2 Images Noel with Guardiola earlier this year

“Whether some of those players should have been there or not, that's nothing to do with the fans. We were there, we know what we saw.

‌



“Does it taint it? I suppose in the eyes of everybody else in England it would but I know what I saw and I know what I felt.”

The Premier League have yet to officially confirm the result of the independent commission, but City did issue a statement shortly after the reports of the verdict leaked.

A statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

‌



“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Noel and his brother Liam are two of the most famous City supporters and have recently announced a series of dates at the Etihad Stadium as part of their upcoming tour in 2027.

Article continues below

In response to a fan on social media, Liam said: “We’ll win the appeal and all the WET WIPES from other clubs begging for our titles need to sit down…embarrassing.”

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha cut from Thomas Tuchel's England squad to face Spain due to UEFA rules
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha cut from Thomas Tuchel's England squad to face Spain due to UEFA rules

Liverpool wonderkid Rio Ngumoha has impressed after being called up by Thomas Tuchel, but he will not be included in the final squad to face Spain at Wembley

View 2 Images Rio Ngumoha will not feature for England against Spain

Liverpool teenager Rio Ngumoha is the odd man out from England’s squad to face Spain at Wembley.

‌



UEFA rules state only 23 names can be put on the match day squad list which means one player had to be cut from Thomas Tuchel’s group to face the world champions tonight.

‌



UEFA confirmed the updated list this morning and 18-year-old winger Ngumoha is not included in the group. All 24 players in the squad trained yesterday so one player had to be cut.

‌



Ngumoha has been a big hit with England as he made his debut for the seniors in the pre World Cup warm-up friendlies in Florida and was immediately elevated to the seniors for the Nations League campaign.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said this week he was “fearless” and wanted to be a part of success for England. Speaking to talkSPORT, Ngumoha said: "I don’t even know what to say about the manager, Thomas.

"He’s really helpful, and I think him picking me shows his belief in me and how exciting and explosive he thinks I am.

"All I can do now is just show him again why I should be here for the many more camps and why he thinks I should be a big part of the team and help the team.

‌



"I’d say I’m fearless. I like to take on players, whether it’s one-v-ones, sometimes two-v-ones as well. But also, I want to help the team out with goals and assists because at the end of the day, it’s not just about me and the team."

View 2 Images Ngumoha is likely to get his chance during an extended international break

He is certain to get a chance in this run of games - four in ten days - as Tuchel plans to rotate and utilise his squad. Tuchel said on Friday that Harry Kane wants to play all four but otherwise no player can complete them all.

‌



When asked whether a player can play all the games, Tuchel said: “Maybe not all of them. It’s not happening, I think. We will use our substitutes. Harry is desperate to start all four and there is a chance he will.

“This would actually be my mindset, to not make so many changes, to keep it going and to give the players we can rely on the trust and responsibility to take the next step and carry this team. Ideally.

Article continues below

“We have six or seven positions with regular starters but we must look at the reality. This is just my head. If you ask me after the game we may be having a completely different discussion and then we will travel to the Czech Republic and see. I would like to give players a regular start.

“That doesn’t mean they have to stay on the pitch for 90 minutes. It makes a big difference in our opinion if you play 70 or 90. From 70 on it makes a big difference. Up until 70mins its generally fine.”

Sports.title: What Erling Haaland said about Man City's 115 charges before his U-turn confirmed
Sports.content:
What Erling Haaland said about Man City's 115 charges before his U-turn confirmed

Manchester City star Erling Haaland has previously discussed the club facing 115 charges

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has addressed the charges against Manchester City on several occasions (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Erling Haaland has previously insisted he is not concerned by the charges facing Manchester City. On Friday, it was reported that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.

‌



The charges, which relate to alleged financial breaches from 2009 until 2018, were first announced in 2023. A 12-week hearing was overseen by an independent three-person commission between September and December 2024. While sanctions are currently unknown, City will be able to appeal the reported verdict, having consistently denied the allegations.

‌



A club statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

‌



“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Despite the alleged breaches pre-dating Haaland’s arrival at City in 2022, the Norwegian national team have reportedly removed the striker from a scheduled press conference ahead of their Nations League match against Portugal on Sunday. While the U-turn in his schedule prevents Haaland from giving his immediate reaction to the latest update, the City star has made his stance clear on several occasions.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The 26-year-old signed a nine-and-a-half-year deal in January 2025, the longest contract in Premier League history. Haaland emphasised that he had not considered the 115 charges during his negotiations with the club.

“No, I haven't thought of that or anything,” he said at a press conference shortly after signing his contract. “I am confident that the club know what they are doing and I really don't think I should speak too much about this.”

The striker, who has scored 169 goals in 205 games for City, repeated his stance during an international break in March 2025. The forward insisted that he was not concerned about City potentially being punished for the alleged breaches, following his discussions with the club.

‌



“I don't do that, obviously, when I sign a nine-and-a-half-year contract,” Haaland told reporters. “I've said 300 times why I signed the contract. I talked to the club, got a good feeling and agreed to it in the end. That's why.”

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has won two Premier League titles, the Champions League and several other major honours with Manchester City (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



That summer, he reiterated his feelings on the situation when asked about the 115 charges. Haaland explained that he was happy to extend his contract with City, given what he had been told about the case.

“I spoke with the bosses, and in the end, I believe them,” Haaland said to TIME Magazine in July 2025. “It's such a tricky situation for me to even sit there and speak about, because I wasn't really involved in it. So I think the club knows what they're doing. They will sort it out.”

City’s latest update states that the club’s position remains consistent with the statement released in February 2023, which read: “Manchester City FC is surprised by the issuing of these alleged breaches of the Premier League Rules, particularly given the extensive engagement and vast amount of detailed materials that the EPL has been provided with.

Article continues below

“The Club welcomes the review of this matter by an independent Commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position. As such we look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”

Sports.title: Andy Robertson makes feelings clear on Man City 115 charges verdict and Liverpool impact
Sports.content:
Andy Robertson makes feelings clear on Man City 115 charges verdict and Liverpool impact

Former Liverpool star Andy Robertson has had his say on the verdict that Manchester City breached a huge number of Premier League rules

View 2 Images Andy Robertson has had his say on the Man City charges verdict (Image: Nik Moder/Shutterstock)

Tottenham Hotspur left-back Andy Robertson insists it would be wrong for Manchester City’s players to be tarnished by the club’s alleged breach of financial regulations. The Scotland international was part of a Liverpool team which missed out on several major trophies to City, including two Premier League titles by narrow margins.

‌



The news that an independent panel reached a decision emerged on Friday afternoon, sending the world of football into a frenzy. City, who have always denied any allegations of wrongdoing, now face a nervous wait for their punishment after being found to have breached English top-flight rules 114 times

‌



The panel found that City breached the regulations over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, with the club originally charged in 2023. It is understood that the East Manchester side will appeal the verdict.

‌



Every word Mikel Arteta has said about Man City's 115 charges with Arsenal boss refusing to budge READ MORE :

And now Robertson, who made 378 appearances for Liverpool before leaving to join Spurs in the summer, has now had his say on the seismic verdict. The full-back was speaking in Scotland's pre-match press conference before their Nations League clash against Slovenia.

He said: "I think you can hear the shock in my voice. The case has obviously been going on. For me, the [Man City] players showed they were good enough on the pitch.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"I don’t know too much about the charges. But they had an incredible team, one that I loved battling against.

"I don’t think when it comes to these things that players are ever to blame. That’s all I can focus on."

View 2 Images Andy Robertson and Liverpoolmissed out on several major trophies to Man City (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

‌



Premier League clubs are planning potential legal action against City following their guilty verdict. With the club earning huge success during the nine-year period they are accused of breaching regulations, other sides in England look to be after financial compensation.

City claimed eight Premier League titles since the 2011/12 campaign, when they famously snatched the crown from Manchester United on the final day of the season. Domestic cup competitions and one Champions League have also been claimed since 2009, with the legitimacy of those triumphs now under scrutiny.

The Athletic claim that one possible scenario could see all those impacted coming together to launch a class-action lawsuit. United, specifically, are said to be looking into their options and the knock-on effects of City's misconduct on their own success and finances.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

An appeal from City is anticipated first, however, with any action from rival clubs expected to follow that process. It has been further suggested that United have been specifically scrutinising the seasons in which they were most adversely affected.

Topping that list would undoubtedly be the 2011/12 campaign, when Sergio Aguero's iconic last-gasp goal snatched the title away from Old Trafford. City's record-breaking 100-point season, during which United finished as runners-up, also fell within the nine-year period in which City are accused of committing financial breaches.

Article continues below

The same situation occurred during the campaign without supporters following the Covid-19 pandemic, though this came after 2018, which marks the final season under the club's investigation period.

Missing out on those trophies would almost certainly have had financial consequences for the club, including prize money and Club World Cup qualification.

Sports.title: Man City chairman responds to reports surrounding 115 charges
Sports.content:
Reports on Friday claimed an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case – and that virtually all were found to have been proven; Man City deny all wrongdoing

Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has reaffirmed his belief the club will prove their innocence in the 115 charges case following reports on Friday.

Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges were found to have been proven.

However, in a statement released on Saturday afternoon, the City chairman said: "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Describing his stance on the situation, Al Mubarak said in a message to City's supporters: "Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Al Mubarak then pointed readers to the statement the club made on Friday and a statement issued in February 2023.

He also insisted the situation had not changed.

He said: "While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium - moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family."

Sports.title: Russell holds off Verstappen to win by 0.1s in thrilling Azerbaijan GP finale
Sports.content:
George Russell held off Max Verstappen in a thrilling finale to claim victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by just a tenth of a second.

Mercedes' Russell had been on course for a dominant victory before two Safety Cars wiped out the 11-second lead he had built and left him desperately defending Red Bull's Verstappen in the closing stages.

The lights-to-flag triumph reduces Russell's deficit to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the world championship to 66 points after the Italian fought back from 16th on the grid, following a qualifying crash, to finish fifth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell fended off Max Verstappen for the win.

Isack Hadjar took third to seal Red Bull's first double-podium since the 2024 Chinese Grand Prix, completing an impressive comeback after missing three races with a wrist injury.

Charles Leclerc took fourth for Ferrari after dropping back from second in the early stages, while his team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished where he started in sixth after lacking pace throughout.

Lando Norris was taken out of the race along with Pierre Gasly when the latter's Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto crashed into them at the restart after the first Safety Car interruption, which had been caused by Williams' Alex Albon crashing out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The result leaves Russell as the only realistic threat to Antonelli claiming the title, with third-placed Hamilton now 103 points back, and fourth-placed Norris 116 points off the lead with eight rounds remaining.

Mercedes also took another step towards sealing a first constructors' title since 2021, moving 160 points clear of Ferrari at the top of the standings.

That multi-car collision opened up points-scoring opportunities for others, with Arvid Lindblad taking seventh after overtaking Haas' Esteban Ocon on the run to chequered flag.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alex Albon found himself in the wall at Turn Five, bringing out the safety car at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Oliver Bearman was just behind them to secure a double-points finish for Haas, while Carlos Sainz took the final point for Williams as he overcame a five-place grid penalty and losing time from pitting before the first Safety Car, unlike most of the field.

Another dismal weekend for Aston Martin saw both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll fail to finish the race after suffering technical issues.

Azerbaijan GP Result: Top 10 1) George Russell, Mercedes



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



6) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



7) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



8) Esteban Ocon, Haas



9) Oliver Bearman, Haas



10) Carlos Sainz, Williams

Supreme Russell overcomes Safety Car scare

Russell had been imperious as he took pole by the best part of a second on Friday, and backed up that performance by making a fine start to comfortably retain the lead, while Piastri got past Leclerc behind him.

While it took Verstappen just seven laps to surge from eighth on the grid up to third, Piastri then provided a blocker that had enabled Russell to build an 11-second lead by the time Albon crashed into the barrier with the leaders on their 31st lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell holds onto the lead on the opening lap of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The field poured into the pits during the stoppage before a short-lived restart at the start of lap 36.

Russell controlled the rolling restart well, but Verstappen got past Piastri before chaos ensued behind, with Colapinto locking up before sliding into Gasly, who was shunted into the path of Norris.

That left Russell with the speedy Verstappen on his rear wing when the race restarted with 13 laps remaining.

Another well-managed restart kept Russell in front, but he was unable to shake Verstappen, creating a tense finale.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen gain several places with brilliant overtakes as they work together in the early stages of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Russell appeared to have seen off the threat as the final lap begun, but the stricken Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas caused him to slow under yellow flags and threw off his energy deployment for the remainder of the lap.

That gave Verstappen an opportunity, and the Dutchman was very nearly able to claim his first victory of the season, as he closed to within 0.196s as the pair took the chequered flag.

The margin was the smallest a race has been decided by since Michael Schumacher beat Rubens Barrichello by 0.011s as Ferrari stage-managed the finish of the 2022 United States Grand Prix.

Russell said: "The first half of the race felt pretty plain-sailing, getting the gap. The Safety Car restart with Max behind I thought 'this is not going to be easy' and he drove incredibly at the end of the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell describes his tense showdown with Max Verstappen for the Azerbaijan GP win.

"When the yellow flag came out [for Bottas crash] I lifted off the power and when I went back, I had no turbo, so then I had no power and Max almost got me at the line

"That would have been a real shame but all in all an incredible weekend."

It would have been extremely cruel for Russell to miss out on victory on what had been his most complete weekend of the season since the opening round in Australia back in March.

While Russell still has an enormous task on his hands to catch Antonelli, especially given he will receive a grid penalty for taking a new engine at one of the remaining races, the result provides the Brit with a huge confidence boost after being outperformed by his team-mate for much of the season.

The victory brought Russell back level with Antonelli on eight career wins after the Italian had moved ahead of him last time out in Madrid.

"It's amazing to be back on the top step of the podium," Russell added. "I want to say a big thanks to the team for continuing to believe in me through the tough moments and helped me come through it. I'm really proud to have had this weekend."

Sports.title: Slovenia v Scotland: Nations League – live
Sports.content:
now 10.34 EDT 73 min: Ferguson’s delivery is sublime and met by the head of McBurnie, whose header brings a reflex save out of Oblak from point-black range. Scotland are not so much knocking on the door as trying to kick it open. Share

26s ago 10.33 EDT 72 min: Lewis Ferguson tries his luck with a pot-shot from distance but his effort is blocked. Moments later, Stephen Welsh picks out Bowie with a terrific slide-rule pass. The substitute is unable to lift the ball over Oblak, who puts it out for a corner. Share

3m ago 10.31 EDT 70 min: Kieron Bowie chops inside a defender and sends a low shot straight at Oblak. The susbtitute kicks out in frsutration at a divot as he too glares accusingly at the cut-up pitch. Share

5m ago 10.29 EDT 66 min: Kieron Bowie is on for Robbie Ure and Scotland have another corner. McGinn’s delivery is excellent and met by Aaron Hickey. He sends his header drifting narrowly wide of the far post. Share

8m ago 10.25 EDT 64 min: Scotland finally win a corner and have to wait to take it as Slovenia make a double-substitution. Zec and Zabukovnik come on for Drkusij and Elsnik. Nothing comes of the set-piece. Share

11m ago 10.23 EDT 62 min: McBurnie connects with a McGinn cross and his header goes over the bar off the head of David Brekalo. Slovenia are awarded a goal-kick, much to McBurnie’s disgust. Scotland’s wait for a first corner goes on. Share

12m ago 10.21 EDT 61 min: Ure latches on to a first-time pass from GIlmour and wins a corner for Scotland, their first of the match. Actually it isn’t – the Sevilla man was offside. Share

14m ago 10.20 EDT 59 min: Gilmour and McBurnie combine to good effect on the edge of the Slovenia penalty area but the Napoli midfielder’s low shot doesn’t trouble Oblak, who gets down to save comfortably. Share

15m ago 10.19 EDT 59 min: Scotland have been much improved in this second half but with their high line, still look extremely vulnerable to counter-attacks. Share

16m ago 10.18 EDT 56 min: John McGinn is clattered by Adam Cerin and wins a free-kick near the centre-circle in the Slovenia half. Lewis Ferguson lofts the ball into the penalty area, where Oblak comes for it and doesn’t get it. Stephen Welsh tries to lob the loose ball towards the vacant goal but Vanja Drkusic heads it away and wins a free-kick. Share

18m ago 10.15 EDT 54 min: McGinn tries to stand the ball up for McBurnie near the byline and the Scotland striker leaps to contest it with Oblak. The Slovenian looked to have carried it wide for a corner but wins a free-kick because an outfield player had the audacity to jump in the same postal district as him. Goalkeepers, eh? Share

21m ago 10.13 EDT 51 min: Oof! Oli McBurnie is played in behind the Slovenia defence and finds himself in a one-on-one with Oblak. The Slovenia goalkeeper’s legs are gaping and you could drive a bus between them, but McBurnie tries to take the ball around him instead of going for the nutmeg. Oblak almost certainly can’t believe his luck as he plucks the ball off the Scottish striker’s toe. Share

23m ago 10.10 EDT 50 min: Scotland have started the second half on the front foot but are struggling to create anything much in the way an opening. They’re playing with a high line today but their wing-backs Robertson and Aaron Hickey are struggling to have any sort of impact on the game. Share

26m ago 10.08 EDT 46 min: John McGinn spins his man, gallops up the right flank and plays the ball inside to Billy Gilmour. His pass wide to Andy Robertson takes a massive bobble off the poor surface and the Scottish captain is unable to control the ball. Share

28m ago 10.06 EDT Second half: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland 46 min: Scotland get the ball rolling, with no changes in personnel on either side and the sound of bagpipes audible in the Ljubljana air. Share

42m ago 09.52 EDT Half-time: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland Peeeeeeeep! It’s scoreless at the break although both teams have hit the woodwork. Scotland finished the half with something of a flourish but were poor for the first 40 minutes. The Slovenian trio of Matko, Sturm and Sporar have caused Scotland’s defence all manner of problems and will rue their missed chances during a long period of first-half dominance. Share

45m ago 09.49 EDT 45 min: Another excellent pass from McGinn and Robbie Ure’s low daisy-cutter from distance hits the foot of the right post. Much, much better from Scotland. Share

46m ago 09.48 EDT 43 min: An excellent pass from John McGinn sends Robbie Ure on his way down the left and his cross drops at the feet of McBurnie whose back is to goal. He tees up Hickey, whose shot is blocked. View image in fullscreen Hickey, right takes a shot. Photograph: Igor Kupljenik/AP Share Updated at 10.02 EDT

48m ago 09.46 EDT 42 min: Andraz Sporar wins a free-kick wide on the left after the referee unfairly judges Aaron Hickey to have fouled him as the pair contested a 50-50 ball. Nothing comes of it. Share

50m ago 09.44 EDT 40 min: We’re approaching half-time and Scotland have yet to have a shot on or off-target. They’ve had one touch of the ball in the Slovenia penalty area. Share

51m ago 09.43 EDT 37 min: Gunn races off his line to collect a free-kick but gets nowhere near it. His blushes are spared by the linesman’s offside flag. The pitch at the Sozice Stadium is cutting up really badly. Share

53m ago 09.40 EDT 35 min: On the advice of the fourth official, Andy Robertson is penalised for some sort of off-the-ball incident he got embroiled in with Zarnicek. I’m not sure what he’s supposed to have done and judging by his reaction, neither is he. Share

55m ago 09.38 EDT 34 min: Scotland get forward again but are having trouble getting long balls to stick upfield. I suspect Oli McBurnie will not be pleased with his own contribution in this first half, after five years out of his naitonal side. His hold-up play has been poor on the few occasions the ball has come his way. Share

1h ago 09.37 EDT 31 min: Slovenia corner. Vanja Drkusic connects with the inswinger at the near post and hits the outside of said upright. It was a decent effort from a tricky position. Share

1h ago 09.35 EDT 30 min: It hasn’t been the most exciting of football matches thus far but the lively Aljosa Matko gets the locals off their seats with a wild shot from a tight angle that goes harmlessly wide. Share

1h ago 09.32 EDT 27 min: Jack Hendry puts the ball out for a corner under pressure from Sturm. I think he was trying to pass the ball back to Gunn, but his delivery was dreadful. The Scotland defender casts an accusatory glance in the direction of the pitch and nothing comes of the set-piece, which is overhit. Share

1h ago 09.29 EDT 26 min: Gunn goes Route One, booting the ball long and far down the middle. Slovenia win the header. Share

1h ago 09.28 EDT 24 min: Matko gets on the ball down the right flank again, pouncing on a misplaced Gilmour pass. Slovenia work the ball across to the other side of the pitch but are forced backwards by Scotland. Share Updated at 09.29 EDT

1h ago 09.26 EDT 22 min: Scotland have got a foothold in the game after being dominated early doors but have yet to fanshion anything resembling a scoring chance. On another day, Slovenia could be 2-0 up already. Share

1h ago 09.24 EDT 19 min: McBurnie loses the ball halfway inside his own half but Lewis Ferguson immediately wins possession back for Scotland. Robertson and Gilmour combine down the inside left, trying to find an opening. Share

1h ago 09.22 EDT 17 min: Scotland try to play the ball out from the back under a heavy Slovenian press. John McGinn draws a foul from David Brekalo and the visitors get a chance to ease the pressure. View image in fullscreen McGinn gets to his feet after a challenge by Brekalo and Cerin. Photograph: Igor Kupljenik/AP Share Updated at 09.35 EDT

1h ago 09.20 EDT 16 min: Slovenia corner. Robbie Ure clears the inswinger with a thumping header at the near post. Share

1h ago 09.19 EDT 14 min: Danijel Sturm latches on a toa long diagonal and sends in a low cross from the left. Sporar gets in front of McKenna and somehow steers his effort wide of the far post. That’s an awful miss and a huge let-off for Scotland. Share

1h ago 09.16 EDT 11 min: Andy Robertson tries to play Robbie Ure in behind the Slovenian with a weighted pass but overhits his delivery. Slovenia break upfield and Aljosa Matko drills in a low cross in from the right but neither Sporar nor Sturm are able to get on the end of it. Slovenia are looking dangerous, while Scotland look very porous at the back. Share

1h ago 09.14 EDT 9 min: Oli McBurnie is penalised for a blatant barge on Drkusic as he jumped to try to connect with a cross from the left. Aaron Hickey’s follow-up shot is blocked but wouldn’t have counted anyway. Share

1h ago 09.12 EDT 8 min: Slovenia carve Scotland open and Danijel Sturm converts a cross from the right, arrowing a shot past Angus Gunn from about 12 yards out. The flag goes up! Share

1h ago 09.09 EDT 5 min: Angus Gunn advances off his line to grab a cross that Scott McKenna was about to head clear. The Dinjamo Zagreb defender heard the shout from his goalkeeper and left it to him. Share

1h ago 09.07 EDT 3 min: John McGinn tries to advance upfield but is held by Slovenia centre-back Vanja Drkusic. The Scottish midfielder appeals for a free-kick but doesn’t get one. Share

1h ago 09.06 EDT 3 min: Erik Janza hoys a long throw into the Scotland penalty area, where Angus Gunn leaps to claim the ball at the second time of asking. Share

1h ago 09.05 EDT Slovenia v Scotland is go ... 1 min: Following a coin-toss that couldn’t be conducted until Slovenia defender Jaka Bisol had been summoned to join his captain Jan Oblak, Scotland’s captain Andy Robertson and the referee, the game kicks off. I’m going to hazard a guess that the Leeds defender might be the ref’s Slovenian point of contact out on the pitch because Oblak will be in goal. If you know better, feel free to get in touch and educate me. Share Updated at 09.10 EDT

2h ago 08.59 EDT Not long now: Led by Romanian referee Horatiu Fasnic and his team of match officials, the teams march out on to the Stadion Sozice sward and line up for the anthems. The players of Scotland are wearing red (well, coral or salmon pink, if you want to be pedantic) shirts, blue shorts and red socks. Kick-off is just a couple of minutes away. Share

2h ago 08.38 EDT Sebastien Pocognoli: “We had a good camp, we reached all the aspects that we wanted to reach on the pitch but also off the pitch,” said Scotland’s head coach during his press conference at the Stozice Arena. “Regarding the first game for Scotland, I’m excited because we want to see what we worked on this week. I’m very curious to see if we can produce this. I hope we are well balanced, well focused and well concentrated in the good moment, but also in the challenging moments. “The mental aspect to have a first game with a new gaffer, with new ideas, it’s a consideration, the mental aspect. We try to plan the games on the physical aspect, the tactical aspect and on the performance aspect. These will be the last details.” After today’s game against Slovenia, Scotland are scheduled to play Switzerland at Hampden Park on Tuesday. Following that, they’ll face North Macedonia next Saturday before wrapping up the lengthy internatinoal break with a home game against today’s opponents the following Tuesday. Share

2h ago 08.34 EDT View image in fullscreen Billy Gilmour starts in midfield for Scotland today after missing out on the World Cup due to a knee injury he picked up in a warm-up game against Curacao. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA Share

2h ago 08.31 EDT Andy Robertson: This isn’t the Scotland skippper’s first Slovenian rodeo, as both he and the home team’s head coach Bostjan Cesar were on the pitch when last these two sides met in 2017. “When the international break comes we always get excited for it,” he said yesterday. “This one’s no different and we look forward to the challenge ahead that we’ve got. It’s been enjoyable. We’ve had a good week. Obviously, the manager’s trying to get his ideas across. “It’s a really new squad, we’re trying to get to know each other, trying to make sure we keep the values that have worked well for us but also adapting to the new squad and the new characters. It’s been a really important week. I think the manager’s enjoyed it. I think the staff have enjoyed it. It’s all about preparing for the games now. We’ve got four games, which is quite unique. It’s something that we’re all looking forward to. “We’re going to be tested. Saturday, Tuesday, Saturday, Tuesday is intense when you’re at club level. We’re not really used to that kind of schedule at international level. It’s going to be intense, but at the end of the day, footballers want to play football. I suppose it will be a learning curve for us, but one that we want to learn on the job. We still demand results and we still expect results. It’s up to us to try and produce them.” View image in fullscreen Andy Robertson (left) will win his 98th cap for Scotland this afternoon. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA Share

2h ago 08.04 EDT Slovenia v Scotland line-ups Slovenia (possible 4-4-2): Oblak; Brekalo, Bijol, Drkusic, Janza; Karnicnik, Cerin, Elsnik, Matko; Sturm, Sporar. Subs: Vidovsek, Leban, Balkovec, Zabukovnik, Kuzmic, Begic, Lovric, Celar, Svetlin, Zec, Vipotnik, Horvat. Scotland (possible 5-3-2): Gunn; Hickey, McKenna, Hendry, Welsh, Robertson; McGinn, Gilmour, Ferguson; McBurnie, Ure. Subs: Kelly, Bain, Binks, Doig, Christie, Miller, McPake, Gannon-Doak, Graham, Bowie, Patterson, Montgomery. Share

3h ago 08.01 EDT Oli McBurnie starts for Scotland Scotland: Sebastien Pocognoli picks his first Scotland team and has handed debuts to Swansea City centre-back Stephen Welsh and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure. Oli McBurnie also gets the nod and will make his first appearance for Scotland since March 2021. Share

3h ago 07.55 EDT Early Slovenia team news: The headline story from the home camp is that Benjamin Sesko has withdrawn from their squad. The Manchester United striker has featured in six Manchester United games this season, mainly off the bench, but is suffering from a shin injury. “I am very sorry that I will have to miss the next matches of the national team,” he posted on Instagram. “I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride. The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery. “I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again.” Slovan Bratislava striker Andraz Sporar could lead the Slovenia line in the big man’s absence. Defenders Kenan Bajiric and Marcel Ratnik have also been forced out of the squad with injury. Goalkeeper Jan Oblak will skipper the Slovenia side and is set to earn his 85th international cap. View image in fullscreen The Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has pulled out of Slovenia’s squad as he continues to struggle with a shin injury. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Nigel French/Apl/Sportsphoto Share

3h ago 07.55 EDT Early Scotland team news: After his omission from Scotland’s World Cup squad caused no end of consternation, Oli McBurnie earns the recall his early-season Premier League performances for Hull City deserve. He is joined by a host of untried talent, including Luis Binks (Brondby), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Josh McPake (Hearts), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), Colby Donovan (Celtic), John McCracken (Bradford City) and Stephen Welsh (Swansea City). There is no place in Pocognoli’s squad for World Cup particpants Lyndon Dykes, Ross Stewart, George Hirst, Grant Hanley, John Souttar and Anthony Ralston, while goalkeeper Craig Gordon has retired. Scott McTominay, Che Adams, Lawrence Shankland are all unavailable through injury, while Kenny McLean and Kieran Tierney also withdrew from the squad earlier this week. Along with McBurnie, Aaron Hickey, Lewis Ferguson, Josh Doig and Kieron Bowie return to the Scotland squad after missing out on World Cup selection. View image in fullscreen The Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana, where Slovenia will host Scotland today. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA Share

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca posts ‘I know nothing’ message after Manchester City’s guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, posted a cryptic message on social media reading “I know nothing” after the club was found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.

News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty on almost all of more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, prompting reactions from figures associated with the club. City have always denied all counts and are expected to appeal.

Oasis’ Noel Gallagher, a longtime City fan, has described his shock at the news, while the club’s former chair David Bernstein believes “money is not sufficient” in terms of a potential punishment. The culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, described the case as unsettling for football fans and is hopeful of a swift resolution.

On Saturday morning, Maresca was approached for comment about whether he is seeking reassurance from the club on their continued stance of innocence. The Guardian was sent by his representatives a screenshot of a quote by Socrates, the Greek philosopher, which Maresca posted on Instagram.

The quote reads: “The only thing I know is that I know nothing.” Maresca also wrote: “Time to breathe. Time to analyse. Time to learn.”

On the Let Me Talk podcast, Gallagher said: “A little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges.

“So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we’ve been found guilty of all but one. But really just quite sad. Sad for the fans and for the players.”

View image in fullscreen Noel Gallagher, a longtime Manchester City fan, is ‘sad for the fans and for the players’. Photograph: Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty Images

Asked if it changes the context of moments like Sergio Agüero’s title-winning goal in 2012, Gallagher said: “Our focus as fans is always on the pitch and we know what we saw.

“Whatever goes on in the boardroom, it’s nothing to do with the supporters or the players. The players won that game and won that title on the pitch. Whether some of those players should have been there or not, that’s nothing to do with the fans.

“Does it taint it? I suppose in the eyes of everybody else in England it would, but I know what I saw and I know what I felt.”

Bernstein, City’s chair from 1998-2003, told Times Radio: “I felt absolutely awful, I felt in shock yesterday. You’ve asked me on the programme because of my time as chair of City and the FA, but basically I’m a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“When I was chair I think I helped get the club out of a very difficult period and started the road to better things. But to see all this tarnished in this way is very sad.

“I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who’ve stayed with the club through thick and thin. It’s a pretty bad day for the fans in blue of Manchester.”

As for the correct punishment, Bernstein said: “First of all, the timing is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process has to be done quickly because you’ve got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it’s just not viable.

“The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case, but for English football generally.

“I can’t give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty. All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that.”

On BBC Radio 5 Live, Nandy said: “Most football fans will be feeling this is not a good moment for football as a whole and Manchester City fans will be feeling very anxious about what happens next.This is a really longstanding investigation, it dates all the way back to allegations that begin in 2009.

“The football fans need to know the rules are applied fairly and consistently, they need to know they’re upheld and they need to know the right decision has been reached.

“We do have a way to go with this, it’s very unsettling for football fans and I hope it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.”

Nigel Huddleston, who was shadow secretary of state for culture from 2025 to 2026, stated on X: “Whatever the next steps are, they must be conducted in an accelerated and more transparent manner or risk further damage to the reputation and integrity of English football and more unnecessary anxiety for millions of football fans.”

A City spokesperson said on Friday: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sports.title: Liverpool rehire Julian Ward as sporting director to replace Richard Hughes
Sports.content:
Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as their sporting director for a second time after the departure of Richard Hughes to Al-Hilal. Ward, who was Liverpool’s sporting director for the 2022-23 season, has spent the past two years as technical director for Fenway Sports Group, the club’s owners.

The process of finding a successor to Hughes, who left for the Saudi Pro League after two and a half years at Anfield when the summer transfer window ended, was led by the FSG president, Mike Gordon.

Ward has worked in various capacities for Liverpool over the past 14 years, including European scouting manager, assistant sporting director and sporting director.
