Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua in chaos as Gypsy King claims rival wants to pull OUT of  £150m Cardiff mega fight just over 24 hours after bout was confirmed
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury’s heavyweight blockbuster with Anthony Joshua has been thrown into chaos after the Gypsy King claimed his rival is pulling out of the Cardiff contest.

In a dramatic escalation a little over 24 hours after their £150million bout was confirmed, Fury took to Instagram to say the fight is now in jeopardy owing to a feud between Joshua’s promoter Eddie Hearn and the UFC’s Dana White.

White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia’s boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and had fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest.

In an expletive-laden Instagram video, Fury claimed the fight has been cancelled because of Hearn's ego – and that he is 'making up a million different things'.

He said: 'Breaking News: Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight they are saying he is not going to fight now.

'They're little s*** house cowards, mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego, he's making up a million different things and threatening that "we're not going to fight" you little coward.

'AJ pull your finger out you white flag, yellow-bellied coward. You know now we're coming home, now I'm coming home the Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdom to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales.'

Tyson Fury announced the news in a video on social media

Fury and Joshua's fight was due to take place on Friday December 11. The pair were set to meet for a press conference next week on September 30

Fury exchanges words with Anthony Joshua after his fight in April 2026

Fury went on to call Joshua a 'body-building sausage'.

He also claimed that Al-Sheikh is now looking to find a new person to fight Fury at 'the drop of a hat'.

Fury continued: 'So I hope [Hearn and Joshua] are happy you little cowardly b*******, I've never seen anything like [Hearn and Joshua] you pure s*** houses and this is mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. What a little p****.'

The 38-year-old then posted a mocked up poster of himself and light heavyweight champion David Benavidez, hinting that the 29-year-old American could replace AJ in the Cardiff contest.

Fury and Joshua, 36, are due to meet on September 30 in a pre-fight press conference, but Hearn warned that White – who he labelled a ‘loser’ and a ‘soppy t**’ after the fight was confirmed – must not be present at the London face off.

But Fury now claims that this latest demand could see the fight unravel. In a stinging response, Al-Sheikh also threw his weight behind White by posting a photo of the American smoking a cigar on Instagram.

It is understood that both men would have pocketed around £75million for arguably the biggest bout to be staged on British soil.

Hearn had also succeeded in forcing the promotion’s Saudi backers to scrap plans to stage the showdown in New York.

Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff.

The event, broadcast on Netflix, was expected to take place around 2am to accommodate a US audience.

This is a breaking news story. More to follow.

Sports.title: The many faces of Wayne Rooney: From the fresh-faced teenager who took the world by storm to his remarkable Disney glow-up - but football legend insists he has NOT been on the weight-loss jabs
Sports.content:
The many faces of Wayne Rooney: From the fresh-faced teenager who took the world by storm to his remarkable Disney glow-up - but football legend insists he has NOT been on the weight-loss jabs

Wayne Rooney: hotshot, superstar, manager, pundit. And a husband, and a father.

The Manchester United icon has been involved in football for more than 20 years now. He started off as a teenager with high hopes at Everton, and is now one of the faces of football analysis on the tele.

After initially enduring some growing pains in his punditry career, the 40-year-old came into his own over the World Cup, and is now one of BBC's top dogs on Match of the Day and has a family documentary – The Real Rooneys – with wife Coleen and his family.

And, as he continues on his punditry journey, his looks appear to change too. Fans have been stunned by his recent weight loss and, dare we say it, glow up – which has included nose surgery.

Rooney went under the knife over the summer post-World Cup, correcting breathing difficulties he had endured from two separate injuries in his playing career.

'It's actually really lucky I've got no black eyes, but I've still got two plastic tubes up my nose, which are coming out very soon,' Rooney shared last month.

Wayne Rooney burst onto the scene at Everton at the age of 16 and suited up to sign his contract in January 2003

After joining Manchester United, he formed a love-hate relationship with club team-mate Cristiano Ronaldo (left)

'I can't wait for them to come out. So, they've cut here (under the nostrils). So, that's all stitched, a little bit uncomfortable.'

That may be now, but there were no thoughts of plastic surgery when he was a teenager with a dream.

After joining Everton at the age of nine, a fresh-faced Rooney would make his first team debut – and announce himself to the world – at 16. The Toffees, responsible for ending Arsenal's 30-game unbeaten run in October 2002, secured a last-minute winner against the Gunners through Rooney, and he was first team regular thereafter.

It seems a long time ago now – a youthful-looking Rooney suited up after signing his new deal with the Toffees in January 2003 – but it wasn't long until he was on his way to Manchester United.

He secured a £27million move to United in the summer of 2004, picking up around £50,000-a-week.

It was there he would really kick on. He won the Golden Boy trophy in 2004, before eventually winning his first Premier League title in the 2006-07 season.

He became a household name as he continued his fine form after moving to Manchester

His wife - and childhood sweetheart - Coleen (right) was by his side and hit the mainstream

As time went on, it was evident that Rooney's hair began to thin - so he decided to take action

He had tried the bald look, particularly around the 2010 World Cup, in which England failed

He had, by that point, become a household name, forming a love-hate relationship with a similarly babyfaced Cristiano Ronaldo, who was his team-mate at club level but arch enemy on the international stage.

Rooney was in somewhat of a bulking phase. Turning from boy to man. Naturally, with success on the field came public interest off it too, and his wife, Coleen, entered the limelight.

Wayne and Coleen had been together since they were children, with the latter catapulted into WAG stardom due to Rooney's success. The couple would attend events together, and had their first child, Kai, in 2009.

By that point, it became clear Rooney's hair was thinning, and a photo of the forward and United manager Sir Alex Ferguson in April 2011 highlighted that perhaps more than had been done before.

Rooney had tried the bald look – famously turning out for England at the 2010 World Cup with a shaved head. We'll ignore the outburst at Three Lions fans after the 0-0 with Algeria.

It was in 2011 that Rooney had his now-infamous hair transplant, joking that he had gone bald at a young age. He was 25 at the time.

He had a hair transplant, which would become infamous, and appeared happy with the results

He joked in a social media post: 'I was going bald at 25 why not,' with Coleen also commenting

Coleen, meanwhile, shared: 'Hiya!! Yes waynes had his hair done! His own decision not me asking him, like alot are saying!!'

Rooney rocked up to the 2011-12 season with a full head of hair and stern hairline again.

'I was going bald at 25 why not,' he posted on Twitter. 'I'm delighted with the result.'

He would also add that the area was 'a bit bruised and swollen' and joked: 'Anyone recommend any good hair gel. Haha.'

Things didn't totally work out. Just two years later, in June 2013, he had a second transplant. Harley Street Hair Clinic, who carried out the procedure, said the plan was also to carry out work for a second time, rather than it being a situation of their work failing.

Wayne stayed quiet on that one, but Coleen said on Twitter: 'That's what happens!! It falls out before it grows back!!'

In 2011, for what it's worth, she said: 'Hiya!! Yes waynes had his hair done! His own decision not me asking him, like alot are saying!! Pleased for him and it will look great x.'

Rooney had a second hair transplant in 2013, with the clinic insisting it was always the plan

By 2017, Rooney was England's captain, though trophies dried up with Manchester United

He would return to boyhood club Everton after leaving United, though only for a year

A move to the United States followed as he started playing for MLS side DC United

By 2013, at 27, Rooney was a prolific winner. He had lifted the Premier League five times, the Champions League, the Club World Cup and three League Cups.

Having first captained England in 2009, he became the permanent skipper in August 2014.

He was rocking the beard to go with the new trim, and, in his latter years at United, often went for a cleaner look with shorter hair.

By 2017, though, it was clear his time at United was coming to an end. He had been less effective in forward positions, often dropping deeper into attacking or even central midfield roles, and was receiving a lot of criticism.

He had already nearly left United at the turn of the decade, and did leave in the summer of 2017. He exited Old Trafford as the club's all-time top goal scorer with 253 goals in 559 games, a feat he achieved earlier in the year.

Having won the Europa League in his final game with United, he would return to Everton in a move that split fan opinion. Previous visits to Goodison Park as a United player had been mixed, but supporters were largely on board with his return.

Rooney served just 18 months of his three-and-a-half-year contract before returning to England with Derby County

He would take on a player-coach role before taking over officially following the sacking of Philippe Clement

Rooney's grey beard stood strong as he stood beside Coleen in her Wagatha Christie case

He appeared to be putting on the pounds, though, as he plunged further into retirement

By late 2024, Rooney looked completely different to his playing day, with his last management job ending in January 2024

Now 31, Rooney was clearly getting towards the end of his career, but still a capable player. He netted a hat-trick against West Ham in November 2017, but left Everton after just a year to move to America.

He signed a three-and-a-half-year deal at DC United, but served just 18 months of that before returning to England with Championship side Derby County in a player-coach role.

By that point, his hair was of a much better blend, though greys soon appeared in his beard. Blame ageing or management, with his playing retirement coming in January 2021 when he was appointed Derby manager.

The Rams' off-field struggles likely didn't help the greys. Though he took the club from bottom of the league to 18th, the Rams were relegated a season later following a 21-point deduction due to the club entering administration.

By the time he had taken charge of former side DC United back in the States, it was clear Rooney was gaining weight, with his grey beard now his dominating feature.

There's no shame in that happening – the need to stay fit as a player is no longer there, and Rooney was focusing on management, while wife Coleen hit the mainstream more than ever before due to her run-in with Rebecca Vardy – wife of Rooney's former England team-mate Jamie Vardy.

He began a career in punditry, working for the likes of Sky Sports and TNT Sports

His goal-scoring appearance in Soccer Aid last year highlighted how far his fitness levels had declined

The Rooneys' son, Kai, was by this point storming through the ranks at United. Kai's parents were pictured alongside him at the Nordoff and Robbins Legends of Football charity gala in October 2024, and Rooney really had seemed to have put on the pounds.

Kai, meanwhile, had scored 56 goals in one season at Under-12 level, and has now worked his way up to Under-18 level.

After being sacked by Birmingham City after less than three months in charge in January 2024, and then Plymouth Argyle after seven months in December, he would embark on punditry.

He worked with the likes of Sky Sports, TNT Sports and Prime Video as he tried to find his feet – his hair now as grey as his beard.

An appearance in the Soccer Aid match in June 2025 at the age of 39 highlighted how his fitness had declined since his retirement – though he still managed to score the fastest goal in the game's history.

And it wasn't too long after that he became a television regular. In fact, he started working with Prime Video in February 2025, and explained after Soccer Aid that he wanted to concentrate on his television work rather than management.

Now, though, as a regular pundit, Rooney looks a different man, having lost weight and undergone nose surgery

He stars in documentary series The Real Rooneys - which premiers this month - alongside Coleen and the rest of his family

Soon after, as of August that year, he had been announced as one of Match of the Day's pundits for the season, and is again this campaign.

His regular TV work may have coincided with his latest glow up.

Rooney was in attendance this week at the UK premiere for The Real Rooneys – a documentary series featuring the Rooney family behind the scenes.

Disney have the rights to the ten episodes, and fans are introduced to the usual off-camera life of Coleen and Wayne, as well as their four children.

Fans were left stunned by Rooney's appearance at the premiere. Clean shaven and obviously a lot lighter, the former England captain glowed post-nose surgery.

He then went on This Morning, asked whether he had been on weight loss jabs. 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing about me,' he said. 'It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'

Maybe it comes with being in front of the camera more often. Maybe it was a change he wanted to make.

At 40, he is just getting started with his television career. These are the many faces of Wayne Rooney so far – but there may still be plenty to come.

Sports.title: Ex-Man City chairman predicts 'drastic' sanctions as Premier League rivals plan response
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City chairman predicts 'drastic' sanctions as Premier League rivals plan response

An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 charges for breaching Premier League financial rules - with an appeal set to be launched

View 2 Images Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has had his say on the guilty verdict (Image: (Photo by Julian Finney - The FA/The FA via Getty Images))

Manchester City have been left facing a massive bill and backlash - and could be heading for an even bigger “disaster.”

‌



Rival clubs are plotting huge legal actions against the former champions after the guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules.

‌



They believe they could be due hundreds of millions in compensation if City are proven to have cost them Champions League football, commercial deals, bonuses and prize money.

‌



But City have also been warned by one of their biggest fans that dragging out a long appeal process would see the club’s already “tarnished” name damaged even further.

Former City chairman David Bernstein said: “To see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who’ve stayed with the club through thick and thin.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because…you’ve got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it’s just not viable.

“The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally.”

‌



There are fears that if City launch an appeal - which was described as “inevitable’ by one executive of another club - then that could drag on because a different panel would have to be set up to hear a review of the case.

That would cast a huge shadow over the Premier League while it goes on and if it is not resolved during the course of the season then it could see City be crowned champions despite having been found guilty which would be unthinkable.

View 2 Images Man City are facing huge sanctions if their appeal is unsuccessful (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Former FA chairman Bernstein, talking to Times Radio, believes any punishment must be way beyond a fine. He added: “I can’t give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

“All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that.”

City have not confirmed anything but issued a statement insisting the process is ongoing. But this latest development has left the whole football world in meltdown.

‌



The alleged offences - they are believed to have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges - came between 2009 and 2018 during which time they became the most dominant team in English football.

Premier League rivals are certain to look at their options. Burnley made a claim against Everton in June after the Merseyside club’s PSR breach in 2021. Burnley claimed it gave them a sporting advantage and were awarded £35.1m.

‌



Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham are believed to have taken out a legal notice and reserved their Section W of the competitions rules and some estimates suggest they could be in line for £200m each.

But it is highly likely that other clubs - despite being bound by time constraints under a statute of limitations and also effectively being part of a “private members’ club” within the Premier League rules - could also attack the process and push for compensation.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: “I think most football fans will be feeling this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very anxious about what happens next.

‌



“You’ll know this is a really long standing investigation, it dates all the way back to allegations that begin in 2009. There is still a way to go with the investigation, Manchester City is contesting the charges.

“The football fans need to know the rules are applied fairly and consistently, they need to know they’re upheld and they need to know the right decision has been reached.

“We do have a way to go with this, it’s very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.”

Sports.content:
Premier League sent demand over Man City 115 charges appeal as punishment verdict given

Manchester City are at the centre of a huge storm after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules 114 times, which they will appeal

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca's Man City could be handed a severe punishment (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein believes "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment for his old club. City have been found to have breached Premier League financial rules 114 times in a verdict which has sent shockwaves throughout football.

‌



The East Manchester side, who have always denied any wrongdoing, now face a nervous wait for their punishment. Potential repercussions include relegation, a points deduction, and the stripping of titles. It is understood that City will appeal the verdict.

‌



The independent panel found that City breached the regulations over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. The Blues were originally charged in 2023, and the 12-week hearing ran from September 16 to December 6 2024.

‌

Now, Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998 and 2003, has had his say on Times Radio. The 83-year-old wants to see City's case dealt with quickly.

He said: "I felt absolutely awful, I felt in shock yesterday, actually. I think you've asked me on the programme because of my time as chair of City and the FA, but basically I'm a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years.

"It's really awful that this great period of success, which followed many years of being less successful, when I was chair I think I helped get the club out of a very difficult period and started the road to better things.

"But to see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin. It's a pretty bad day I think for the fans in blue of Manchester."

The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial.

"I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty. All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

Sports.title: Stripping Man City of Premier League titles 'unlikely' as new charges punishment theory given
Sports.content:
Stripping Man City of Premier League titles 'unlikely' as new charges punishment theory given

Manchester City won four Premier League titles during the nine-year period in which they have been accused of breaching financial rules

View 2 Images Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 rule breaches (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images))

Manchester City have been found guilty of alleged financial rule breaches, but are unlikely to have Premier League titles stripped, it has been claimed. On Friday evening, it emerged through media reports that the club had breached 114 of the 115 financial rules they had been accused of by the Premier League.

‌



Multiple punishment theories have since been given with that ranging from a major fine to a significant points deduction that would essentially relegate them from the Premier League. City have won the title eight times in their history with half of those coming between 2009 and 2018, which is the period of the alleged rule breaches.

‌



Despite gaining a potential advantage over rivals in those title-winning campaigns, City are unlikely to be stripped of that silverware, according to The Times.

‌



Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges READ MORE :

Noel Gallagher responds to Man City guilty verdict with plea to Premier League bosses READ MORE :

Liverpool, and Manchester United finished runners-up to City twice while Arsenal could argue past success impacted the two seasons in which they came second to Pep Guardiola's side.

The latter left the club over the summer but made it clear he had been told by higher-ups that they were not guilty. City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 with an eight-week hearing taking place just over 18 months later.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



The outcome of that has now been discovered but the case is far from over with it understood that City will be launching an appeal against the ruling.

Everton and Nottingham Forest were docked points for just one breach which suggests that for allegedly breaking 114 financial rules, the punishment will be severe. City have denied the charges against them throughout the process and released a statement in the wake of the guilty verdict emerging.

Via a spokesperson, that read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the Club's statement of February 2023.

‌



"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

View 2 Images Man City have been cleared of at least one financial charge

City have have been cleared of at least one charge, with The Financial Times reporting it was among the most serious alleged violations levelled against the club.

‌



The club will be hopeful that their appeal yields some success, while other Premier League sides are watching the outcome closely before pursuing potential legal action, according to The Athletic. Their report suggests a class action against City remains a possibility should affected Premier League clubs unite in their efforts.

United, in particular, have been weighing up their own options for some time, examining the impact of City's alleged financial misconduct on their own achievements, according to a separate report from The Athletic.

What will unfold over the months ahead remains uncertain, with the extended international break leaving City without a fixture for a fortnight, and Enzo Maresca set to avoid the press for at least 10 days.

Article continues below

That opening encounter is against Liverpool at Anfield, with the long-standing rivalry between the two clubs during the period in which City's alleged rule violations occurred adding an extra edge to the fixture.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland player 'boycotts' Israel match as teammates call emergency meeting
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland player 'boycotts' Israel match as teammates call emergency meeting

Republic of Ireland are scheduled to face Israel in a Nations League match in Hungary on Sunday night, amid vocal opposition to the game taking place

View 2 Images Gavin Bazunu has informed Republic of Ireland bosses of his final decision

More Republic of Ireland players could boycott Sunday’s match with Israel after Gavin Bazunu confirmed he does not want to play in the fixture.

‌



The Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper, who is his country’s second choice, told bosses on Friday about his intention to not play, according to the Telegraph.

‌



His teammates are now considering their options and it's thought more could follow the same path throwing the UEFA Nations League match into major doubt. There have been increasingly vocal calls for Ireland to boycott the fixture, amid the backdrop of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

‌



A UN-commissioned inquiry previously found Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in war-torn Gaza. More than 73,000 people have been killed after Israeli military action was launched in response to the Hamas attack on the Nova Festival in southern Israel of October 7 2023, which killed approximately 1,200 people.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



An open letter from more than 160 Irish athletes urged the Irish Football Association (FAI) to withdraw from the fixture, with protests outside the team’s hotel in Dublin earlier this week.

It was expected that Ireland’s players would issue a statement at Saturday morning’s pre-match press conference. However, that was cancelled and rearranged minutes before the scheduled time, with no reason offered.

Last year, the FAI voted to submit a motion to UEFA that would have seen Israel banned from club and international competitions. The FAI cited two alleged violations of UEFA rules, including organising clubs in occupied Palestine without the permission of the Palestinian FA and the failure to enforce an effective anti-racism policy.

‌



Ireland captain Dara O’Shea made clear it was important that the opinions of all players were heard in the build-up. He said: “We’ve got to respect each other’s opinions and each other’s views and really sit down and take the time, because it deserves the time to talk about.

View 2 Images Heimir Hallgrimsson, Head Coach of Republic of Ireland (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

“It’s the main thing and it’s something that can’t be brushed over. Whatever decision that we go through as players is taken as one and everybody’s view is respected as well.”

‌



Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson elicited a response from the Israeli FA earlier this week when he said “we are not playing with genocide. We are playing against genocide. We are playing against Israel; we are not playing with Israel.”

In response the Israeli FA issued a statement which read: We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

“Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by the @IrelandFootball team coach. We’re not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we’re playing against the coach who embodies them.”

Article continues below

Israel are currently prohibited from playing games at home, due to security concerns, with this weekend’s match scheduled to take place in Hungary. The return fixture will also be played on neutral ground - in Serbia - amid the opposition to the game taking place.

Sports.title: Every word Mikel Arteta has said about Man City's 115 charges with Arsenal boss refusing to budge
Sports.content:
Every word Mikel Arteta has said about Man City's 115 charges with Arsenal boss refusing to budge

Manchester City have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 financial charges brought against them by the Premier League, with Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta having previously spoken on the matter

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta worked at Man City for several seasons (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has previously insisted that he witnessed no evidence of misconduct during his spell at Manchester City. The East Manchester side have been found guilty of all-but-one of the 115 charges levelled at the club by the Premier League.

‌



Arteta served as Pep Guardiola's assistant manager at City for three years between 2016 and 2019, before taking the reins at Arsenal in December of that year. The Premier League confirmed the charges against City in 2023, with the violations spanning 2009 to 2018.

‌



City now await confirmation of their sanction which could stretch from a points penalty through to expulsion from the Premier League. The club vehemently denies any wrongdoing and are likely to appeal.

‌



Rodri speaks out on Man City guilty verdict as press conference stopped after 'justice' claim READ MORE :

Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict READ MORE :

Arteta faced questions about the charges against City when the story first broke in 2023. The Arsenal manager, however, remained tight-lipped with his response.

"I'm not going to make any comment on that I'm sorry," Arteta said. The Spaniard was then pressed on whether he had any awareness of potential wrongdoing at City while serving as Guardiola's assistant, to which he promptly answered: "No."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Arteta was questioned 12 months later about the charges that had been filed against City, and delivered another guarded reply.

"That's something for the authorities to manage. It's not for us," the Arsenal boss said.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta spent three years at Manchester City as Pep Guardiola's assistant manager (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"If they're playing that means they can play and they are entitled to play. That's it."

Amid the news that City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League rules, the club released a statement asserting that the case is far from concluded.

Article continues below

A statement from City read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Sports.title: World's richest footballer and Chelsea flop worth 12 times Messi and Ronaldo now free agent
Sports.content:
World's richest footballer and Chelsea flop worth 12 times Messi and Ronaldo now free agent

The nomadic player, who had stints at various English clubs, finds his career at a crossroads

View 3 Images Faiq Bolkiah didn't make the grade at Chelsea (Image: Getty)

A footballer with a net worth that dwarfs the combined wealth of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo has been left without a club. The name Faiq Bolkiah won't be familiar to most fans, but the former Chelsea and Arsenal youngster has an incredible backstory.

‌



The 28-year-old is a nephew of the Sultan of Brunei and one of numerous heirs to a £200billion fortune. Individually, he boasts a reported net worth of £16bn. Incredibly, that's 12 times more than Messi (£680m) and Ronaldo (£640m) combined.

‌



Unlike those two greats of the game, Bolkiah now finds himself without a club following the expiry of his contract with Thai club Ratchaburi. It comes after a varied career, which started in English football.

‌



Born in Los Angeles, Bolkiah moved to the UK and grew up in Berkshire. After spells at Southampton, Reading and Arsenal, he moved to Chelsea, where he played alongside the likes of Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Tammy Abraham in the youth ranks.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

After leaving the Blues, Bolkiah had a trial at Stoke City before moving to Leicester City in 2016, around the time the Foxes won the Premier League. Bolkiah played in Leicester's U18 and U23 sides but failed to break through into the first team. After four years with the Foxes, he moved on to Maritimo in Portugal before switching to a club closer to his roots, playing for Thai side Chonburi and then Ratchaburi.

‌



Cristiano Ronaldo vows to carry on playing for Portugal and targets 1,000-goal landmark READ MORE :

However, following his departure from the latter, where he made just 23 appearances in three years, his career is now up in the air. Despite his extreme family wealth, Bolkiah has been described as down-to-earth and humble.

One of his team-mates at Chelsea, Ruben Sammut, once told The Athletic: "You would never ever have thought he was something like the 12th in line to the throne. You would not have thought of him as royalty.

"He was a humble guy, trying every day like every academy player. We used to joke he didn’t need to play football but he wanted to play because he loved football.

‌



View 3 Images Bolkiah finds himself a free agent (Image: Peter Van der Klooster/Getty Images)

"It wasn't a regular thing we mentioned. It was that typical banter, saying he is royalty, saying, 'What’s he doing playing with us?' But we all knew deep down how much he wanted to play, so it was more good-willed passing comments.

"We don't know the ins and outs of the wealth of his family but he took football seriously, so full credit to him. He lived in digs like everyone else. I can't remember who with.

‌



"He just came in with the boy he was in digs with. This would have been age around 16-18, youth team group. We lived in digs, walking distance to the training ground. He didn't do the schooling.

View 3 Images Bolkiah had a spell at Leicester before leaving England (Image: Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

"It was youth team full-time training and stayed with a host family. He was just humble, he never wore flash clothes or came in flash gear, he just wore a tracksuit. Just a down-to-earth guy.

Article continues below

"I think he did it so he didn't draw attention to himself. He knew if he was splashing the cash, it would create a bad image for himself."

Sports.title: Presidents Cup star blasted by team-mates as Wyndham Clark reveals what he did wrong
Sports.content:
Presidents Cup star blasted by team-mates as Wyndham Clark reveals what he did wrong

A Presidents Cup debutant has been singled out for a rookie mistake

View 2 Images Presidents Cup rookie Jackson Koivun has been singled out (Image: James Gilbert, PGA Tourvia Getty Images)

Jackson Koivun's Presidents Cup debut got off to a rocky start after turning up last for the team bus. Koivun was the standout captain's pick for Team USA's clash with the International team at Medinah.

‌



The 21-year-old is the PGA Tour's latest sensation after triumphing in just his third outing as a professional. Three-time SEC Individual champion Koivun enjoyed an outstanding college career before wasting little time in establishing himself in the pro ranks.

‌



Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker was convinced enough to use one of his six captain's picks on the breakthrough talent. While Koivun's ability and composure caught the eye of his peers, he committed a rookie blunder when the squad assembled at the beginning of the week.

‌



According to Wyndham Clark, Koivun was the last man to board the bus. Clark said: "Jackson, literally the first practice round we did, he was the last one to show up, and we gave him so much crap, 'Hey, you can't be showing up late as a rookie."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

That wasn't the only difficult initiation the youngster faced this week. He delivered a rendition of Kanye West's Heartless for his karaoke performance, a rite of passage for rookies.

‌



JJ Spaun makes comments about English culture as Rory McIlroy shocked by winner's omission READ MORE :

What is the Presidents Cup and how does it work? Tournament rules and prize money explained READ MORE :

But things did not go according to plan, if Collin Morikawa's verdict is anything to go by. He said: "Jackson, I'll give a three out of 10 [for his performance]. Not good, struggled. Got through it."

Yet those uncomfortable moments have only enriched the experience for Koivun, who has thoroughly enjoyed mixing it with the sport's elite. He said: "It's been so much fun. The week has kind of flown by. Really excited. The golf course is great, and getting to know everyone is really cool.

"I've just been nothing but excited this week. I've been waiting for Thursday to come. Definitely going to feel some nerves on the first tee, but we're all human. I think everyone does.

‌



"I told Justin [Thomas], once I get my first tee shot out of the way, I'm going to be good. Just kind of balancing adrenaline, nerves, everything like that to the best of my ability because I've put myself in situations like that.

View 2 Images Koivun with fourballs partner Justin Thomas on Thursday (Image: Luke Hales/Getty Images)

"I don't really know if anything is going to recreate what I'm going to feel on the first tee tomorrow, but just getting into that mindset that this is here and we've got to go play some good golf."

Article continues below

Koivun and his US team-mates have work to do if they are to retain the competition they have traditionally dominated. The International team won all five matches on Friday to take a commanding lead.

Having trailed 3-2 to the US after Thursday's fourballs, the International side swept the board in the day-two foursomes to open up a 7-3 advantage.

It raised hopes of a first victory in the event since 1998 and only a second since the competition began in 1994. There will be four further foursomes matches and four more fourballs on Saturday, with 12 singles games taking place on Sunday.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
