Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: Former world heavyweight champion boxer, 53, loses sad comeback against club fighter after 12 years retired
Sports.content:
Former world heavyweight champion boxer, 53, loses sad comeback against club fighter after 12 years retired

Hasim Rahman shocked the boxing world when he knocked out Lennox Lewis to become heavyweight champion in 2001.

But 25 years later, he was fighting in front of just a handful of people in Lowell, Indiana and losing a split decision to a club fighter on Thursday night.

Rahman made a sad return to the ring 12 years after his last fight at VFW Post 6841, fighting against 4-4 opponent Phillip Triantafillo for the Indiana State heavyweight belt.

And he lost a six-round unanimous decision, with two judges' scorecards scoring the bout 59-55 and the other 58-56. The loss drops his record to 50-10-2 in a fight that was a far cry from his glory days as the king of boxing's biggest division.

Rahman has been threatening a comeback for years, finally announcing in May he would return to the ring and claiming he had ambitions of becoming boxing's oldest heavyweight champion.

That record is held by George Foreman, who regained the heavyweight championship at 45, eight years younger than Rahman.

Hasim Rahman lost a unanimous decision as he made a sad comeback to boxing at the age of 53

Rahman was once the IBC and WBC heavyweight boxing champion back in 2001

His low-key loss against Triantafillo drew criticism from those within the boxing community.

Legendary promoter Lou DiBella wrote on X: 'In the early hours of this morning, in Lowell, Indiana, 53 yr. old former heavyweight champion Hasim Rahman lost a six round sanctioned #boxing match to a 3-4 guy... a SANCTIONED fight.

'Every day, in many ways, across borders, from billionaire and corporate supported events to unsafe silliness in tiny venues, boxing is showing you what it is in 2026. You can have it!'.

Boxing writer Dan Rafael wrote: 'Just watched some sad s***: Utterly washed former heavyweight champion Hasim Rahman, age 53, ending a 13-year retirement & losing a slow motion 6-rounder to 40-year-old novice Phillip Triantafillo (now 5-4) in what looked like a community center gym in front of maybe a dozen people. #Boxing is unforgiving.'

Baltimore, Maryland native Rahman last fought professionally in June 2014, losing a three-round decision in Auckland, New Zealand against Anthony Nansen.

Two years earlier, he had been knocked out in the second round by Alexander Povetkin in a fight that marked the end of his career at the top level.

Rahman produced one of the sport's great upsets when he beat Lewis in April 2001 in South Africa, knocking him out in the fifth round before losing a rematch later that year.

He went on to fight the likes of Evander Holyfield, James Toney and Wladimir Klitchsko in his long career which has now featured another chapter long past his 50th birthday.

Rahman was beaten by his 4-4 opponent in a six-round contest in front of barely any people

Rahman shocked the boxing world when he knocked out Lennox Lewis in South Africa in 2001

Another former world heavyweight champion, Mike Tyson, made headlines for his return to the ring in 2024 aged 58 against Jake Paul.

He recently insisted he would 'never' return again, saying: 'That’s why I did the last fight. So I never have to do it again.'

Tyson earned a reported $20 million payday for that return to the ring, which ended with a sad unanimous decision loss, but he later wrote: 'This is one of those situations when you lost but still won.

'I’m grateful for last night. No regrets to get in ring one last time. I almost died in June. Had 8 blood transfusions. Lost half my blood and 25lbs in hospital and had to fight to get healthy to fight so I won.

'To have my children see me stand toe to toe and finish 8 rounds with a talented fighter half my age in front of a packed Dallas Cowboy stadium is an experience that no man has the right to ask for. Thank you.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua £150m fight is finally CONFIRMED - in Cardiff at 2am on a Friday night in December - and Netflix reveal price it will cost to watch
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua's long-awaited fight with Tyson Fury has finally been confirmed for December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium – and it will save Joshua around £7.5million in tax. It is understood each man will pocket around £75m for arguably the biggest bout to be staged on British soil after Joshua’s team, led by Eddie Hearn, succeeded in forcing the promotion’s Saudi backers to scrap plans to stage the showdown in New York. Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff. The ring walk is expected to take place around 2am to suit a US-based audience, in line with the demands of Netflix, which will broadcast the heavyweight showdown. Although the delivery of the fight in Wales will be positioned as a victory for British fight fans, pragmatism around tax was also a key consideration in Hearn’s argument against Madison Square Garden in New York. As Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this month, the two fighters would have been taxed around 30 per cent of their purses in America, compared to 20 per cent in the UK, with Joshua particularly unhappy about the prospect of an extra £7.5m being added to his bill. The two-time world champion instead demanded that his contract be honoured, which stipulated a British-based fight. Boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh said: 'Back in April, I said that any announcement would come from me. I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. 'The time for talking is over. Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua. Years in the making. One night to settle it. December 11th. LIVE on Netflix.' Netflix today confirmed the fight would be available 'at no additional cost' to subscribers. Their general membership pricing starts at £7.99 a month in the UK. Bookmaker Betfair make Fury the early favourite to win, pricing him at 8/15. Joshua is priced at 13/8. Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua has been announced for Friday, December 11 The roots of Joshua-Fury stretch back more than a decade, to when both men were emerging as Britain's leading heavyweight prospects Joshua tweeted: 'I am inspiring a generation', alongside an emoji of the British flag. His promoter Eddie Hearn, who fought relentlessly to keep the fight in the UK, wrote: 'WE DID IT. Forever indebted to the U.K. public for their support of Anthony Joshua. We couldn’t have got this over the line without you.' Fury's name appearing first on the card for the Battle of Britain will be an early win for the Gypsy King in his constant PR war with Joshua. The pair had originally been pencilled in to fight on November 20 at Madison Square Garden in New York, but a determined push from Joshua and Hearn saw the contracts re-negotiated to bring the fight back to British soil. Hearn had been adamant that British fans deserved the opportunity to watch two of the country's biggest sporting stars go head-to-head at home, and fought hard to make that happen. Fury, too, wanted the fight in the UK, but had been prepared to accept a move to America because of his concerns that the bout could once again slip away. Now those fears, after ten years of frustration, have been put to bed. The fight will take place in Cardiff, with the later-than-usual start time expected to mean ring walks at around 2am UK time as organisers attempt to satisfy the American audience watching on Netflix. Wembley had been the preferred venue for the showdown, but the major stumbling block was securing the necessary late-night permit. With Netflix and Turki Alalshikh keen for the event to cater to viewers in the United States, organisers required a start time significantly later than would normally be permitted at Wembley. Cardiff, however, was able to secure the required permit - clearing the final obstacle to bringing the fight back to Britain. Cardiff's Principality Stadium has come out on top to host the fight after weeks of negotiations

Your browser does not support iframes.

The scale of the occasion is already being felt in the Welsh capital, with hotels in Cardiff now understood to be sold out as supporters scramble to secure accommodation for one of the biggest fights in British boxing. For Joshua, the move represents the culmination of a push to ensure the fight was staged in the UK. The former two-times world champion and Hearn had been clear that, after years of watching British heavyweight stars travel overseas for major fights, Joshua-Fury belonged in front of their home crowd. Fury was willing to compromise on the location if necessary, however, with his priority being to finally get the fight over the line. The roots of Joshua-Fury stretch back more than a decade, to when both men were emerging as Britain's leading heavyweight prospects. Joshua won Olympic gold at London 2012 before turning professional, while Fury had already made his professional debut in 2008 and was building an unbeaten record of his own. For years, the prospect of the two eventually sharing a ring became one of British boxing's great hypothetical match-ups. Fury's stunning victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 elevated him to the summit of the heavyweight division, while Joshua was rapidly closing in on world-title status himself. FURY VS JOSHUA - BIG FIGHT ODDS Fury to win - 8/15 Draw - 16/1 Joshua to win- 13/8 Victory method: Tyson Fury by Points or Decision - 16/5 Fury by TKO/KO/DQ - 13/10 Anthony Joshua by Dec/Tech Dec - 15/2 Joshua TKO/KO/DQ - 13/5 Fight to go the distance: Yes - 13/8 No - 4/9 Odds courtesy of Betfair Joshua claimed the IBF heavyweight title by stopping Charles Martin in 2016 before adding the WBA and IBO belts to his collection. By 2017, Joshua-Fury had evolved from a fantasy fight into a genuine target. But the negotiations repeatedly broke down. The closest it came to fruition was in 2021, when the two camps appeared to be on the brink of agreeing a two-fight deal. The proposed showdown was publicly discussed and appeared to be edging towards reality, only for Fury to become contractually obligated to face Deontay Wilder after an arbitration ruling. That fight ultimately took place, with Fury beating Wilder for a third time, while Joshua embarked on his own defining chapter against Oleksandr Usyk. Joshua lost his WBA, IBF and WBO titles to Usyk in 2021 before suffering a second defeat to the Ukrainian in their 2022 rematch. Once again, Joshua-Fury seemed to drift further away. Then came another tantalising opportunity. Negotiations accelerated in late 2022, with both camps discussing a potential December showdown, but the fight again failed to materialise. Fury moved on to other opponents while Joshua began rebuilding his career following the two defeats by Usyk. The emergence of Alalshikh and the rapid expansion of Saudi Arabia's influence over boxing created a fresh route to making the fight. And this time, the years of disappointment are finally over. The contracts have been signed. Joshua-Fury is no longer a fight being negotiated, teased or promised. It will take place in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua's torture training! Boxer uses ancient Cossack warriors' stretching machine to prepare himself to fight Tyson Fury in a painful-looking workout routine
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has been summoning the strength of an ancient warrior as he prepares for his long-awaited bout with Tyson Fury on a stretching machine.

Boxing's biggest battle of the year is expected to take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in early December, after a venue war that saw it move from Madison Square Garden in New York.

Despite the superfight being shrouded in uncertainty for much of the year, both Joshua and Fury have been knuckling down in the gym in preparation for their showdown.

Away from the usual training drills associated with boxing, it appears that Joshua is trying something new in order to get the best out of himself when he faces the Gypsy King.

The two-time heavyweight world champion has posted a video to Instagram of him using a Pravilo machine, a stretching machine used by warriors in medieval times.

The machine is a training and conditioning device that originates from Slavic and Russian traditions. It is best-known for being used by historical Cossack warriors for over 1,000 years.

Anthony Josshua has posted a video of him using the ancient warrior Pravilo machine

And if the video posted by Joshua is anything to go by, it can be somewhat of a torturous bit of equipment, based on how it stretches out each limb of the human body.

The 36-year-old can be seen being pulled into a starfish position by the modern version of the machine, which he keeps in his new training gym in Dubai.

Earlier this year, Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic due to the conflict in the Middle East.

The post on Instagram – which is captioned 'When the instructor says, relax and breathe' – also shows the 251.0lb (113.9kg) frame of Joshua being easily rotated 180 degrees, displaying the strength of his core.

Joshua will be returning to the Welsh capital where he has won twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in 2017 and 2018 respectively.

Wembley had looked an ideal venue for the fight, but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in December

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

The streaming giant Netflix has yet to sign off on Cardiff, but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last week reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr fires brutal dig at fierce rival Conor Benn after Brit's devastating second round defeat by Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr fires brutal dig at fierce rival Conor Benn after Brit's devastating second round defeat by Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas

Chris Eubank Jr brutally mocked his fierce rival Conor Benn after the Brit suffered a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn, 29, was crushed via a second-round stoppage in Las Vegas as they fought for Garcia's WBC welterweight crown.

Benn was dropped by a right hook in round two, and although he managed to beat the count, he struggled to fend off Garcia's subsequent attack, leading to referee Thomas Taylor bringing the fight to a stop, shattering the Brit's world title dream.

It was Benn's first fight at welterweight for four years after he had taken on Eubank Jr at middleweight, meaning he had to cut weight ahead of the fight, something his great rival had to do for their bitter showdowns.

And, Eubank Jr seemed to enjoy his foe's struggles having gone through something similar.

Taking to X shortly after the fight concluded, he posted: 'Welcome to the "fighting after cutting too much weight" club… Enjoy.'

Chris Eubank Jr aimed a brutal dig at Conor Benn after his defeat to Ryan Garcia on Saturday

Benn suffered a heavy defeat by Garcia and his long-time rival Eubank Jr seemed to enjoy it

Eubank Jr had previously posted a photo with Garcia ahead of the fight with the caption: 'Get the job done kid.'

For his two fights against Benn last year, Eubank Jr had to cut down to 160lbs.

He missed that weight for the first bout, before he came under the limit for the second.

Meanwhile, Garcia's triumph over Benn, who was taken to hospital as a precaution, was the Mexican-American's first defence of his WBC crown.

Speaking afterwards, he insisted he hadn't been at full fitness, but outlined his ambitions going forward.

'I have always had the right hand,' he said. 'But I carried a lot of injuries, so I couldn’t really show it.

'I know people question my Mexican heritage because I don’t speak Spanish. But I always feel my people with me and I do it for them. Teofimo Lopez can get it next.

'I want to clean the division out. I want Devin Haney’s a** again, too.'

Sports.title: Why Conor Benn's 85-second humiliation against Ryan Garcia was the inevitable consequence of his fast-tracked career - and how the Brit became a sacrificial pawn in boxing's power struggle, writes JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
Why Conor Benn's 85-second humiliation against Ryan Garcia was the inevitable consequence of his fast-tracked career - and how the Brit became a sacrificial pawn in boxing's power struggle, writes JEFF POWELL

The Wizard Of Oz is now a spectacular fantasy production encompassing the inside of the giant globe called The Sphere which looms large over the Las Vegas Strip.

Where the yellow brick road leads for Conor Benn after his one round, one minute and 25 seconds destruction by the fastest gun in Sin City is a question to which nobody had the answer as he was being ferried to hospital for precautionary checks. And may not have for some time to come.

There is no clear pathway back to the heights to which he was thrust all too prematurely and without justification this Saturday night.

Benn had no place being in the same ring as world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia, who is emerging as the golden goose saviour of American and Mexican boxing. Nor had he done anything like enough in his patchwork career thus far to qualify for the honour of topping the bill at an arena as grand as the T-Mobile in as hallowed a home of boxing as Las Vegas.

This was a match made far away from fight heaven, deep in the casino vaults. Benn Jr leaves here millions of dollars the richer but with not so much as a scintilla of evidence that he will ever be able to mix it with the royalty of the ring, in which King Ry sits upon the throne. He has the payoff but not the legacy he craved.

For the second time in as many months English sport comes home from America with its tail between its legs. Only this clinical beat-down of an inferior boxer was aeons more humiliating than the retreat of our footballers from the World Cup. His defeat more comprehensive than that by Argentina.

Conor Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

Benn's humiliating defeat came after he thrust all too prematurely and without justification into the title fight

Benn had no place in being in the same ring as world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia

Little did Benn know, in his delusion of self grandeur, that in return for securing his family’s financial future he was used as a sacrificial pawn in the power struggle for control of big-time boxing between the houses of Queensberry and Matchroom against the arrival of UFC promoter Dana White on their doorstep.

Garcia, younger of the two by a year but a decade wiser, knew. He tried to cushion Benn’s fall from grace by calling him a ‘good dude who I hope can come back from this.’

But as a man who likes to tell it as it is he felt compelled to add: ‘ I knew exactly how the fight would go. Rushing in against me from the start is not a good idea. Not the way to go. You need patience in this game.’

When it was pointed out to him that Benn has not stopped an opponent for more than four years he added: ‘I must be honest. I did not feel any power in his punches.’

Not that there were many of them. Benn’s charge from the first bell was suicidal against the best, fastest and hardest counter puncher in the world. He ran headlong into a hail of Garcia’s trademark left hooks. To note that he lost the first round is as understated as saying that Goliath had a bad day at the office against David. And when in the second Garcia brought into play the right hand which is now almost as deadly as the left Benn was gone in 85 seconds.

Gone crawling on the canvas and still so unsteady when reeled to his feet that the referee let him continue only so far as the next battering.

Garcia observed: ‘It could have been stopped after the first knock down. I looked into his eyes down there and they were glazed over. He was already gone.’

He echoed the pre-fight fears of many of us that Benn could be in critical jeopardy if this went on too long, saying: ‘It would not have been good for Conor if this lasted any further.’

Benn appears to have been a sacrificial pawn in the power struggle for control of big-time boxing between Queensberry and Matchroom against the arrival of UFC promoter Dana White

Has he lived to fight another day? Dana White sounded less than totally convinced: ‘I’ve told Conor to go on holiday with his family and call me when he’s ready to come back. Then we can try to find the right fight for him.’

That would not be at welter after his ‘hellish’ struggle to cut his poundage. But if he can be hammered into oblivion by a 147-pounder what will become of him if he goes back up two divisions to middleweight?

No such doubts hang over Garcia. Having been saluted to the reverberating rafters of the T-Mobile by his half-brother Mexicans in the delirium of their Independence weekend celebrations, this Californian will resume his American love affair in more world title fights against the likes of Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez.

He, not Conor Benn in his wildest dreams, is the face and the future of boxing over here.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia destroys Conor Benn with brutal second-round TKO to retain WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas showdown
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia sealed a stunning second-round TKO win over Conor Benn in Las Vegas on Saturday night, retaining his WBC welterweight title in the process.

Benn ran blindly to the slaughter - in a fight which was always a lunge too far - and was left groveling on hands and knees at the feet of the new face of American and Mexican boxing.

Garcia took just four minutes and 25 seconds to devastate and humiliate the upstart son of Nigel the great.

Benn’s predictable sally forth from the first bell was as pointless, desperate and doomed to disaster as The Charge of the Light Brigade.

He was stopped in his tracks by the barrage of left hooks which have taken Garcia to the welterweight championship of the world, over which he will reign for as long as he likes.

The first round was but a prelude to the carnage to come in the 85 seconds which the first round lasted. A punishment doubled by the dynamite which also explodes from Garcia's right fist.

Ryan Garcia sealed a stunning second-round TKO win over Conor Benn in Las Vegas

Garcia took just four minutes and 25 seconds to devastate and humiliate the British star

The 28-year-old retained his WBC welterweight title after the devastating display in Sin City

Conor was reduced to crawling on the canvas by a two-fisted assault to which he had no answer. When he staggered drunkenly to his feet referee Thomas Taylor looked long and hard into his glazed eyes before letting him carry on.

The kill was mercifully swift. A combination of lefts and rights which the third man in the ring could no longer ignore.

This is a warning which his handlers must not forget. This was fight too much, too soon. As Garcia had warned he done nothing to deserve the tilt at the WBC belt his father had worn with such pride.

Nor his elevation the top of a bill in the T-Mobile arena nor in this Mecca of boxing Whether he will ever be ready to mix with the company of prize-ring loyalty is doubtful.

He was not only outclassed, out-sped an out-thought but was treated to punching of almighty power with which his dad could not gift him.

The last 24 hours before the first bell had been consumed by doom-casts about Benn’s drastic weight draining to reach the welter limit of 147 lbs.

Followed by extraordinary claims that he had put on more than two stones following Friday’s weigh-in which, if authentic, would have catapulted him into the ring three divisions even heavier than the super-middleweights.

The truth would out as his robe slipped off. But if he had gorged himself between stepping on the scales and the first bell that might done him much good. Such drastic shifts in poundage are as debilitating as dehydration.

If this was another of the mind games played by Benn and Garcia throughout the wind up and build up it seemed doubtful that any of that would have a material effect on the fight itself. Would anyone in this hardest of all games risk being beaten by indigestion.

Conor was reduced to crawling on the canvas by an assault to which he had no answer

The referee swiftly waved off the bout after a barrage of punches from the American star

The substantive issue was Garcia’s boxing class and knock out power versus Benn’s frenzy and punch resistance.

For the high-paying fans – Benn’s long-haulers from the old country and Garcia’s Gen Z armies of groups from his two nations of identification the US and Mexico – what mattered most was that both delivered the barn-burner of a fight they promised.

Quite beautifully those three congregations fell silent together in commemoration of one boxer who never gave in, never gave up, never delivered a disappointing fight, never offended anyone, never betrayed a friend.

The giant screens in the 02 went into black and white mode for a nostalgic picture of Ricky Hatton who died too young as the previous British fighter to top the bill in what was until recently the fight capital of the world. Over to you Master Benn.

Garcia came to the ring to the strains of a patriotic Mexican song, wrapped in that country’s flag and to rapturous acclaim from the baying Amex majority in the house.

Unabashed and as expected Benn went instantly on the offensive only to be met by barrage of Garcia’s trademark left hooks.

Less than three minutes later it was all over.

Sports.title: Conor Benn shows off remarkable weight transformation after piling on 32 pounds in just HOURS, having been 'dragged to the pits of hell' during excruciating weight cut ahead of mega-fight with Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn shows off remarkable weight transformation after piling on 32 pounds in just HOURS, having been 'dragged to the pits of hell' during excruciating weight cut ahead of mega-fight with Ryan Garcia

Conor Benn has shown off a dramatic 32lb weight gain just hours after coming in one pound under the 147lb welterweight limit ahead of his bout with USA's Ryan Garcia.

The 29-year-old Briton came in at 146lb (66kg) at Friday's weigh-in for Saturday's fight, half a pound heavier than champion Garcia.

Just 12 hours later, Benn revealed on social media that he had added 32lb, taking him to 12st 10lb (80.73kg).

Speaking at a ceremonial event in front of fans later on Friday, Benn already appeared noticeably bigger, with his face and shoulders having filled out.

'Did it look hard? How did I look?' he asked. 'We'll see tomorrow night how good I really feel.'

Benn had previously said he could weigh as much as 12st 7lb (80kg) by the time he stepped into the ring on Saturday evening (around 4am Sunday, UK time).

‼️ Conor Benn has rehydrated to 178.4 pounds already.



📈 He is up 32.4 pounds (including clothes etc) in just 10 hours! 😱 pic.twitter.com/m6netuS2c1 — EverythingBoxing | Darshan Desai (@EverythingBoxi2) September 12, 2026

Benn revealed on social media that he had added an incredible 32lb hours after the weigh-in

The 29-year-old Briton had come in at 146lb (66kg) at Friday's weigh-in for Saturday's fight, half a pound heavier than champion Garcia before quickly adding it back on

Speaking at a ceremonial event in front of fans later on Friday (above), Benn already appeared noticeably bigger, with his face and shoulders having filled out

He has not fought at welterweight for more than four years, having moved up through the divisions before competing at middleweight during his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Now, for the biggest fight of his career, taking on Garcia for the World Boxing Council (WBC) title under the bright lights in Las Vegas, he has had to come all the way back down.

'It feels like I've been dragged down to the pits of hell, had a fight with Satan and God brought me back to life,' he told BBC Sport earlier this week.

'Making weight has been the hardest thing I've done. I haven't made weight for four and a half years so it's going to be hard.'

Whether the weight cut affects Benn's strength and power on Saturday night will be one of the central questions of his WBC world title fight.

Garcia has suggested Benn's move back down could leave him vulnerable, but Benn was dismissive of that concern when he spoke to Daily Mail Sport earlier in the week.

'You think I've been up at middleweight, mixed it with someone who's competed at super middleweight? You think I'm worried about what a lightweight can do to me?' he told this publication.

'You think I'm concerned in the slightest about this guy? I'm not concerned about one little thing he brings to the table… that silly left hook of his is useless. He can bring whatever he wants. It don't concern me.'

USA's Garcia claimed the WBC title with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making the first defence of his belt against Benn on Saturday

Benn's unusual route to this fight has been shaped by his rivalry with Eubank.

Their first meeting at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April 2025 was the culmination of years of animosity between the two families, with Benn and Eubank Jr inheriting a rivalry that began with their fathers in 1990.

The fight itself was fought at a catchweight above 160lb, with Benn stepping up significantly from his previous division. Eubank won a close decision, leaving Benn to reflect on a performance in which he felt the occasion and the emotion had affected him.

Seven months later, the pair met again at the same venue. This time Benn won the decision, dropping Eubank twice in the final round in a dramatic conclusion to their second fight. It left them level at one victory apiece and appeared to finally close the door on one of British boxing's most talked-about rivalries.

Benn insisted the atmosphere this week is nothing like those two nights when asked whether his hatred for Garcia compared.

'This is nothing like the Eubank fight,' he said. 'The Eubank fight, there was nothing pleasant or friendly or fake about the Eubank fight. There was a lot more raw emotion in that fight and I let that get the better of me the first time. That won't happen here.'

Garcia has won 25 of his 28 professional fights, including 20 by knockout, with two defeats and one no-contest. He claimed the WBC title with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making the first defence of his belt against Benn. Benn has 25 wins, 14 by knockout, and one defeat.

Benn said of his rival: 'He just carries on like a spoiled brat, like a big child who throws his toys out of the pram. I'm not worried about him in the slightest. If anything, I'm gonna have a bit of fun with him. He's a little bit sensitive, highly emotional, and a little bit insecure.'

There is also an uncomfortable shared history between the two men when it comes to drugs testing.

Benn's original 2022 fight with Eubank was cancelled after he returned two adverse findings for clomifene, something he has consistently denied intentionally taking. Garcia subsequently returned an adverse finding for ostarine following his 2024 victory over Devin Haney, which he also denied intentionally taking.

Both men were asked at the fight's press conference whether they had concerns that the other could use performance-enhancing drugs ahead of Saturday's contest.

Neither appeared keen to make it a central issue, with the focus instead returning to the fight itself.

Benn defeated Chris Eubank Jr by unanimous decision to take revenge in their rematch at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last November

Garcia has also questioned whether Benn's career has prepared him for this level of opposition, arguing that the Briton is taking a step too far by challenging for the world title.

Benn's response was typically blunt. 'How is this too far? He quit against Tank Davis. He got outclassed by Rolly (Romero), and then got a world title shot with Barrios,' he said.

'Then there is me. Stepping up to fight the contenders up at middleweight, fight of the year up at middleweight, avenging my loss. Two big stadium shows. Just come off beating a two-time former world champion and having to make 147, which again I ain't made in four years in six weeks.

'What's he talking about? Ultimately, who cares what he thinks? I don't listen to quitters anyway.'

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia was banned for racial slurs, hit with a $1m doping fine and U-turned on his support for Donald Trump... but America's controversial rock-and-roll boxer is out to save his sport by beating Britain's Conor Benn
Sports.content:
A dazzling talent just reaching his prime will enter the T-Mobile Arena here this Saturday night with the hopes of a fighting nation resting on his shoulders. Conor Benn, not so much. British boxing is enjoying a boom, not least with its dominance in the marquee heavyweight division. The young man the son of Nigel is challenging for the world welterweight crown carries the burden of restoring America to its historic pre-eminence in the prize-ring. Not just by adding to an unusually low head count of their champions but by resuscitating the excitement, the stardust, the impudence, the controversy, the brilliance and the fascination of the public over here with the hardest game of all. Ryan Garcia is the only poster boy left to them following the retirement of Floyd Mayweather. Vitally, he has all it takes to bring a new generation of fans clamouring to his fights. At 28 he has the matinee idol looks of a young Elvis Presley which brings the girls squealing into the crowds. A rock and roll bad-boy reputation which chimes with the lads. Showmanship within the ring and charisma outside the ropes. Ryan Garcia will take on Conor Benn on Saturday night with the American carrying the hopes of a fighting nation on his shoulders Garcia has reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde (left), the beautiful mother of two of his three children (above) Benn has arrived in Las Vegas with the aim of taking the WBC welterweight belt from Garcia Glamorous blondes vie for his favours. Even though he is resisting those temptations now he has scrapped divorce proceedings and reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde, the beautiful mother of two of his three children. And, boy, can he box. The speed of hand and foot. The knock-out punching power. The taunting evasion. And, yes, the conceit which on occasion gets him into trouble. The two defeats scarring his 28-fight record – against two of America’s other world champions Gervonta Davis and Rolly Romero – came when he was at his most arrogant and complacent. The no-decision verdict which negated his stand-out victory over Devin Haney was imposed for failing a post-fight drug test for performance-enhancing Ostarine. Like Benn he protested his innocence: ‘I’ve never knowingly taken drugs.’ His relatives revealed he had been struggling with his mental health and against alcohol. But unlike Conor he preferred taking his punishment – a $1million fine and a 12-month ban – rather than financing a protracted court case which would also have kept him under lengthy suspension. Not that King Ry - he wears a gold crown for his ring entrances - is prone to compromising his regally unvarnished opinions. Garcia was a vociferous backer of Donald Trump in his first presidential election campaign. But given his Mexican roots he criticised Trump’s second-term deportation policy. Finally he renounced his support, denouncing the Trump administration’s handling of the Epstein Files. A devout Christian, he called rapper Eminem a satanist and posted on Twitter: ’I don’t support the LGBTQ+. F*** you guys. Rot in hell.’ He called for a boycott of the Olympics for ‘disrespecting Jesus Christ' with the section of the opening ceremony of France 2024 in which drag queens imitating Greek gods were widely supposed to be parodying the Last Supper. Garcia scrapped divorce proceedings with influencer Andrea in August 2025 Garcia turned down WBC offers to help with his mental health difficulties but progress has been deemed to be made, leading to him fighting and beating Mario Barris in February The rock-and-roller came out in him when he was arrested for causing $150,000- worth of damage while trashing a room and a corridor at the ritzy Waldorf Astoria hotel in Beverly Hills. That risked a short prison term, which has not been applied. Another suspension was imposed. This one from competing in fights sanctioned by the WBC for racist slurs live on the internet against the black community and muslims. President Mauricio Sulaiman reported that Garcia had turned down a number of offers from the WBC to help Garcia with his mental health difficulties. Sulaiman relented last November, saying he recognised the progress made in that regard by the fighter’s large family. Promptly, this February, Garcia defeated the highly rated Mario Barrios to claim the WBC welterweight belt, inflicting a first round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision. The braggadocio bubbles to the surface before fights. As soon as this weekend’s bout was announced he told Benn to his face: ‘You box like amateur trash. You're just a flashy trash can. I’m going to throw you out with trash.’ All the ingredients are there for the making of a turbulent, troubled super-star son of this angry and violent 21st century. All wrapped up in the rare skills and brave heart of a potentially great fighter. Some indication of whether all that will be enough for him to kindle another golden age in US boxing may be seen in how he deals with Benn. The huge scale of that task is evident in this, my overwhelmingly American list of the 20 greatest boxers of all time, with Lennox Lewis the Brit who came closest to inclusion...

Sports.title: Norris demands ban for Colapinto after Azerbaijan GP crash
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris thinks Franco Colapinto deserves "at least a one-race ban" for causing a pile-up at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

On a lap 36 restart in the streets of Baku, Colapinto locked up his cold front tyres and aimlessly speared into Alpine team-mate Gasly into Turn 1, with Norris also collected by the tangling pair.

The incident knocked both Gasly and Norris out of the race, as well as Colapinto himself, capping off a frustrating afternoon for the McLaren driver who lacked pace and made a Turn 1 mistake of his own that dropped him into the pack on the restart.

The restart clash left Norris furious, feeling Colapinto's careless driving should be punished harshly by F1's race stewards.

"I've not seen it. I just got taken out. I think the FIA should be stricter and start handing out bans for this kind of stuff," Norris vented. "It's careless from people. It costs a lot of money; all my parts are in the bin now. People should just get banned, because that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1."

When asked if there were mitigating circumstances for what happened on the slippery Baku circuit, Norris added: "In Formula 1, I think you expect drivers to anticipate things. Grip is going to be low; tyre temps are low; they weren't even that low. In Formula 1, we want to be against the best drivers in the world, and when stuff like this happens, it's because [they] shouldn't be there.

"I've not seen it, but if you cause a crash in a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban."

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

Colapinto, who also drew the ire of team-mate Gasly as the pair was on for points, was apologetic afterwards.

"A big mistake," the Argentinian acknowledged. "I locked up completely with cold tyres and cold brakes and was out of control completely. Not a lot to say more than sorry to the team, to Pierre of course, to all the factory.

"We've been working really hard to score points and I threw it away with that big mistake. So, I'm very sad for the team. Of course it's a big disappointment. I'm sorry to Lando as well."

Sports.title: F1 Azerbaijan GP: Russell fends off Verstappen for victory; Colapinto takes out Gasly and Norris
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell has taken a dominant pole-to-flag victory at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, overcoming two safety cars to beat Max Verstappen and clinch his third grand prix win of 2026.

Russell took pole by a massive eight tenths on Friday and confirmed Mercedes' dominance in race trim. The Briton led either side of a pair of mid-race safety cars to snare his first win since June's Austrian Grand Prix, while team-mate Kimi Antonelli could only manage fifth.

At the start Russell made a good getaway to defend his lead on the short burst towards Turn 1, with Piastri picking off second-starting Charles Leclerc.

Russell started on medium tyres with his nearest rivals on softs, but tyre degradation wasn't much of a factor on the low-impact street circuit, reducing race strategy to a simple one-stopper at the most opportune moment.

The Briton quickly broke free of the pack while Piastri and team-mate Lando Norris, who had passed Isack Hadjar four fourth, immediately came under pressure from the two Red Bulls. Hadjar and Verstappen appeared stronger on the straights than the Mercedes-powered papaya cars, who also struggled for traction out of Turn 16, the corner leading onto Baku's massive 2km straight.

After Verstappen cleared Pierre Gasly and Lewis Hamilton, both he and Hadjar made their way past Norris and put pressure on second-placed Piastri, with Hadjar waving his team-mate by. But as Verstappen started to go through a graining phase on his medium tyres, his challenge on Piastri stalled, making soft-tyre runner Hadjar impatient about having a go at the McLaren driver instead.

Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren, Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

Mid-race safety car plunges race into chaos

Just as Hadjar was given the green light to start challenging Verstappen, the race was interrupted by a safety car on lap 30 of 51 for a crash by Alex Albon. While holding off Esteban Ocon for a distant 13th place, the Williams driver locked up his tyres into Turn 5 and pierced the TecPro barriers on exit, escaping without harm.

With every frontrunner yet to make their one and only pitstop, the stoppage led to a flurry of activity it the pits, with Russell retaining his lead from Piastri, Verstappen, Hadjar, Leclerc and Hamilton, while Norris dropped to ninth behind Gasly and Antonelli after going deep into Turn 1.

That error would go on to haunt Norris as all hell broke loose on the lap 36 restart. While Verstappen picked off Piastri for second, Franco Colapinto locked up his tyres and speared into Alpine team-mate Gasly, taking Norris out with them as Antonelli narrowly escaped the carnage. In the background there was more intra-team contact as Arvid Lindblad punted Liam Lawson into a spin, with the Turn 1 melee breeding another safety car.

The entire top 10 held station on a much more timid second restart on lap 39, with Russell leading from Verstappen, Piastri, Hadjar and Leclerc. But on the following tour there was more Baku drama for Piastri as he went deep into Turn 1 while defending against Hadjar, throwing away a potential podium.

Amid all the chaos, the double neutralisation turned what should have been a cruise for Russell into a nail-biting finish, defending against an aggressive four-time world champion in Verstappen.

But Russell held on in a drag race to the finish to hold off the Dutchman, with Hadjar joining the pair on the podium on his ironclad return from injury. Leclerc finished fourth ahead of Antonelli, who came back from 16th on the grid after a qualifying crash.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

As Antonelli predicted before the race, repeating his spectacular Monza comeback win was going to be tough on the streets of Baku. The championship leader had made his way up to eighth by the time the race was yellow-flagged, and then benefitted from the Turn 1 chaos and overtook Hamilton for fifth.

Lindblad crossed the line in seventh, beating Esteban Ocon at the line by 0.030s, with Haas team-mate Oliver Bearman in ninth, while Carlos Sainz sneaked into a points finish in a heavily upgraded Williams car.

Both Aston Martin cars again failed to make the finish after the team's latest horror weekend, while Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas ended the race in the wall on the final lap.

Courtesy of his third win of the campaign and first since Austria, Russell claws back 15 points to Antonelli in the championship, now trailing his team-mate by 66 points going into next weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix hosted by Malaysia.

Sports.title: Why Verstappen feels Baku was Red Bull's best chance to win in F1 2026
Sports.content:
A problem with the internal combustion engine cost Max Verstappen a good starting position for the Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The four-time world champion readily acknowledged that he probably could not have matched George Russell’s pole time, but given the large gap behind him, a place on the front row would have been a logical outcome.

However, due to a problem with Red Bull’s combustion engine, Verstappen was already losing half a second on the straights compared to team-mate Isack Hadjar, before a yellow flag caused by Lando Norris and battery problems were added to the equation.

It means Verstappen has to start from eighth on the grid, although polesitter Russell still described the Dutchman as the biggest threat to victory.

When Autosport put those words to Verstappen in the Baku paddock, a smile appeared on his face: "That’s good, if he thinks that way!

"But on a serious note, they are really quick. So I think they might be a bit too strong for us, although I’m going to give everything to fight for the podium, of course."

Despite Mercedes’ pace at the Baku City Circuit, Verstappen is crystal clear: in his view, this weekend represented Red Bull’s best chance to win a grand prix in 2026.

"They [Mercedes] are obviously getting an upgrade next week in Malaysia, so this was the chance to win. And we’ve certainly done a great job messing up that chance," Verstappen told the Dutch media in Baku.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Asked whether Baku would normally have been the only opportunity during the remaining race weekends, Verstappen continued: "Well, I’m sure Mercedes can do even more with that upgrade. They are already faster now, so it will become really difficult. Of course I never give up. I try again every weekend, but we have to be realistic."

With Red Bull already having its final major upgrade of the year available and Mercedes only set to follow in Malaysia, Verstappen believes a standout result in Baku would have been on the cards.

However, avoiding problems every weekend is also part of the job, and Verstappen therefore concluded after getting out of the car that Red Bull does not deserve it this way either.

"I felt good in the car and I was really on top of it all weekend," he said. "Look, maybe it wasn’t as quick as Mercedes, but that has been the case all season. But I was in a good place and of course it’s frustrating when you can’t show it."

However, Verstappen was able to put things into perspective. Yes, he would like to win a race in 2026 to avoid his first winless year since 2015, and yes, Baku represented an opportunity to do so, but all the setbacks hurt less because he is not in the title fight.

"I was extremely frustrated in the car. I can also stay very frustrated now, but there’s nothing I can do about it anyway", Verstappen realised.

"The whole weekend was going really well. And then when it matters, you have an engine problem. That really sucks. And if you want to fight at the front as a team, then those things can’t happen. But yeah, they do happen, and that also sums up our season a bit."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Peter Fox / Getty Images

With those final words, Verstappen is referring to the fact that he has already experienced plenty of setbacks this year. The Dutchman has previously said that something seems to go wrong at Red Bull every weekend and that he will have to spend the winter break like a Buddhist in Tibet to calm down.

However, Verstappen essentially sees the fact that his bad luck still causes irritation as a good sign – a sign that his passion for F1 is still there.

"I'm genuinely frustrated by it, and that means I still care a lot. Of course I could also say, who cares about this season, I’m not fighting for the championship anyway. But yeah, I still care a lot. I always try to get the maximum out of it, and when that isn’t possible, it’s still very frustrating."

Frustrating will also be the word if Verstappen drives onto the podium on Saturday, as he will be left with the feeling that even more had been possible.

"Yes, that depends on how the whole race unfolds and what our pace is like. But imagine we’re the fastest on track and you finish third or second… Yeah, then I’ll be frustrated because there would have been more in it."

Finally, the one piece of good news is that the upgrade package in Baku is doing what Verstappen had hoped it would.

"That was a decent step, yeah. But for next year, if you really want to compete, we need to make a much bigger step. And that applies to everything: the car, the power unit, everything.” When it is pointed out that Red Bull cannot do much to the power unit without an ADUO token, Verstappen concludes: "That’s true, but of course we can still fine-tune things."

Sports.title: What’s behind Norris’ top-speed issue in Baku – and why McLaren itself is down on Mercedes
Sports.content:
A technical problem caused a lack of top speed on Lando Norris’ McLaren Formula 1 car in Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying, with the reigning world champion down in fifth.

Despite having outqualified team-mate Oscar Piastri 9-1 in the 10 previous sessions, Norris found himself three tenths’ adrift in Q3 – his worst deficit of the season. A lock-up in Q3 didn’t help, but as it happens, the McLaren driver was hindered by an issue on his MCL40.

“There's more in my car for some reason than the other car,” Norris said of his top speed deficit, addressing the media right after the session. “So we have to understand why I'm basically having to push more than Oscar to try and make up for my straightline speed.”

The Briton’s top speed was 3.4km/h down on Piastri’s in qualifying, but McLaren already has clues as to where the problem originated.

“On Lando's side specifically, we observe a deficit of power that we are investigating,” team principal Andrea Stella explains. “It seems to be linked to some behaviour of the fuel injection, something that hopefully we, or the adaptive systems, should be able to improve for tomorrow.

“It looks that occasionally the power unit generates a bit less power, but this is a specific phenomenon, a specific issue. It has nothing to do with the overall behaviour of the power unit.”

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

This occurred in the wider context of McLaren suffering from a much more substantial lack of straightline speed relative to its own power unit provider, Mercedes. George Russell was 8.1km/h quicker than Piastri and 11.5km/h faster than Norris in Baku.

Asked if this was down to power unit exploitation or a draggy McLaren, Norris said: “It's both. They have a very efficient car, they always have done for years. We need to take a big step in that direction if we want to be competitive in any straightline-speed track for the rest of the season.”

Stella mostly concurred and insisted this was a mere case of McLaren needing to match Mercedes’ level across all areas.

“In a circuit like this, we have seen in every practice session and then in qualifying that we were losing time in the straight compared to Mercedes,” the Italian pondered.

“While we have the same power unit, there's a few differences, and I think it's fair to say that their package, chassis, ratios, power unit itself, it just seems to be more effective when it comes to generating top speed. We saw how strong they were in Monza, pretty much in every long straight in the championship they were able to generate more speed.

“It would be incorrect from an engineering point of view to say that there's a difference in power unit or they use the power unit a little bit better, because in fact we don't know and we are not assuming that there's any difference.

“It’s the package that is more effective for them, like they might have even less aerodynamic drag; we know that drag is an area that we need to keep working on. As a fact, we think it's an opportunity to do better.”

Sports.title: Verstappen reveals why Red Bull's engine problem in Baku was different than it seemed
Sports.content:
After setting the fastest time in final practice and feeling good about the upgrades, Verstappen hoped to pull off a surprise in Baku, but an engine problem threw a spanner in the works.

Initially, it appeared to be related to deployment issues and therefore problems on the electrical side of the power unit, but speaking to the (very small) group of Dutch media in the Baku paddock, Verstappen clarified what was actually going on.

"Throughout qualifying, already from Q1, I had a problem with the engine, which meant I was losing at least half a second compared to my team-mate. And it only got worse. In Q2 and Q3 it was a complete disaster, so I think we clearly have a problem with the engine."

When asked by Autosport, Verstappen clarified that the problem was initially not about deployment – as it perhaps seemed – but rather the internal combustion engine.

"No, not on the electrical side. In Q1, we immediately saw a problem. Of course, at that point you still think, ‘What could it be? Is the engine too cold or actually too hot?’ All of that is possible, because it is all very sensitive nowadays. But later it became clear that we really did have a problem with the ICE. It only got worse and in Q3 that engine was no longer working properly at all."

How the initial issue led to further setbacks

That problem with the combustion engine subsequently caused numerous other issues, leaving Verstappen going from one problem to another on Friday afternoon.

"The top speed just became less and less. On that second lap in Q3, my battery wasn’t charging either, but that was obviously because the combustion engine had a problem. That causes a lot of misfires and a lot of other problems, and it confuses the system completely."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

The latter was clearly visible in the onboard footage. Between Turns 15 and 16, Verstappen’s head suddenly jolted forward, whereas this would normally be a straightforward flat-out section.

"Yeah, because my battery switched off there", the Dutchman explained. "Because you’re so slow on the straights, you obviously use more battery coming out of the corners to try to compensate for that. As a result, you go into super clipping in some places, and that clip is quite aggressive.

"The whole system was just confused. You spend longer on a straight because you’re going slowly and as a result you use more battery. That’s the same as what happens with Honda, you also see them clipping a lot more than everyone else because they have to spend longer at full throttle on the straights."

Besides the engine problems themselves, this also disrupted the run plan. Verstappen had to abort his second flying lap – or what should have been a flying lap – which in turn had consequences for the remainder of the session.

"I had to abort that lap, but then you lose so much tyre temperature, which is actually very important around here. You could see everyone pushing all the time and continuing to weave", Verstappen said, pointing out that almost everyone in Q3 completed just one long run – unlike in a normal Q3 session.

Only McLaren opted for a visit to the pitlane, but Verstappen continued: "You can see that it wasn’t really a success for them either, so we just kept going.

"But if you have to abort a lap, then you don’t have the right tyre temperature for the very last lap. And the engine is basically breaking down, and then there was a yellow flag on my final lap as well”, he said, referring to the moment involving Lando Norris. “So I had to leave at least two tenths on the table in that corner."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

An engine change, but no grid penalty for Verstappen?

Red Bull is currently investigating the engine problem further, but Verstappen’s story makes it seem unlikely that he will start Saturday’s race with the same ICE. However, the four-time world champion immediately makes clear that such an engine change will not result in a grid penalty.

"Well, if there are still question marks, we have to replace the engine. But we still have another engine available in the pool."

A grid penalty will follow later in the year, however, the Red Bull driver confirmed when asked by this website. "Yeah, there definitely has to be a penalty at some point."

In theory, Baku appeared to be quite a good place to take one, as overtaking seems possible, but Verstappen puts that into perspective.

"The problem is that everyone completely drains the battery on the long straight. So you can’t really use the battery to overtake someone, because going from 100 to zero is the same for everyone."

It means Verstappen retains his eighth starting position and will still be aiming for the podium on Saturday, although he believes he could otherwise have started from the front row.

"It’s obviously a real shame, because it had been going well this week. Maybe I wouldn’t have matched George’s time, but there’s such a big gap between P1 and P2, we definitely would have been somewhere in between."

Sports.title: Hamilton frustrated after late Ferrari qualifying strategy change: ‘I towed Charles the whole time’
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has rued Ferrari’s qualifying strategy at Formula 1’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix, explaining it left him without a slipstream.

Hamilton’s performance worsened throughout qualifying on Friday in Baku, as he outpaced team-mate Charles Leclerc by exactly one tenth in Q1 before ending up 0.257s and 0.495s adrift in the following two segments respectively. As a consequence, he was sixth in Q3, with his team-mate up to the runner-up spot.

However, the seven-time world champion reckoned his lack of pace was down to two factors: not just his struggle to extract the most from his tyres, but also Ferrari’s strategy, as he found himself tow-less on his single, six-lap Q3 run.

“We've been struggling all weekend to get the tyres working,” Hamilton said. “Q1 was pretty OK. I felt like the car wasn't too bad in Q1.

“In Q2 we started struggling even more with the rear tyres. And I was behind at least some cars in those two sessions. After Q2 they decided to change the run plan and just do one run, which hadn’t foreseen the fact that I would come out with no one ahead of me, and just towing Charles the whole time. I was 25 seconds behind George [Russell], so…”

He added: “Charles did a really good job. Right at the end I gave him a really good tow all the way to the start line.”

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton did experience a tow in today’s FP3 session and believed it was worth “six tenths” – which would theoretically have vaulted him to the front row in Q3.

“It's literally just not having people up ahead,” he insisted as to his underwhelming result. “As I said, I was weaving to try and save my life, and I still couldn't get these stupid tyres working. It's such a pain in the arse. We've got to bring back some good tyres.”

Despite Leclerc’s encouraging result – and Hamilton’s apparent belief he could have been even quicker – the Briton doesn’t believe Ferrari has the second-fastest machinery. “Maybe the third-fastest car,” he added. “I think Max [Verstappen] has been quicker all weekend, and I don't know what happened to him in the session.

“It will be hard to overtake any of the cars.”

When his qualifying was described as a ‘perfect storm’ where ‘nothing went right’ - including a "gentle" hit with the wall in Q3 - a downbeat Hamilton responded: “It happens all the time, so I'm used to it.”

This was the first time in 2026 that the Ferrari racer qualified more than a second down on pole position, with a whopping 1.332s deficit to Mercedes’ George Russell – who was eight tenths faster than anyone.

Sports.title: Antonelli angry at "unnecessary" Azerbaijan GP qualifying crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he needs to "do a much better job" after an "unnecessary" qualifying crash in Baku left him 16th on the grid.

Antonelli made an unforced error in Q1 when he tagged the inside wall in Turn 1 left-hander to start his second flying lap, sustaining terminal suspension damage that forced him to park his Mercedes W17.

Antonelli's first lap had already qualified him for Q2, but with the Italian unable to take part, he is facing a comeback in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Saturday from 16th on the grid.

To add insult to injury, Mercedes proved the class of the field in Baku as team-mate George Russell demolished the competition to take pole by eight tenths, meaning Antonelli likely cost himself a front-row start.

"It was just a misjudgement with the grip changing so much," Antonelli explained. "An unnecessary one in Q1, and it's a very good reminder that like this, things don't go my way, so I need to do a much better job.

"I had a lot more headwind compared to the lap before, so the front just was much stronger, and I turned in roughly in the same spot, but obviously the car turned more and I clipped the wall."

Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

With Antonelli missing a large chunk of Thursday practice due to a hydraulic issue, the 20-year-old had already been on the back foot all weekend, so he acknowledged he "wasn't 100% there" and Russell would have been tough to beat.

"George has been doing an incredible job this weekend," Antonelli admitted. "He's been feeling very good with the car, so for sure he has made the difference. I have to be honest with that, but also the car has been very, very quick."

The last time Antonelli started from the rear of the grid, the Italian put in a drive for the ages with a spectacular comeback to win the Italian GP in Monza.

But while Baku's 6km street circuit also offers overtaking potential on its long straight, Antonelli cautioned a Monza repeat would be much more difficult to pull off.

"A good start, stay out of trouble, and then try to set a really good pace," Antonelli summed up his Saturday plans. "Obviously, it's going to be a bit harder than Monza because it's a bit harder to overtake here, but I believe we can still do a good race.

"I have nothing to lose, and I just need to do the best race I can. With experience, you learn how to move forward. Of course, this weekend has been a bit off with everything, but tomorrow I think we can do a good race."

Sports.title: F1 Azerbaijan GP: Russell dominates to pole after Antonelli crashes out in qualifying
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell has beaten Charles Leclerc to take a dominant pole at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, while team-mate and title favourite Kimi Antonelli is set for a comeback race from 16th after crashing in Q1.

At the 6km Baku City Circuit, Antonelli tagged the barriers on the inside of the Turn 1 left-hander during Q1 and was unable to limp back home in his Mercedes W17 with terminal front-left suspension damage. Antonelli had already set a time quick enough to advance to Q2, but was out of the session and is set to start 16th at best.

Team-mate Russell, who had already proven rapid all weekend, capitalised to take a dominant pole ahead of Leclerc and Oscar Piastri - the Briton's fifth pole of the campaign.

McLaren sprung an early surprise in Q3 when Piastri and Lando Norris jumped early pacesetter Russell to top the first barrage of qualifying runs. Off the back of a messy brace of practices, the papaya squad had yet to string together optimal qualifying laps, with Norris even suspecting something was wrong in his car in Q1.

But Piastri's 1m43.571s lap proved an achievable target for Russell to beat, with the Briton going half a second faster on his second run to set a rapid 1m43.037s, which none of his competitors could find an answer for.

On the final run, Russell took yet another five-tenths chunk out of his own benchmark to set a dominant 1m42.526s pole lap.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

Ferrari employed a different run plan by delaying its first run, which yielded Leclerc provisional second, and the Monegasque found another tenth that secured second on the grid ahead of Piastri, albeit a sobering eight tenths behind Russell.

Isack Hadjar celebrated his return from injury with fourth on the grid, while Norris slipped up on his final attempt and settled for fifth ahead of Hamilton. Pierre Gasly secured seventh for Alpine as Max Verstappen could only manage eighth after having to slow down for yellow flags caused by Norris on his final lap.

Carlos Sainz made full use of Williams' upgraded FW48 to claim ninth, as Franco Colapinto qualified 10th following an erratic Q3 session.

Russell topped Q2 with a late 1m43.462s effort, two tenths ahead of Verstappen as it promised to set up a tight pole shoot-out.

The battle for the final Q3 spots was as close as it has been all season with Williams now in the hunt, and Sainz capitalised to go ninth and claim a rare Q3 berth. The dramatic rate of track evolution meant drivers were fuelled up for multiple laps to try and peak on their final run In the dying seconds, Alpine's Colapinto snatched 10th away from Haas driver Oliver Bearman, joining his team-mate Gasly in the next segment.

Racing Bulls was the biggest victim in Q2 with Liam Lawson out in 12th, followed by the second Williams of Alex Albon and Esteban Ocon in the remaining Haas. Arvid Lindblad could only muster 15th to continue what has been a messy weekend so far for the Briton, off the back of an FP2 crash which team principal Alan Permane ascribed to "rookie enthusiasm".

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Russell also led the way in Q1 after Antonelli disappeared, demoting Verstappen at the end of the session with a 1m43.615s lap. In the background, Williams comfortably made it through with both of its upgraded cars.

On a high-speed track exposing its power unit deficit, Audi paid the price of Williams' progress as Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg were both eliminated in 17th and 18th. The four cars from Cadillac and Aston Martin were also punched out, with Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll already facing a back-of-the-grid penalty for Honda power unit changes.

Sports.title: Norris says “some drivers shouldn’t be in Formula 1” after Colapinto takes him out | Formula 1
Sports.content:
A dejected Lando Norris said some drivers on the grid should not be in Formula 1 after he was taken out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The reigning world champion was involved in a three-car collision at the restart of the race. The crash began when Franco Colapinto arrived too quickly on the inside of turn one, hit his team mate Pierre Gasly, who in turn hit Norris’s car.

“In end of the day I just got taken out,” said Norris, “so just some drivers that shouldn’t be in Formula 1 to be honest.”

Colapinto received a 10-second time penalty for the collision. Alpine recently renewed Colapinto’s contract to drive for the team again next year.

Norris endured a frustrating race as he said he lacked straight-line speed. He also went off at turn one earlier in the race.

“I just was slow, struggling a lot in the straights,” he said. “You saw how quickly everyone came past me, so it’s just an impossible race out there for me from that side in straight line speed today, so hopefully we get that fixed for next time.”

Sports.title: Colapinto handed 10-second penalty for crash which took out team mate and Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix stewards penalised Franco Colapinto for the Safety Car restart crash which eliminated three drivers.

Colapinto crashed into his team mate Pierre Gasly , who in turn hit McLaren’s Lando Norris, at turn one.

The stewards issued a 10-second time penalty to Colapinto. As he did not finish the race, the stewards may choose to convert this into a grid drop penalty for the next round.

The FIA’s 2026 penalty guidelines state a 10-second penalty is the baseline sanction for causing a collision. They may issue a drive-through penalty or 10 second stop-and-go penalty. A five-second time penalty is permitted if mitigating circumstances apply.

Colapinto said he was “very sad for the team” and offered his apologies. “A big sorry to all of them, to the factory to Pierre, of course, I took him out. So I’m really disappointed.

“We were both in a position to score points. So it was a big day for the theme and I did a big mistake.”

He admitted he lost control of his car before the crash. “I’m just really sorry, it shouldn’t happen. I was locking up and completely out of control. So not a lot I could do.”

Sports.title: Mercedes overtake Ferrari to become F1’s most successful engine builder | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes have become the most successful engine builders in Formula 1 history by scoring their 252nd victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Their latest victory moves them past Ferrari, whose engines held the record for winning the most races since 2004.

Mercedes’ factory team account for the majority of their wins. However three customer teams have also contributed to their wins tally, notably McLaren, who have scored 101 wins. The remainder were contributed by Brawn GP, who took eight wins in their sole season in 2009 before Mercedes bought the team, and Racing Point, who claimed a single victory with Mercedes power in 2020.

In contrast only one of Ferrari’s victories was not scored by their factory team. Sebastian Vettel claimed a single victory for Toro Rosso using Ferrari power at Monza in 2008.

Sports.title: Russell soaks up pressure from Verstappen to win Azerbaijan Grand Prix | 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
George Russell claimed his third victory of 2026 by leading every lap of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver led home the Red Bull pair of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, who rose through the field with strong pace early on.

Russell led the majority of the race until it was interrupted by a Safety Car period triggered by Alexander Albon. The Williams driver crashed out at turn five.

Almost the entire field took the opportunity to pit, after which Russell led from Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar. Verstappen pounced on Piastri for second place at the restart, than carnage broke out behind them.

Franco Colapinto dived down the inside of turn one from a long way back and clattered into his team mate Pierre Gasly. The pair also skittled Lando Norris, who had dropped down the order earlier on by running wide at the same corner.

Remarkably, this wasn’t the only collision by a pair of team mates at the restart. Arvid Lindblad slithered wide into the sister car of Liam Lawson, tipping him into a spin, though the unimpressed Lawson was able to continue. “Man I love getting taken out by my team mate,” he remarked sarcastically. “That’s pretty sick.”

The second restart was clean and Russell led away with Verstappen close behind. Hadjar began applying pressure to Piastri and did not have to wait long for the McLaren driver to slip up. Piastri ran deep at turn one, just as Norris had earlier, and tumbled out of the points places.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen spent the final laps chasing Russell but dropped out of Overtake Mode range when the final lap began. However he closed suddenly after the pair passed the crashed Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas at turn 15. Russell reached the line less than two tenths of a second before Verstappen, while Isack Hadjar completed Red Bull’s first double podium finish for over two years.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli made slow progress initially from 16th place on the grid, losing a place on the first lap. However the Safety Car brought him within range of the front-runners, aided by the disaster for the Alpine drivers. He picked off Lewis Hamilton for fifth place on lap 43 but ran out of time to catch Charles Leclerc.

Lindblad made amends for colliding with his team mate by passing both Haas drivers in the final laps. He took Esteban Ocon as they sprinted for the line, crossing it just three hundredths of a second before his rival.

Oliver Bearman took ninth while Carlos Sainz Jnr picked up a single point in the upgraded Williams.
