Hughes, with Chief Financial Officer Victor Debah, is attending the Airports Council International (ACI) Africa 35th Annual General Assembly, 75th Board and Committee Meetings, Regional Conference and Exhibition, running from September 19 to 25, 2026.



According to a press release issued by the Authority, the weeklong gathering is bringing together airport executives, policymakers, regulators, development partners and aviation industry stakeholders to discuss the future of African aviation under the theme, “Next-Gen Airports: Driving Performance and Resilience.”

The LAA said its participation is intended to strengthen Liberia’s engagement with regional and international aviation institutions while exploring opportunities to improve airport operations, infrastructure and service delivery.

During the conference, the delegation is expected to hold bilateral and multilateral discussions with airport authorities, aviation agencies, development partners, financial institutions and industry stakeholders.

The proposed engagements will focus on technical assistance, operational support, logistics cooperation, capacity development, infrastructure advancement and institutional strengthening.

The Authority said it also plans to explore opportunities for investment, innovation, knowledge transfer and resource mobilization to support the development of Liberia’s airports.

Hughes Pursues Regional Aviation Cooperation

Beyond the ACI Africa conference, Hughes is undertaking separate engagements with key Nigerian aviation institutions, including the Nigeria Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).

The discussions are intended to strengthen technical cooperation and secure logistical and capital support that could improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of Liberia’s aviation infrastructure.

The LAA said the engagements align with its broader objectives of strengthening aviation safety, advancing airport infrastructure development and building technical partnerships to support the long-term growth of the sector.

The Authority also views the conference as an opportunity to deepen regional integration, exchange best practices with other airport operators and explore emerging technologies that could support Liberia’s aviation modernization efforts.

LAA Links Participation to National Development

The Authority said its participation reflects its commitment to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s national development agenda, particularly in improving infrastructure, strengthening regional cooperation and expanding transportation connectivity.

ACI Africa, the regional arm of Airports Council International, represents African airports and promotes advocacy, capacity-building, innovation, connectivity and sustainable growth across the continent’s aviation industry.

The LAA said it remains committed to developing a modern, safe, secure, efficient and resilient airport system capable of supporting economic growth, trade, tourism and regional connectivity while improving services for the traveling public.

The press release did not specify the amount of funding or capital support being sought, identify any agreements finalized during the engagements, or provide a timeline for the anticipated infrastructure improvements.

World.title: Liberian Leader Demands Two Permanent African Seats On Security Council, Fairer Global Finance System
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS, New York – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on Thursday night told world leaders that trust in the United Nations has been broken by the uneven application of its founding principles, and called for sweeping reforms of the Security Council and the global financial system to restore it.

By Rodney D Sieh, rodney,[email protected]

Addressing the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly, held under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All,” the Liberian leader said the world is facing “a lingering crisis of legitimacy and relevance that demands urgent attention.”



“Our answer to that fragmentation cannot be less multilateralism,” President Boakai declared. “It must be better multilateralism!”

‘Eighty years of patience is enough’

The President reserved his strongest words for the Security Council, noting that Africa, home to 1.5 billion people and nearly one-third of UN membership, still has no permanent seat, even though 80 percent of the Council’s mandates concern African peace and security.

“Eighty years of patience is enough. The time for structural reform is now,” he said, describing the imbalance as a “historical injustice” that “is no longer tenable.”

Reaffirming Liberia’s support for the Common African Position, President Boakai said Africa demands no fewer than two permanent seats with full rights, including the veto for as long as it exists, plus additional non-permanent seats. “Correcting this imbalance is not a favor to Africa,” he said. “It is necessary to restore the United Nations’ trust, credibility, and legitimacy.”

Security Council seat and the drug war

Speaking as a current member of the Security Council, the President highlighted threats facing West Africa, including transnational organized crime, cyber warfare and narcotics trafficking along maritime routes in the Gulf of Guinea.

He said Liberia’s Joint Security forces are “tightening the vise on transnational drug cartels,” but stressed that no nation can fight global criminal networks alone. He appealed to international partners for targeted support in coast guard surveillance, intelligence sharing and port security technology.

He also called for an immediate end to hostilities in conflict zones, unhindered humanitarian access and stronger investment in preventive diplomacy, arguing that “the cost of preventing a war pales in comparison to the cost of rebuilding a broken society.”

‘Governed by so few’

On the economy, President Boakai said developing nations are being “squeezed by unsustainable debt, shrinking fiscal space, and mounting external shocks” as the 2030 deadline for the Sustainable Development Goals approaches.

He called for structural reform of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, whose governance, he said, still reflects the world of 1945. “A financial system that decides the fate of billions cannot continue to be governed by so few,” he said.

At home, he pointed to progress under the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development – focused on Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation and Tourism – citing gains in revenue administration and rural farm-to-market roads. He also said his administration is strengthening accountability, financial management and the fight against corruption.

Climate justice, youth and AI

The President noted that Liberia contributes virtually nothing to global emissions yet suffers coastal erosion, flooding and disrupted farming seasons, while holding 42 percent of the remaining Upper Guinean Rainforest. He urged industrialized nations to honor their climate financing pledges and put loss-and-damage mechanisms into operation.

He called for investment in STEM education and digital skills for Africa’s youth, more than 60 percent of whom are under 25, reaffirmed Liberia’s commitment to equality for women and girls, and joined calls for binding rules on artificial intelligence, particularly in warfare. “Innovation must protect human development, not automate human destruction,” he said.

From San Francisco to today

Recalling that Liberia was one of only four African nations to sign the UN Charter in 1945, President Boakai presented the country’s journey from civil war to constitutional democracy as proof that “institutions can be rebuilt.”

He opened his address by congratulating Khalilur Rahman on his election as President of the 81st Session, thanking outgoing President Annalena Baerbock, and saluting Secretary-General António Guterres as he prepares to end his tenure.

“Let us leave this Assembly committed to a United Nations that not only deliberates on crises but also resolves them,” he concluded.

World.title: Liberia: Kwarbo vs. Coleman: The Drug Van Order that Nobody Owns
World.content:
A statement attributed to detained former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell Kwarbo says IG Gregory Coleman ordered him to escort the drug van. His family denies he made it, and the IG calls it part of a four-month disinformation campaign.

MONROVIA — A few days ago, Wadell Kwarbo’s father appeared on Spoon FM with an account of what his detained son had allegedly told him before he was taken into custody.

By Rodney D. Sieh



According to the father, a senior officer had called Kwarbo and instructed him to escort a shipment of drugs. At the time, he did not publicly identify the officer.

This week, however, a name emerged.

A statement attributed to Kwarbo, the former chief of the Liberia National Police Highway Patrol Division who remains detained at the Monrovia Central Prison, identified Police Inspector General Gregory O. W. Coleman as the officer who allegedly made the call.

“Police IG Gregory Coleman ordered me to escort the van. He instructed me to escort the drugs with my patrol vehicle (RL-141). And I acted on his order,” Kwarbo was quoted as saying on Spoon FM.

The statement reportedly went further, calling for his telephone records and written statement to be made available.

“Let them get my call log. My call log can be subpoenaed through the Court,” he was quoted as saying. “Let them release my written statement also. Why are they keeping it? They have it.”

But there is now a direct contradiction over whether Kwarbo actually made those statements.

Family: “He Never Made Such A Statement”

On Thursday, Kwarbo’s wife, Bendu Kwarbo, issued a statement on behalf of the family distancing her husband from the allegations against Coleman.

The family said it “categorically dissociates” Kwarbo from reports attributing the allegations to him and said neither the family nor his lawyers knew about or authorized any statement accusing the police chief.

“Mr. Kwarbo himself firmly rejects and denies this allegation in its entirety and maintains that he has made no such statement,” the family said.

The family said Kwarbo’s lawyers had advised him to remain silent and allow the court process to determine the case.

It described the statement circulating in his name as “malicious” and urged media organizations and the public to verify information before publishing or repeating allegations.

The family also maintains that Kwarbo should not have been arrested and that the case against him is based on what it described as false and misleading allegations.

Coleman: “Sustained Disinformation Campaign”

Coleman, meanwhile, has rejected the allegation and characterized it as part of what he says has been a prolonged campaign to undermine his credibility.

“For the past four months, I have been the target of a sustained disinformation campaign intended to damage my character and silence my fight against the culture of impunity, including the ongoing drug investigation,” Coleman said.

The police chief said freedom of expression must be respected but warned against spreading what he described as false information concerning an active criminal investigation.

“The facts must be established through evidence and lawful process. Anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable under that same process,” Coleman said. “I will remain focused on my duty. I will not be intimidated.”

The US$ 317 Million Drug Case

The dispute comes against the backdrop of Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking investigation, involving a shipment authorities have valued at approximately US$317 million.

Kwarbo, a former Highway Patrol chief, was stripped of his duties and later arrested and charged alongside Anthony T. Blaye, who served as Chief of the Liberia National Police Financial Crime Division.

The two have been accused of using marked police vehicles to escort a large cocaine shipment.

According to findings attributed to a joint Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and Liberia National Police investigation, the cocaine was transported from a coastal landing site to a stash house using two police vehicles in an escort formation, with one vehicle reportedly positioned ahead of the shipment and another behind it.

Coleman said investigators uncovered evidence indicating that state security personnel played a role in moving the narcotics from the landing site to a holding location.

The foreign nationals, a Serbian and a Colombian, are being accused of bringing the cocaine into Liberia through aircraft and shoreline landing operations.

Liberian authorities publicly destroyed the seized cocaine on July 30 in what officials described as the country’s largest-ever drug destruction exercise.

Kwarbo’s Bail Fight

Kwarbo has denied wrongdoing and, in August, filed a motion seeking bail before Criminal Assizes “C” at the Temple of Justice.

His lawyers, including Cllr. Sayma Syrenius Cephus, maintain that he is being detained largely on allegations that he provided an escort to principal defendants after the alleged crimes had already been committed.

Kwarbo’s lawyers argue that the prosecution has not presented objective evidence placing him at the scene before or during the commission of the alleged offenses.

The defense has also challenged allegations attributed to co-defendant Christian Nyantee, arguing that Nyantee may have a motive to shift responsibility and that uncorroborated accomplice testimony should not be sufficient to establish the legal standard required for continued detention.

Kwarbo’s lawyers further contend that he had no prior knowledge of the alleged drug operation and that providing security escorts can form part of routine security duties during major national-security operations.

The Questions That Remain

The latest dispute leaves several questions unanswered.

It remains unclear who spoke to Spoon FM on Kwarbo’s behalf, whether the statement attributed to him was actually made by him, and how the statement emerged from the prison.

It is also unclear whether the written statement Kwarbo was quoted as referring to exists, what it contains, and whether investigators have sought or obtained his telephone records through the court.

Analysts say those questions may be resolved through evidence presented in court rather than competing accounts outside the courtroom.

For now, the public has two sharply different versions: one attributed to Kwarbo naming Coleman as the officer who allegedly ordered the escort, and another from Kwarbo’s family saying he never made the statement.

Kwarbo remains in detention and, under Liberia’s Constitution, is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia: Bail Denied, The Former Vice President’s Lawyers Weigh A Trip To The Supreme Court And a Long Legal Fight
World.content:
MONROVIA – For three weeks, the most important document at Jewel Howard-Taylor’s home has been a visitors’ log.

By Willie N. Tokpa

Every person who passes her gate is written down. Police officers stand watch around the clock. She may step outside only when the court has approved a trip to the hospital in advance. The former vice president, once second in line to lead the country, now needs a judge’s permission to see her doctor.



On Thursday, her lawyers went to court hoping to change that. They left with the same restrictions in place and a stinging rebuke from the bench.

By evening, the defense team had gathered in Monrovia to decide what comes next. For lawyers who have shifted strategy more than once in five weeks, the choices are narrowing. The road now leads up Capitol Hill, to the Supreme Court.

“We believe that she is eligible”

Atty. Gbawu Kowou, one of her lawyers, said the defense would take its case to the Justice in Chambers.

“The court argued that the crime extended up to 2026 based on the allegation that she received US$15,000. We disagree,” he told FrontPageAfrica. “The defense believes the court did not properly apply Liberia’s law on bail and pretrial detention, and that is the reason we are filing a petition for certiorari before the Justice in Chambers. We believe that she is eligible for bail.”

The papers are ready, he said. The team hopes to file on Friday, September 25, or by Monday, September 28 at the latest. Cllr. Kabina Ja’neh and former Associate Justice Lavalah Supuwood will lead the fight.

And the woman at the center of it? “The Vice President has been briefed on the latest decision from the court,” Kowou said.

A judge’s rebuke

The defense’s argument was simple. The 2023 Controlled Drugs and Substances Act makes the charges against her grave and non-bailable. But her lawyers said the conduct she is accused of happened in 2021 and 2022, before the law existed. A law, they argued, cannot reach back in time.

Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C” turned to the defense’s own paperwork to answer them.

Attached to their motion was the Writ of Arrest. It alleges that she received US$15,000 from the cartel through Sheikh Bashiru Kante as recently as August 2026. If true, the judge reasoned, the alleged conduct did not stop in 2022. It ran well past the new law.

Then he went further. He accused the defense of ignoring a major part of its own exhibit and warned that such conduct runs against the lawyers’ code of ethics. It is rare for a judge to scold counsel this way in a pretrial ruling.

Her lawyers noted their exception and told the court they would “take advantage of the statute controlling.” In Liberian courtrooms, everyone knows what that means: we’ll see you upstairs.

The road upstairs

The tool they will likely use is a writ of certiorari. Just last month, on August 28, the Supreme Court ruled in the Capitol arson case that certiorari is the proper way to challenge a trial judge’s interlocutory ruling. Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay explained that it lets the high court review a lower court that has jurisdiction but is alleged to have acted irregularly or contrary to law.

Recent history offers the defense both hope and caution.

In March 2025, Justice in Chambers Ceanneh Clinton Johnson overturned a Criminal Court “C” decision revoking the bail of Peach Bility, son of Representative Musa Hassan Bility, and sent him home.

Six years earlier, it went the other way. Justice Joseph Nagbe granted the State’s petition and overturned a trial judge who had found grounds to admit murder suspect Oliver Dillon to bail. Dillon stayed behind bars.

A filing could also buy time. In a 2024 case, the State’s certiorari petition automatically halted scheduled Criminal Court “C” proceedings until a conference with the Justice in Chambers. A similar pause here would freeze action before Judge Feika while the high court looks at his ruling.

Whatever the outcome, the question reaches beyond one defendant. The Justices may have to decide whether a no-bail law passed in 2023 can apply to conduct that allegedly began before it. Judge Feika’s order leaned on the continuing nature of the alleged offense and did not squarely answer that argument. The defense is likely to press the gap.

Waiting on the grand jury

Other fights remain unresolved. Judge Feika still has to rule on defense motions to quash the arrest writ, a habeas corpus petition and a motion to suppress evidence.

The defense has already shown it is willing to change course. On September 17, it withdrew the preliminary examination before Magistrate L. Ben Barco, giving up an early chance to test the State’s evidence. That evidence includes WhatsApp messages and audio recordings investigators say came from Kante’s phone. No one has yet heard them played in court.

And over all of it hangs the grand jury. Judge Feika can decide whether she goes home or stays confined. He cannot put her on trial without an indictment, and more than a month after her arrest, there is none.

Her allies have noticed. Lenn Eugene Nagbe, chief of staff to former President George Weah, said the government’s failure to indict her raises questions about the strength of its case.

The August Term of Court is in its 39th day of jury sitting. The clock is running.

The bigger picture

Her case sits at the heart of Liberia’s widest drug investigation. It began with a cocaine seizure valued at about US$317 million and has reached into the police, the intelligence services and the prison system.

Her party, the Coalition for Democratic Change, calls it political persecution. The government says she is presumed innocent and will have her day in court.

She was released from Monrovia Central Prison on medical grounds on September 4. The court has warned she could be sent back if her health improves significantly.

So she waits. Behind her gate, under guard, with each visitor’s name written in a book, while her lawyers climb the hill to argue that the case against her belongs to 2021, and the State insists it runs right up to this summer.

World.title: Namibian Government eulogizes Lt Gen Zuze
World.content:
The Government of Namibia says it is deeply saddened by the passing of first Indigenous Zambia Airforce Commander, Peter Zuze (Retired).

In a statement Issued to the media in Lusaka by Namibia’s Ministry of International Relations and Trade, Lt Gen Zuze has been described as a distinguished military leader, diplomat, and a steadfast friend of Namibia.

The Namibian government stated that Lt. Gen. Zuze, who died in Lusaka on September 14, 2026 after an illness, had left behind a legacy of leadership and solidarity that extended beyond Zambia’s borders.

According to the Namibian Ministry, he is remembered as the first indigenous Commander of the Zambia Air Force and later as Zambia’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations between 1986 and 1991.

The Namibian Government noted that during the period, Lt. Gen. ZUZE also served as President of the United Nations Council for Namibia from 1988 to 1991, a role the ministry said was pivotal in advancing Namibia’s independence.

The Ministry stated that Lt. Gen. Zuze had presided over the Council’s special meeting in Windhoek in April 1990, where he transmitted the declaration affirming Namibia’s determination to achieve independence.

The Ministry noted that these actions symbolised Zambia’s unwavering support for Namibia’s liberation.

The Namibian Government emphasised that Lt. Gen Zuze’s passing represented not only the loss of a distinguished son of Zambia but also of a brother in the struggle and a friend in peace.

The ministry added that the nation remained eternally grateful to late Lt. Gen Zuze, for his contributions to justice, democracy, and international cooperation.

World.title: Siavonga Police officer Jailed for corruption
World.content:
The Siavonga Subordinate Court has convicted and sentenced a Police Officer, of Chirundu Police Station in Southern Province to 12 months imprisonment with hard labour for corruption involving Eight Hundred Kwacha (K800.00).

Lusaka High Court Judge, Ireen Wishimanga, presiding over the Siavonga Subordinate Court of the First Class, convicted Francis Chisala on one (1) count of Corrupt Practices by a Public Officer, contrary to Section 19(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act, Chapter 91 of the Laws of Zambia.

This is contained in a statement issued to the media in Lusaka, by Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Head of Corporate Communications, Joseph Mwenya.

Mr Mwenya stated that in July 2024, the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) arrested and charged Chisala, with one count of corrupt practices by a public officer.

He explained that Chisala, on dates between 30th November 2020 and 3rd December 2020, in Chirundu district, being a public officer and a Police officer at Chirundu Police Station, corruptly obtained Eight Hundred Kwacha.

Mr Mwenya added that the money was obtained as gratification from Jeremiah Phiri, as an inducement not to charge him with a traffic offence and allow him to use the Chirundu-Lusaka road, a transaction concerning the Zambia Police Service, a public body.

He has since warned public officers against soliciting or accepting bribes or any form of gratification in the execution of their duties, stressing that their office is a position of trust and must be exercised with integrity and in the interest of the public.

“This conviction and sentence should serve as a warning to all public officers that engaging in corrupt practices has serious consequences,” said Mr Mwenya.

He emphasised that the Commission will continue to investigate and, where evidence establishes an offence, ensure that those involved in corruption face the full force of the law.

World.title: MOH PS bemoans high cases of Childhood Cancer
World.content:
Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary, Kennedy Lishimpi, has noted that Childhood Cancer remains an important public health concern not only in Zambia but on the globe.

Dr Lishimpi revealed that approximately 400,000 children and adolescents aged between zero and 19 years develop Cancer every year globally, with the majority of cases occurring in low- and middle-income countries where survival rates remain low.

Dr Lishimpi was speaking in a speech read for him by Cancer Diseases Hospital (CDH) Head of Clinical Care, Paul Kamfwa at a candlelight vigil held in Lusaka last evening to commemorate Childhood Cancer Awareness month at the (CDH) in Lusaka.

He also noted that Zambia continues to face challenges in Childhood Cancer care, including delayed diagnosis, referral processes, access to specialised treatment, availability of medicines, human resources and the ability of families to remain on treatment for the required duration.

He said the Government, working with cooperating partners, has made progress in addressing some of the barriers to Childhood Cancer treatment.

Dr Lishimpi stressed that Zambia remains committed to contributing to the WHO Global Initiative for Childhood Cancer target of achieving at least 60 percent survival among children with cancer by 2030.

He cited Zambia’s participation in the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer medicines, a collaboration involving the World Health Organisation (WHO).

He stressed the need for early diagnosis, saying unusual symptoms in children should not be ignored and assured that early recognition and detection of Cancer can save lives.

Dr Lishimpi further emphasised the need for compassionate, child-centered care, emotional and social support for children and families throughout the treatment journey.

Meanwhile, Lions District 413 Zambia Governor, George Banda said the organisation has continued to support efforts aimed at raising awareness of Childhood Cancer.

Mr Banda said Lions International designated September as Childhood Cancer Awareness Month to promote advocacy and support for children affected by the disease.

Mr Banda said the Lions Club of Roma has identified CDH as one of its partners and regularly responds to requests for support from the hospital.

And a cancer survivor, Chawaza Chalwe, said Cancer is a treatable disease when diagnosed early.

World.title: Chipolopolo will bounce back against Togo – Lwandamina
World.content:
Coach George Lwandamina is banking on home advantage to revive Zambia’s AFCON 2027 qualification hopes after injuries and mistakes condemned Chipolopolo to a 3-1 defeat in Algeria.

Zambia’s campaign got off to a false start on Friday night at the packed Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium, where Algeria punished a brave but inexperienced Chipolopolo side.

Despite the loss, Lwandamina insisted his young team fought to the end in a hostile atmosphere.

“It was a tough match and the boys played well. Away from home, it wasn’t easy for them, but they fought to the bitter end,” he said.

The Chipolopolo mentor was candid about what went wrong. Algeria took an early lead through Jaouen Hadjam after just two minutes, and after Fashion Sakala equalised in the 57th minute, Ibrahim Maza and Anis Hadj Moussa struck in the 67th and 72nd minutes.

“Few mistakes, of course, and we were punished. Injuries also affected us. We had to make changes which we wouldn’t have made, and that cost us the game,” Lwandamina admitted.

With Togo beating Burundi 1-0 in Lomé to join Algeria on three points, Zambia are now bottom of Group I. But Lwandamina issued a stern warning ahead of Monday’s home clash.

“Definitely, we need to win our home games if we are to qualify. Togo won’t have it easy,” he said.

The former ZESCO United and Yanga tactician believes his youthful squad will only get better.

“This is a young team and they are coping very well. We can actually change the tables. The boys are fighting very hard and, with a little bit of experience in the team, I’m sure we’ll be able to bring them together.”

He also paid tribute to Algeria’s depth, describing them as a football powerhouse.

“Algeria enjoyed their game. They played well. Algeria has a new team, mind you, Algeria is one of the big countries in the world, so the population is very big and you have more options of players out there. You can even make 10 teams here in Algeria.”

Zambia host Togo on September 29 at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola, where only victory will keep their qualification bid alive.

World.title: Njobvu Says Judiciary Dented Its Reputation by Closing Courts After the Election
World.content:
Democratic Union leader Ackim Njobvu has said the Judiciary dented its own reputation when it closed courts after the disputed general election, and that it will be difficult for the institution to erase the effect on citizens’ access to justice.

Mr Njobvu said the damage was greatest at a time when people needed the courts most, particularly during the election. In an interview, he said the Judiciary must now work harder to restore public confidence and ensure citizens can exercise their constitutional rights.

He questioned whether denying citizens access to the courts was consistent with the responsibility to uphold justice.

“When you are closing courts, when you are denying people justice, when people needed to petition you close the courts. People lost trust and confidence in such institutions,” Mr Njobvu said.

The Judiciary, he said, should take steps to restore its reputation and prevent citizens from losing confidence in the country’s justice system. He addressed it directly.

“You have to respond to this. You have to redeem yourselves. You have dented your reputation as a Judiciary. Zambians have no respect and trust in this dented Judiciary,” he said.

Mr Njobvu also pointed to major judicial decisions on the eligibility of the late former president Edgar Lungu and on constitutional amendments. The Judiciary’s handling of such matters, he said, should be examined against its previous decisions.

He said citizens should be allowed to exercise their constitutional rights, including access to the courts, and closed with an appeal.

“What I would love to appeal is that where we are right now, let’s accord citizens the opportunity to access the courts. Let’s accord citizens the opportunity to exercise their rights,” Mr Njobvu said.

He then turned to the losing candidates of the United Party for National Development (UPND). Mr Njobvu questioned their decision to challenge the results of the polls after the ruling party had described the elections as free and fair.

World.title: Hichilema Dismisses Talk of Crisis, Warns Social Media Users Against Scaring Off Investors
World.content:
Hichilema Dismisses Talk of Crisis, Warns Social Media Users Against Scaring Off Investors

President Hakainde Hichilema has rejected claims that Zambia is in crisis after the polls, saying disgruntled and selfish individuals are creating a false impression of tension and scaring off the investors the Government has worked to attract.

The President spoke at State House in Lusaka yesterday during the swearing-in of Patricia Malaila as Deputy Auditor-General for the Audit Division at the Office of the Auditor-General. He used the occasion to question the motives of people, at home and abroad, who use social media to portray the country in a bad light, and he opened with an appeal.

“Let’s love our country; let’s not do things that damage our country consciously,” Mr Hichilema said.

He follows what is posted online, he said, and some of it is doing harm without those posting it realising. The Head of State then put the question to them directly.

“I scan social media, the kind of stuff that is thrown in there, you don’t realise what you are doing; you are scaring off an investor we have worked so hard to attract. What is your intention?” he asked.

The effect of such posts, the President said, is to make investors, whether domestic, regional or international, believe that something is wrong in Zambia. Nothing is, he insisted, and the country had already settled the matter at the ballot box.

“There is no issue in this country. We have had an election, Zambians voted, decisions are made by Zambians. We move on. What is this hullabaloo, creating a crisis where there is none?” he said.

Some of the people painting the country in a negative light had selfish interests, he said, because they were unhappy that they did not occupy certain public offices. Citizens who claim to love Zambia, he added, should stop peddling falsehoods, and he then turned to what follows when the law is crossed.

“Let us not have that mentality; let’s love this country, focus on the work ahead of us, let’s stay within the law. If you veer off the law, then you will pay. It doesn’t matter how old you are; the law does not recognise age, it recognises wrongdoing,” he said.

The appeal was not limited to those at home. Zambians living abroad were urged to remain law-abiding and to avoid conduct that could harm the country’s reputation.

The office he holds also featured in the address. State House, the President said, must stay focused on government business and national development, and he asked that it not be turned into something else.

“Let’s not dilute this office and make it something else, this office is sacred; it’s for serious work,” he said.

At the same ceremony, the Head of State called on public officers to treat public money with care, saying every kwacha saved is critical to the success of the Grow Zambia Agenda.

On the economy, Mr Hichilema said falling inflation and rising growth were evidence that the country was moving in the right direction. He asked citizens to support efforts to sustain the momentum.

Figures from the Zambia Statistics Agency (ZamStats) show inflation at 6.2 per cent in August, down from 6.5 per cent in July. The President said the country had come a long way from the high inflation levels recorded when he assumed office in 2021.

Growth was the second marker he pointed to. ZamStats data show the economy expanded by 7.7 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 4.5 per cent in the same period last year, and he urged Zambians to read the signs.

“You must read the writing on the wall, there’s something good happening in this country and be part of that good,” the President said.

Citizens were asked to recognise the progress made so far and to contribute to the implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda. Careless actions, he warned, could undermine the gains being recorded, and he closed with a final appeal.

“Let us accelerate this growth, let us not damage the growth by our carelessness as citizens. Then we will show love to this nation called Zambia,” he said.

The latest ZamStats monthly bulletin, released on Thursday, puts second-quarter growth at 7.2 per cent, slightly below the 7.9 per cent recorded in the same quarter of 2025. It also shows annual inflation easing to 6.1 per cent in September from 6.2 per cent in August.

World.title: Police Say Kalumba Was Lawfully Arrested as Opposition Alleges Abduction and UPND Condemns His Remarks
World.content:
Police have rejected claims that former minister Dr Katele Kalumba was abducted, saying he was lawfully apprehended in Chienge and charged with harassment under the Cyber Crimes Act for allegedly publishing content meant to humiliate President Hakainde Hichilema.

Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said in a statement that Dr Kalumba was apprehended on 23 September in Chienge, in Luapula Province. He was formally charged the following day at Kabwe Central Police Station.

The charge is harassment under Section 22 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025. Police say it relates to content Dr Kalumba allegedly published on 11 August to humiliate the President.

The statement followed claims from the opposition that the arrest was an abduction. We Are One Zambia (WOZA) and Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance secretary general Muhabi Lungu said Dr Kalumba’s wife described the arrest as an abduction by heavily armed soldiers and police, who did not explain why they were taking him or where.

When the arrest was announced, Mr Lungu said, ruling party supporters dismissed it as fake. That forced the wife to make a recording.

Mr Lungu said it was laughable that Dr Kalumba was bundled into a military vehicle in Chienge and driven all the way to Kabwe, in Central Province, only to face charges. He said the journey fitted a pattern he described as a new punishment tactic, using jurisdiction as a weapon.

“Dr Kalumba was transferred all the way from Chiengi to Kabwe because a Kabwe resident allegedly complained. So, we can speculate that we will all be arrested and transported to a distant district for prosecution as punishment. Same with Mundubile and Makebi. From Kabwe, now Solwezi,” he said.

The two men he named, treason-accused opposition leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, were moved from Kabwe to Solwezi, where they appeared in the Magistrates Court on Friday on sedition charges. Mr Lungu said the transfers showed the same law being abused.

He went further, saying the continued arrests and clampdown on opponents and critics were meant to stoke fear and silence dissent. The aim, he said, was to lay the ground for a third term for the President and make him untouchable.

Mr Lungu also accused the United Party for National Development (UPND) Government of repealing the offence of defaming the President from the Penal Code, only to smuggle it back in a stronger and more punitive form through the sedition and cyber laws.

“Essentially, if you offer constructive criticism to the President, you are abducted and booked for sedition or cyber harassment,” he said.

He warned that the conduct of the Government amounted to the militarisation of politics, with Zambia projected as a constitutional democracy but policed like a military state.

“There is no remorse from the perpetrators of this crackdown. One has to ask: Are these arrests meant to create fear so that the President becomes unaccountable to anyone?” Mr Lungu said.

The ruling party took a different view of the matter. UPND deputy spokesperson Elvis Nkandu strongly condemned remarks attributed to Dr Kalumba against the President, describing them as regrettable and entirely out of step with constructive national discourse.

Mr Nkandu was referring to a video now circulating on social media in which the former minister makes disparaging remarks and issues threats against the President. The video is believed to have been made before the general election.

Citizens are free to express personal views, Mr Nkandu said, but such freedoms must be exercised with responsibility and deep respect for vital State institutions, particularly the presidency.

He expressed disappointment that a veteran figure of Dr Kalumba’s stature, a former senior public servant and prominent politician, would resort to disrespectful rhetoric. That was especially so, he said, given the history of his relationship with the current administration.

Dr Kalumba was imprisoned for corruption in 2022. President Hichilema pardoned him on medical grounds, and he was released from prison on 1 August 2023.

Mr Nkandu said that act of mercy should never be misconstrued as weakness.

“President Hichilema had every opportunity to approach the matter purely from a political perspective, but he instead demonstrated humanity and compassion,” he said.

He also issued a stern warning against attempts to promote regionalism and tribal divisions. The presidency belongs to all citizens, he said, and political disagreements should never be allowed to erode national unity.

Healthy criticism of Government policy is welcome, Mr Nkandu said, but it should not compromise the dignity of the Head of State. He urged Dr Kalumba to use his extensive political experience to contribute constructively to national development rather than divisive commentary.

Police maintain that Dr Kalumba was lawfully apprehended on 23 September and formally charged the next day at Kabwe Central Police Station.

World.title: Chipolopolo fall in Algeria
World.content:
Captain Fashion Sakala was on target but Zambia launched the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 3-1 loss to Algeria in Group I.

Algeria posted a well deserved win after dominating both halves at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium.

The home side started on a promising note when Jaouen Hadjam opened the scoring just after two minutes.

Algeria went into the half time break leading 1-0 after wasting some decent chances.

Saudi Arabia based Sakala equalised 12 minutes after the break to make it 1-1.

But Algeria bounced back in front after 67 minutes when Ibrahim Maza beat Zambia keeper Willard Mwanza from inside the box.

Winger Anis Hadj Moussa sealed the win in the 72nd minute with Algeria’s third.

The result puts Algeria top of Group I on three points on goal difference after Match Day One, while Zambia are bottom.

In the other Group I match played today, Togo made a winning start with a 1-0 victory over Burundi at the Kégué Stadium in Lomé.

Karim Dermane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to give the Sparrow Hawks all three points.

Togo controlled the first half and held on in the second, with Burundi unable to find an equalizer.

Group I Table After Match Day 1:

1. Algeria – 3 pts (+2)

2. Togo – 3 pts (+1)

3. Burundi – 0 pts (-1)

4. Zambia – 0 pts (-2)

Togo now travel to face Zambia on 29th September, while Burundi host Algeria on the same day.

World.title: Nigeria: 'Dangote Refinery IPO Opens Ownership to Nigerian Investors'
World.content:
Nigerians can invest in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals with a minimum subscription of N5,250 under an initial public offering launched recently. The company is offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 each. The offer, valued at about N2.15 trillion if fully subscribed, opened September 14 and is scheduled to close October 13.

FCMB Group Chief Executive, Ladi Balogun, said the offer gives Nigerians access to a world-scale business while demonstrating the growing reach of the country's capital market.

"It presents an opportunity for every Nigerian to experience the benefits of investing in world-class and world-scale businesses that would otherwise be inaccessible,"Balogun said at the opening gong ceremony and Facts Behind the Offer presentation at the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos.

Balogun said Nigeria's capital market was deepening as it attracted retail, high-net-worth, institutional and international investors through a widening range of channels.



"Retail investors are buying shares on their mobile phones through fintechs, banks and brokers," he said. "High-net-worth individuals and institutional investors such as pension funds are bringing depth to the market, while international investors are bringing scale." He said the breadth of participation demonstrated the market's capacity to help credible Nigerian companies raise capital at scale. Balogun also described the refinery as largely insulated from the macroeconomic and currency risks associated with the Nigerian economy.

"The number of such companies on our Exchange is growing," he said. "This indicates the potential and direction of the Nigerian economy."

World.title: Niger: Canadians, Australians and Americans Relaunch Niger's Uranium Industry
World.content:
Niamey — Niger's military junta is seeking to relaunch the country's uranium mining industry with the signing of an agreement with Australian company Atomic Eagle, through which the State of Niger has established the Madaouela Mining Company (MAMICO). The company, 60% owned by Atomic Eagle and 40% by the Nigerien State, plans to revive uranium mining operations in Agadez, in the central-northern part of the country.

The agreement provides for an initial royalty payment of 10 million US dollars, as well as investments in local development and in strengthening the capacity of the mining administration. According to the Ministry of Mines, the project should also create around 1,000 jobs for young Nigeriens.

Madaouela has a resource of 52,843 tonnes of uranium oxide, an estimate based on exploration carried out by the previous licence holder, GoviEx Uranium Inc., which obtained the licence in 2016.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The agreement settles the dispute that arose following the expropriation of the project from GoviEx in 2024. GoviEx and Tombador Iron merged in November 2025, creating Atomic Eagle. Under the agreement reached, the new company will withdraw its arbitration proceedings within seven days of the signing of the agreement.

The pact signed with the Australian company came just days after Canadian mining company Global Atomic obtained approval from the Board of Directors of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) for debt financing of up to 414.2 million US dollars for its Dasa uranium mine project, also in the Agadez region.

The Dasa deposit is operated by Société Minière de Dasa (SOMIDA), a Niger-based company 80% owned by Global Atomic and 20% by the Nigerien government. Discovered in 2010 and authorized in 2020, the deposit has been under mining activity since 2022, but its full development has been subject to several delays. The completion of the mine is now expected in the first half of 2028, with commissioning scheduled for the second half of the year.

Niger's mining sector was historically dominated by French industry, first Areva and subsequently Orano. Niamey nationalized the local subsidiary amid deteriorating relations with France and closer ties with Russia. Orano, 90% owned by the French State, has launched several legal actions against Niger, accusing the authorities of confiscating its assets in the country.

Despite the Russian presence in the country and the insecurity caused by jihadist groups, Anglo-Saxon mining companies do not appear to be facing particular obstacles in investing in Niger's uranium sector.

World.title: Africa: WHO Director-General's remarks at the High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response
World.content:
document

New York — Your Excellency Dr Khalilur Rahman, President of the General Assembly, Your Excellency Amar Bendjama, President of ECOSOC, My sister, Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohamed, The Right Honourable Helen Clark, Excellencies, dear colleagues and friends,

Soon after my election as Director-General in 2017, I was invited to speak at an event at Columbia University here in New York during the General Assembly.

The title was: is the world ready for the next pandemic? My answer was no.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Just over two years later, COVID-19 arrived and indeed, the world was not prepared.

It became the most severe global health crisis in a century, causing more than 20 million excess deaths, and wiping over US$ 10 trillion from the global economy.

The pandemic exposed and exacerbated faultlines in global health security.

During the pandemic and since, WHO established 10 initiatives to make the world safer from future epidemics and pandemics, in five key areas. Most of these were recommendations of the panel led by President Ellen Sirleaf and former Prime Minister Helen Clark.

To strengthen national capacities, the Pandemic Fund with the World Bank and the Universal Health and Preparedness Review;

To strengthen surveillance and early warning, the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence in Berlin;

To improve equitable access to vaccines and other tools, the Access to COVID-19 Tools Accelerator and COVAX.; the interim Medical Countermeasures Network; the mRNA Technology Transfer Programme in South Africa, and the Biomanufacturing Workforce Training Initiative in the Republic of Korea;

To encourage international sharing of pathogen samples, the WHO BioHub in Switzerland.

And to strengthen international response capacity, the Global Health Emergency Corps.

In addition to strengthening all these components of global health security, Member States also strengthened the international legal framework that governs pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.

Two years ago, Member States adopted a package of amendments to the International Health Regulations, which entered into force last September.

And at the World Health Assembly last year, you adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement. This is very historic.

In a divided and divisive world, countries found common ground for a common purpose. You showed that multilateralism still works, and it’s alive and well.

The final piece of the puzzle is the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing system, which countries are continuing to negotiate.

Although differences remain, I am confident that countries will find common ground, just as they did with the Agreement itself.

It’s essential they do, so the Agreement can begin the process of ratification and enter into force as international law.

But let me be clear about one thing: the Pandemic Agreement and the IHR do not – I repeat, do not – infringe on national sovereignty in any way.

On the contrary, they have been negotiated and adopted by sovereign states, as an act of their sovereignty.

Because they recognize that pandemics do not respect borders – I think all of us repeated the same thing – and the best defence against them is not isolation, but cooperation.

Pandemic prevention, preparedness and response is not merely a noble aspiration. Is it a global public good.

In my speech at Columbia University nine years ago, I used a phrase for the first time that I came to use many more times during the pandemic.

I said that no one is safe until everyone is safe.

That is the spirit of the declaration that is before you today.

I commend Member States for the seriousness and stamina you brought to negotiating it.

In particular, I thank the co-facilitators, His Excellency Ambassador Ngoga of Rwanda and His Excellency Ambassador Hovhannisyan of Armenia.

I also recognize Her Excellency Annalena Baerbock of Germany for her efforts to advance this work during her time as President of the General Assembly.

I know the negotiations were not easy, and that differences remain.

But you have agreed on important commitments to concrete, measurable and urgent action to address gaps:

A commitment to build and strengthen local and national capacities;

A commitment to invest in resilient health systems;

A commitment to foster trust in public health systems and institutions;

A commitment to community engagement;

And a commitment to solidarity and equity in access to products, tools and resources.

Close 

We welcome the political declaration, and we look forward to its adoption.

Excellencies,

The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as DSG Amina has said, is a reminder of the ever-present threat of epidemics and pandemics, not only for local communities, but the whole world.

Ebola is unlikely to become a pandemic, but the next pandemic is a matter of when, not if.

So today, I leave you with just one request – just one: get PABS done, as soon as possible. Please conclude the negotiation as soon as possible.

Further delays are not just delays in procedure or process. They are delays that cost all countries dearly when the next pandemic arrives.

We can never say the world is ready enough. The threat evolves, and so must we.

But is the world more ready than it was before COVID-19? Yes and no.

But if you fulfil the commitments you are making today, you will make it a yes.

I thank you.

World.title: Nigeria: Unga - Cavista Convenes U.S., African Leaders On Investment Opportunities
World.content:
Cavista Holdings brought together African and U.S. business leaders, investors, policymakers and development finance stakeholders in New York on Monday, September 21, for its annual U.S.-Africa Leadership Dinner, held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

The gathering focused on opportunities and challenges shaping investment across Africa, including infrastructure, energy, agriculture, manufacturing, technology and critical minerals.

Among those in attendance were former Botswana President Dr. Mokgweetsi Masisi; Nigeria's Minister of Education, Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa; the Emir of Kano, HRH Muhammadu Sanusi II; Zamfara State Governor Dr. Dauda Lawal; and former Ekiti State Governor and former Minister of Mines and Steel Development, Dr. Kayode Fayemi.

Two discussions examined the U.S.-Africa investment landscape. The first featured Cavista Holdings Chairman Niyi John Olajide and John Jovanovic, President and Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM). The second brought together Olajide and Sameh Shenouda, Executive Director and Chief Investment Officer of Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), with Tom Sheehy of Quinella Global and KRL International as moderator.



Speaking on the theme, "Catalyzing U.S.-Africa Investment," Olajide, who also chairs the Corporate Council on Africa, said the next phase of investment would depend not only on capital but on strong, trusted partnerships.

"Africa needs long-term capital, but investors also need trusted local partners who understand the market, the operating environment and the realities of execution," he said.

Olajide said U.S. businesses could bring capital, technology and expertise, while African businesses contribute local knowledge, resources, talent and access to growing markets.

Jovanovic said successful investment in Africa requires early engagement, market knowledge and the right partnerships.

"Africa is not a place to go alone," he said, adding that EXIM seeks to help create partnerships that attract more private capital to projects supporting Africa's industrialisation.

Bridging investment and execution

A key theme of the discussions was the gap between investor interest in Africa and successful execution. Speakers stressed the importance of reliable local partners with regulatory knowledge, strong stakeholder relationships and experience operating in complex markets.

Shenouda said Africa's growing importance to the global economy meant investors needed more than capital.

Close 

"Investors need deep local knowledge and the ability to navigate very different markets and execute successfully," he said, noting that AFC combines capital, local expertise and investment experience to develop scalable projects.

Cavista said its own operating experience reflects the importance of bridging capital and execution. The holding company has investments across agriculture, food processing, financial services, hospitality and technology.

In Nigeria, Agbeyewa Farms is developing a large-scale cassava value chain in Ekiti State, while Matna Foods processes cassava into food-grade starch in neighbouring Ondo State. PayZeep operates in financial services in Nigeria and Botswana, while Glocient Hospitality operates Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort.

Through Cavista Technologies, the group also provides technology services across Nigeria, India, Botswana, the Philippines and the United States.

Cavista said its New York engagements around the UN General Assembly form part of its broader effort to deepen commercial ties between African businesses and global partners, helping move investment discussions from interest to execution and create long-term value across Africa.

World.title: Nigeria: Nigeria, U.S.Sign Framework to Unlock $700bn Mineral Wealth
World.content:
The federal government and the United States have signed an agreement to deepen American investment in Nigeria's mining sector and promote greater development of the country's mineral resources, estimated by the government at about $700 billion.

The agreement was signed by the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, at the Nigeria Mission House in New York on Wednesday, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Alake announced the development in a post on X on Thursday, saying the framework would cover geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

According to Alake, the agreement is an important step in strengthening Nigeria-US cooperation around the country's mineral resources.



He said, "This is an important step in strengthening Nigeria-US cooperation around our mineral resources, valued at about $700 billion. The framework covers geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure, and technical capacity.

"Nigeria cannot remain a source of raw materials while others capture most of the value. We want more local processing, quality jobs, stronger skills and greater opportunities for Nigerian businesses.

"In the coming months, we will turn this framework into projects, investments and real results for our people. We will identify viable projects and build partnerships that create value for Nigerians and our US partners."

The agreement comes as the federal government intensifies efforts to attract foreign investment into the solid minerals sector and increase local value addition.

World.title: Liberia: Robtel Pailey Says U.S. Deportee Deal Is Unconstitutional
World.content:
Liberia's agreement to take up to 1,200 people deported from the United States violates the Constitution and undermines the country's credibility on the U.N. Security Council, Liberian academic Robtel Neajai Pailey argues in a commentary calling on the government to cancel agreements with Washington that breach national law.

By David Menjor

Pailey, writing Thursday in Al Jazeera English, said the Legislature never debated or approved the deal and that the executive authorized it alone. Article 34(f) of the Constitution gives the Legislature power to approve "treaties, conventions and such other international agreements negotiated or signed on behalf of the Republic."

"On that basis, implementing the agreement without legislative approval is unconstitutional," she wrote. She called the arrangement "politically fraught, ethically suspect and illegal."

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Her commentary, titled "Liberia is squandering the moral authority it claims at the UN," comes as Liberia prepares to take the rotating presidency of the Security Council in December as a nonpermanent member. Pailey argues that Liberia has spent its time on the council presenting itself as a principled voice on the humanitarian cost of war, and that hosting people expelled by Washington contradicts that position.

The first 20 deportees, most of them from Latin American countries including Venezuela and Cuba, arrived at Roberts International Airport on Aug. 20. Pailey said the agreement was signed Sept. 10, 2025.

Pailey, who researches migration in Liberia, said officials would not show her the agreement. She said Foreign Minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti told her it was "at the level of the National Security Council" and could not be shared. The president's national security adviser professed not to know about it, and the director of the National Security Agency acknowledged having it but has not responded, she wrote. The then-justice minister, now acting defense minister, told her it was classified because it was concluded with a foreign country. She said she eventually found it on the U.S. State Department's website.

She also disputes the government's statement that Liberia did not demand or receive compensation. Citing an Aug. 21 New York Times report, she said Trump administration officials agreed to pay Liberia US$5 million for accepting deportees.

"How was the US$5m negotiated and by whom?" she wrote. "What exactly does funding cover? How are resources being channeled if not through Liberia's budget? Who manages the money? How are expenses monitored and reported?"

Close 

When it announced the deal in August, the government said the deportees would be received as "guests of the Republic," would be free to leave, could apply for asylum, and would receive services with help from the International Organization for Migration and the U.N. refugee agency. It said Liberia had not demanded or received compensation.

Pailey said deportees reported being detained in the United States without due process and chained on the flight to Liberia, treatment she argues may breach the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. She said the arrangement may also breach the 1967 Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees, the Convention Against Torture and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. No court has ruled on those claims.

Some deportees who refused to leave the plane were flown on to Equatorial Guinea. Reuters put the number at five; Pailey puts it at six.

Pailey places the deal in a century of unequal agreements with Washington, including the 1926 arrangement under which Liberia took a US$5 million loan from a Firestone subsidiary and granted the company a 99-year lease on 1 million acres. She also cites a health cooperation memorandum signed last December, under which she says Liberia gave the United States access to citizens' health data in exchange for more than US$124 million in planned assistance.

"By accepting mostly Black and brown deportees under such questionable arrangements," she wrote, Liberia is complicit in U.S. expulsions that would shame the formerly enslaved and free Black Americans who founded it.

She said Liberia must cancel agreements with the United States that weaken its autonomy, violate national laws and erode citizens' trust.

World.title: Niger: Niger Rejects Key Rights Recommendations At UN Review
World.content:
press release

Junta Refuses Calls to Free Detainees, Protect LGBT People, Reconsider ICC Withdrawal

Niger has rejected key recommendations raised by United Nations member countries during its Universal Periodic Review (UPR) earlier this year, including calls to address arbitrary detention, discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) people, and accountability for serious human rights violations.

The UPR is a UN Human Rights Council process in which the human rights records of member states are reviewed by other member countries every five years.

On September 1, Niger's military junta responded to the 265 recommendations made in May by 97 UN member countries and accepted 254 of them, including commitments to strengthen civilian protection and ensure security forces receive training on international human rights and humanitarian law.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The junta however rejected 11 recommendations addressing some of the country's most pressing rights concerns, including to reverse its June decision to start the withdrawal process from the International Criminal Court (ICC). Leaving the ICC risks depriving victims of grave international crimes a last resort to seek justice and remedies.

The junta also rejected calls to release people held arbitrarily, including ousted President Mohamed Bazoum and his wife. The government said their cases fall exclusively under national jurisdiction and denied that anyone is arbitrarily detained. In February 2025, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Bazoum and his wife's detention was arbitrary and called for their immediate release. The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Court of Justice had reached a similar conclusion in December 2023.

Niger also rejected recommendations to repeal the law making consensual same-sex relations a criminal offense and to prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, citing "cultural, social, and religious sensitivities." The rejection is particularly concerning following the junta's adoption of a new penal code in March criminalizing consensual same-sex relations with up to 10 years' imprisonment, contrary to its regional and international human rights obligations.

These rejections come amid a broader crackdown since the military seized power in 2023. Authorities have severely restricted political activity, curtailed media freedom, and targeted civil society activists, journalists and political opponents. The prominent rights defender Moussa Tiangari has been arbitrarily detained since December 2024.

Close 

Niger needs to meaningfully engage with UPR recommendations by fully implementing those it accepted and addressing the serious rights concerns raised in those it rejected.

Ilaria Allegrozzi, Senior Sahel Researcher

World.title: Africa: Africa Urged to Strengthen Budget Oversight
World.content:
African parliaments have been urged to strengthen their oversight of public finances through well-resourced and independent Parliamentary Budget Offices (PBOs) as the continent confronts rising debt vulnerabilities, illicit financial flows, procurement inefficiencies and increasing demands for public services.

Speaker of the National Assembly Saara Kuugongelwa- Amadhila made the call on Mondaywhensheofficiallyopened the 9th Annual Conference of the African Network of Parliamentary Budget Offices (AN-PBOs) in Swakopmund.

Kuugongelwa-Amadhila said African economies were operating in an increasingly complex fiscal environment, with countries facing global economic uncertainty, climate change and concerns over the sustainability of sovereign debt.

She said public debt could be used to support economic growth and prosperity, but warned that unchecked borrowing could become a burden that threatens economic stability and the welfare of future generations.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The effective oversight of public debt and borrowing is therefore not merely a technical financial exercise, but it is a fundamental democratic duty and a profound moral responsibility of the legislature," she said.

The Speaker said parliaments have the cons t i tutional responsibility to scrutinise borrowing decisions, economic policy changes and budget allocations to ensure that they serve the interests of citizens.

She said this responsibility requires more than political will, as lawmakers need access to specialised and independent technical analysis.

The Speaker identified PBOs and Independent Fiscal Institutions as important mechanisms for strengthening legislative oversight.

She said the PBOs provide legislators with independent analysis, fiscal forecasting and technical advice needed to scrutinise executive spending.

Kuugongelwa- Amadhila added that stronger PBOs can help parliaments demand that public spending translates into tangible development outcomes.

She also called for greater citizen participation in budget processes, saying legislative actions should protect and improve the livelihoods of citizens.

While the conference has a continental focus, the Speaker said Namibia was also working to strengthen its own parliamentary oversight capacity.

The Speaker acknowledged that Namibia's Parliament is still at an early stage of establishing a formal PBO.

She said the country was nevertheless committed to establishing its own office and would rely on support from sister parliaments and the AN-PBO network.

"It gives me great pride to reaffirm today the Namibian Parliament's resolute commitment to the establishment of our own parliamentary budget office," she said.

Kuugongelwa-Amadhila said establishing the institution would strengthen Namibia's governance reforms by improving transparency in budget processes, supporting evidence-based fiscal policies and ensuring public resources are used efficiently.

The Speaker said African legislatures have an important role to play in ensuring that national budgets are aligned with the continent's long-term development aspirations under Agenda 2063, which sets out the African Union's vision for "The Africa We Want".

She described the Swakopmund conference as a platform for solidarity, peer learning and South- South technical cooperation among African parliamentary institutions.

Close 

Meanwhile, United Nations Internat ional Chi l d ren's Emergency Fund (UNICEF) urged policymakers to ensure that public resources translate into tangible improvements in the lives of children, particularly those living in poverty, remote communities and vulnerable households.

At the conference, UNICEF Namibia stressed the importance of placing children at the centre of public financial planning and oversight. While Namibia has made important investments in its people, UNICEF said significant disparities and vulnerabilities remain.

It identified children living in poverty, remote communities and households affected by economic, social and climate-related challenges as groups that can face multiple disadvantages.

World.title: Florida real estate sees surge from Washington high earners fleeing new millionaire income tax
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Washington state millionaires are increasingly eyeing Florida real estate to escape a changing tax landscape in the Pacific Northwest, according to a luxury real estate expert.

"I would say that the first thing is taxes. Income tax in Florida is 0%, and in Washington state, it's 9.9% as of January 2028," Margit Brandt, a luxury property specialist, told Fox News Digital.

"Capital gains in Florida is also 0%, and in Washington state, it's 7%. I just think that they've created this really punitive tax environment that's unappealing to the high-net-worth individuals who are the high earners in Washington State, and that's been the biggest kind of feeder for our market here," she added.

Washington's capital gains tax is tiered, with the first $1 million in taxable Washington capital gains subject to a 7% rate and amounts above $1 million subject to a 9.9% rate. Real estate is exempt from the tax.

TRUCKING COMPANY OWNER SUING STATE OVER 'MILLIONAIRES TAX' SAYS POLICY HITS SMALL BUSINESSES

The push comes after the Democratic-controlled Washington Legislature passed, and Gov. Bob Ferguson signed, a 9.9% levy on annual adjusted gross income above the law's $1 million threshold. Set to take effect on Jan. 1, 2028 — with initial returns due in April 2029 — the legislation marks a major change for a state that currently has no individual income tax.

The tax is already facing a court challenge over its constitutionality, while real estate insiders say the new law is influencing some wealthy residents' relocation decisions.

SEATTLE MAYOR SHRUGS OFF MILLIONAIRE-TAX CONCERNS AS 44% OF BUSINESS LEADERS CONSIDER LEAVING

"We've seen actual deals — big deals — happen with high earners from Washington state," Brandt said. "This is not hypothetical. These are closed transactions with people setting up a whole new life here in Florida."

While comprehensive data tracking millionaire migration following the new tax are not yet available, a recent business survey found increased interest among respondents in relocating.

A recent survey released by the Association of Washington Business (AWB) — the state's chamber of commerce and manufacturers association — found that 24% of respondents said they were considering moving their businesses out of Washington. That figure is up from 17% in the previous quarter and nearly triple the rate recorded 16 months ago.

Furthermore, 55% of surveyed business leaders said they are considering moving their personal residence to another state — a number that climbs to 67% in Spokane County, near the low-tax Idaho border.

WHY STARBUCKS PICKED NASHVILLE OVER SEATTLE FOR EXPANSION, ACCORDING TO LOCAL BUSINESS REPORTER

The shift is mirrored in high-profile individual departures. Jesse Proudman, founder and CTO of privacy-focused AI platform Venice.ai, told Fox News Digital in May that he was leaving the Evergreen State, warning that a region once known as a "startup sanctuary" has grown increasingly hostile to business leaders.

Similarly, coffee giant Starbucks announced in April that it would invest $100 million to set up an additional support office in Nashville, Tennessee — a state with no individual income tax — where it expects to have 2,000 support jobs over the next five years. Starbucks said those jobs will include newly created positions, work brought in-house and some teams moved from Seattle.

Beyond balance sheets, Brandt said that safety, culture, and quality of life are primary drivers for wealthy transplants moving to Florida and other states, including Texas and the Carolinas.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"If they're looking at a $10 million house, a $20 million house, a $50 million house, or a $100 million house, it's more than just a house. It's a whole new lifestyle," Brandt said, adding that Florida’s lack of a state estate tax and its proximity to the Caribbean appeal heavily to multi-generational wealth. "They want safety, security, good schools, and to set up their financial future. Florida is just such an easy landing place, and I think we're going to see way more of it in the coming years."

Fox News Digital reached out for comment to Senator Patty Murray, D-Wash, Senator Maria Cantwell, D-Wash, as well as Washington state’s governor, Bob Ferguson.

Fox News Digital also reached out to State Sen. Jamie Pedersen (D-Seattle), the architect of the millionaire's tax bill, for comment. Fox News Digital also reached out to Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson.

World.title: Record WNBA viewership proves the league's drama is driving fans to screens, not away from them | Matt Calkins
World.content:
You're bored, and you want to convince your WNBA-loving friend that the league is a disaster. So you put together a list.

You write down how the league's most popular player, Caitlin Clark, had her throat pushed in by Alyssa Thomas, but needed NBA Commissioner Adam Silver to step in and get Thomas suspended. You add how Caitlin is constantly left out of marketing campaigns, and was voted the 11th best guard in the WNBA by her peers.

You throw in how the league's leaders still can't define what a woman is despite having a meeting on the subject. You jot down that teams regularly ban media (see: OutKick) they suspect will ask unflattering questions. You conclude with commissioner Cathy Engelbert once dismissing a fair question about her future by saying "I wonder whether you would ask that of a man," then note that she will retire after 2026.

CAITLIN CLARK HELPS FEVER DELIVER WNBA'S LARGEST REGULAR-SEASON TV AUDIENCE IN 29 YEARS

You give the list to your buddy. He just smiles.

Check the TV ratings and attendance figures, he says.

Shoot. He might just have you.

Folks can complain about the WNBA being a circus all they want, but circuses tend to draw a lot of people into the tent. One could argue that the league has done a number on its reputation, but you can't argue with the number of eyeballs watching its teams.

The WNBA averaged a record 1.37 million viewers across the ESPN networks during this regular season, which marked a 17% increase from last year. NBC and CBS also averaged at least one million viewers for their WNBA packages in 2026.

And it's not just the broadcasts luring in fans. The league drew a record 3.79 million live attendees across 330 games, which is a 20.5% increase from last season. Yes, the two expansion teams inflated these numbers, but the average WNBA attendance of 11,474 was still a 5% increase from last regular season.

How much of this is cash cow Caitlin Clark being healthy after missing most of last season?

That certainly helps, but this goes beyond CC. Games not involving the Fever averaged 984,000 viewers this regular season — up 24% from last year.

You can't tell me that isn't significant. You can't look at those numbers and say the WNBA is self-destructing.

Perhaps one could argue that viewership and attendance would be even higher if smarter leadership kept the controversies at bay. But maybe, just maybe — the controversies are what's behind this boost.

WILL THE WNBA’S UNSERIOUS, WEEKLY SITCOM DESTROY ONE OF THE GREATEST OPPORTUNITIES FOR WOMEN ATHLETES?

As much as tradition and physical excellence drive sports viewership, drama is every bit as crucial. And whether it's the players' contempt for Clark, Sophie Cunningham's pointing meme, or the league's genuflection to trans activists —theater has the WNBA in the news every day.

I once described it as half basketball, half WWE. My dad corrected me on that — it's half basketball, half Real Housewives of Hoop.

When Clark barks at refs, or yells at White, or gets chewed out by Fever assistant coach Briann January — we don't turn away. Fans condemn players such as Thomas or Chennedy Carter or Mabrey for malicious fouls on Caitlin, but they don't skip the next game.

Natasha Cloud losing her mind on Enes Kanter for wearing a shirt with the definition of a woman on it? Absurd. But it was a talker for a good week. Coach after coach giving pro trans answers when asked about the separation of biological men and women? Predictable, but incessantly newsworthy. The maligning of Fever supporters as racist middle Americans invading the league? Infuriating. But while fans roll their eyes one second, they glue them to the TV the next.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I'll admit I'm as guilty as anyone. In addition to everything above, the WNBA's cowardice in banning media makes me want to stage a personal boycott. And yet, when the Fever start their playoff series against the Aces Sunday, I'll be as invested in that as any NFL game.

There's a lot of talk about how the actions of players, coaches and leaders prevent the WNBA from being taken seriously. But part of me wonders if most of them even care about being taken seriously.

They have their money. They have their eyeballs. They have their culture. Respect from the everyman may be immaterial to them.
