World.title: Belize renews call at UN for end to US embargo on Cuba and removal from terrorism list
World.content:
Belize renews call at UN for end to US embargo on Cuba and removal from terrorism list

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Belize has renewed its call for the lifting of United States sanctions against Cuba and for Havana to be removed from Washington’s list of state sponsors of terrorism.

Prime Minister John Briceño made the appeal during Belize’s address to the United Nations General Assembly on Saturday.

“Belize also stands with Cuba,” Briceño said, arguing that the economic embargo and restrictions affecting fuel supplies have severely damaged the Cuban economy.

He described the situation as “unnecessary and unjustified” and renewed Belize’s call for an end to the embargo and Cuba’s removal from the terrorism designation.

Belize and other CARICOM governments have repeatedly opposed the US embargo and Cuba’s inclusion on the list.

A United Nations report has previously documented statements from Belize, other Caribbean governments and regional organizations calling for Cuba’s removal from the designation.

The United States maintains sanctions and restrictions on Cuba based on its own national-security and foreign-policy assessments. In January 2026, the White House issued a new executive order alleging that the Cuban government posed an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to US national security and foreign policy, citing Havana’s relations with Russia, China, Iran and other actors.

Belize and Cuba maintain longstanding diplomatic and development ties, particularly in health and education.

World.title: Showers and thunderstorms expected across Belize before conditions improve tonight
World.content:
Showers and thunderstorms expected across Belize before conditions improve tonight

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans can expect another round of showers and thunderstorms today, although weather conditions are forecast to improve heading into the evening.

The National Meteorological Service says somewhat moist and relatively unstable conditions continue across the country this morning.

Skies will be sunny with cloudy spells today, with a few showers or thunderstorms developing around Belize during the morning.

By this afternoon, most of the activity is expected to shift inland.

Rainfall and thunderstorm activity should decrease and become isolated by evening before showers begin developing again mainly over southern Belize late tonight.

Temperatures will reach around 89 degrees Fahrenheit along the coast, 94 degrees inland and 81 degrees in the hills.

Winds will blow from the east to southeast at 5 to 15 knots, with waves between one and four feet.

Sunday is expected to be mainly fair with isolated showers or thunderstorms, although southern Belize could experience a few more.

Meanwhile, Tropical Depression Fay and Tropical Storm Gonzalo remain over the Atlantic. Forecasters say neither system poses a threat to Belize.

World.title: International News: Haiti PM calls for shift from aid to investment to achieve lasting peace
World.content:
International News: Haiti PM calls for shift from aid to investment to achieve lasting peace

By Zoila Palma: Haiti’s Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé has called for a fundamental shift in the international community’s approach to Haiti, urging partners to move “from aid to investment, from assistance to production and from dependency to partnership” as the country works to restore security, stability and economic recovery.

Addressing the General Debate of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly this week, Fils-Aimé said Haiti needs greater and fairer access to capital, markets and technology. “No people should have to choose between responding to an emergency and financing its development,” he said.

The Haitian Prime Minister acknowledged that emergency assistance has saved lives, but stressed that the country’s long-term development cannot remain indefinitely dependent on aid and charity. He also argued that security measures alone cannot create lasting peace, calling for resources mobilized during the crisis to be transformed into investments that generate jobs and sustainable opportunities.

Fils-Aimé placed particular emphasis on young people and women, while calling for stronger national institutions, expanded economic opportunities and support for credible elections. He said these measures are necessary to help Haiti break cycles of violence, political transition and dependency.

For Fils-Aimé, lasting peace must extend beyond simply ending violence.

He said peace should be reflected in construction sites reopening, markets becoming active, businesses growing, young people finding work, children playing safely and communities returning to a normal rhythm of daily life.

World.title: PM Briceño calls for heightened United Nations and OAS monitoring following Guatemalan military aircraft incursion
World.content:
PM Briceño calls for heightened United Nations and OAS monitoring following Guatemalan military aircraft incursion

By Zoila Palma: Today, Prime Minister John Briceño informed the United Nations General Assembly of a “serious breach of international law” after a Guatemalan military aircraft entered Belize’s sovereign airspace on September 24, 2026.

In his address, Briceño said the aircraft intentionally disabled its transponder and argued that the incident violated international aviation and sovereignty principles.

“Belize has chosen, and will always choose, law over force,” Briceño told the Assembly. He said the alleged incursion violated the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation, customary norms governing state aircraft and the principle of territorial sovereignty protected under the United Nations Charter.

Briceño also told the UN that the aircraft incident was “not an isolated event,” and said it was a continuing pattern involving Guatemalan state vessels and personnel operating in Belizean territorial waters of the Sarstoon River.

He noted that the territorial dispute between Belize and Guatemala is currently before the International Court of Justice, with hearings scheduled for February 2027.

Briceño called on Guatemala to immediately cease incursions by air, land and sea and to comply with its obligations under the UN Charter, the Chicago Convention and the OAS Confidence-Building Measures. The OAS maintains a mission in the Belize-Guatemala process that conducts incident verification and supports confidence-building and peaceful settlement efforts.

The PM also requested heightened monitoring by both the United Nations and the Organization of American States, saying this was necessary “to ensure that no Member State uses military force or intimidation to influence judicial proceedings.”

World.title: Briceño condemns Netanyahu at UN, calls for end to Gaza war and occupation of Palestine
World.content:
Briceño condemns Netanyahu at UN, calls for end to Gaza war and occupation of Palestine

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño delivered a blistering condemnation of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel’s actions in Gaza during Belize’s address to the United Nations General Assembly on Saturday, calling for an end to what he described as genocide, apartheid and the occupation of Palestine.

Briceño questioned how the General Assembly could be expected to listen to Netanyahu defend Israel’s actions while the Israeli leader remains wanted by the International Criminal Court.

“It is an affront to this Assembly and to humanity to be forced to listen to a man justify apartheid and genocide when he is wanted by the International Criminal Court for war crimes and crimes against humanity,” Briceño said.

Briceño also accused the international community of decades of failure to secure Palestinian self-determination and described Israel as a “settler colonial state.”

“The genocide must end. The apartheid must stop. End the occupation and decolonize Palestine,” Briceño declared.

Netanyahu has been subject to an ICC arrest warrant since November 2024. The Court said there were reasonable grounds to believe that Netanyahu bears criminal responsibility for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, including starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution and other inhumane acts. An arrest warrant is not a conviction, and Netanyahu and the Israeli government have rejected the allegations and challenged the ICC’s jurisdiction.

A United Nations Commission of Inquiry has separately concluded that Israeli authorities committed genocidal acts in Gaza. Israel has rejected accusations of genocide and maintains that its military campaign targets Hamas rather than the Palestinian population.

Briceño said Belize’s position formed part of a broader commitment to the protection of civilians, accountability and respect for international law in conflicts around the world.

World.title: Belize informs UN of “breach of International Law” following Guatemalan military aircraft incursion
World.content:
Belize informs UN of “breach of International Law” following Guatemalan military aircraft incursion

By Zoila Palma: Today, Prime Minister John Briceno addressed the United Nations at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

PM Briceno informed the UN of a “breach of international law” by Guatemala following a military aircraft incursion into Belizean airspace on September 24, 2026.

“Belize has chosen, and will always choose, law over force. Belize informs this Assembly of a serious breach of international law committed on the night of 24 September 2026, when a Guatemalan military aircraft entered Belize’s sovereign airspace and intentionally disabled its transponder. This act violates the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation, customary norms governing state aircraft, and the inviolability of territorial sovereignty protected under Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter.

This incursion is not an isolated event,” the Prime Minister explained.

PM Briceno added that this is a pattern “in which Guatemalan state vessels and personnel operate unlawfully in Belizean territorial waters of the Sarstoon River, which forms part of Belize’s border with Guatemala, in defiance of obligations—binding on both Parties—to refrain from any action capable of aggravating or extending the dispute presently before the International Court of Justice.”

In addition, PM Briceno called on Guatemala to “immediately cease all incursions by air, land, or sea; to comply fully with its obligations under the UN Charter, the Chicago Convention, and the OAS Confidence-Building Measures; and to respect the integrity of the ICJ process.”

The Prime Minister further requests heightened monitoring by the United Nations and the OAS to ensure that no Member State uses military force or intimidation to influence judicial proceedings.

“We await the Court’s judgments with confidence, and we look forward to borders that are respected by all,” PM Briceno expressed.

World.title: The Belize Bank announces winners of Priceless Experience Promotion with trips to Orlando, New York
World.content:
The Belize Bank announces winners of Priceless Experience Promotion with trips to Orlando, New York

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Bank has announced two winners of its “Priceless Experience” promotion, with one cardholder winning a trip to Orlando and another securing a trip to New York.

Neri Monzon was named the winner of the Debit Card Priceless Experience – Orlando Trip, while Allen A. Mendez won the Credit Card Priceless Experience – New York Trip.

The Belize Bank Limited noted that the winners will travel from Belize to enjoy memorable experiences in Orlando and New York, with the promotion highlighting the benefits and experiences available to Belize Bank cardholders.

The bank thanked everyone who participated in the promotion and encouraged customers to continue using their Belize Bank cards, noting that their “next Priceless Experience could be just a swipe away.”

World.title: PM Briceño tells UN Guatemala military aircraft violated Belize’s sovereignty; calls for international monitoring
World.content:
PM Briceño tells UN Guatemala military aircraft violated Belize’s sovereignty; calls for international monitoring

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño used Belize’s address to the United Nations General Assembly on Saturday to formally denounce Guatemala’s recent military aircraft incursion into Belizean airspace, telling world leaders that the incident constituted a breach of international law.

Briceño informed the General Assembly that a Guatemalan military aircraft entered Belize’s sovereign airspace in September and intentionally disabled its transponder. He argued that the action violated international aviation rules and Belize’s territorial sovereignty.

“This incursion is not an isolated one,” Briceño said, linking the incident to what he described as a continuing pattern of Guatemalan state vessels and personnel operating unlawfully in Belizean waters in the Sarstoon River area.

Belizean defence officials said Friday that Guatemalan Army aircraft FAG706 entered Belizean airspace at approximately 7:29 p.m. on September 24, circled in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef and remained inside Belizean airspace for roughly one hour and 10 minutes before exiting in the south. Officials also said the aircraft’s transponder was turned off during part of the flight.

Guatemala’s Ministry of National Defence subsequently issued a statement saying its military operations are conducted in accordance with national and international law, but the statement did not explain the aircraft’s purpose over Belizean territory.

At the UN, Briceño called on Guatemala to immediately cease incursions “by air, land or sea” and requested heightened monitoring by the United Nations and Organization of American States while the Belize-Guatemala territorial dispute remains before the International Court of Justice.

He said Belize would continue to choose “law over force” and would await the ICJ’s judgment with confidence.

CARICOM has also previously expressed concern over tensions in the Sarstoon and has called on Belize and Guatemala to avoid actions that could aggravate the dispute while the matter remains before the ICJ.

World.title: ‘You must die!’
World.content:
Late pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries Kevin Smith

A police sergeant testified on Friday that he opened gunfire on a knife-wielding male attacker at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, after the man, who hurled death threats, refused to comply with law enforcers’ orders to drop his weapon.

The cop, who was the fourth witness in the murder trial of Andre Ruddock at the Home Circuit Court in downtown Kingston, said that the knife-wielding man was rushing from the church towards the police and using threatening language.

Ruddock is being tried in relation to the October 17, 2021 killing of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner, whose throat was cut, allegedly by the accused, at the church in what has been described as a human sacrifice ritual. Ruddock was said to have been acting on the instructions of the pastor of the church, Kevin Smith.

Smith died a few days later in a motor vehicle crash in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to be charged in relation to the incident.

On Thursday, another member of the constabulary testified that Smith had instructed members of the church to kill the police if they gained access to the compound.

On Friday, the second police witness told the court that he and members of his team were attacked by the male member of the church and because he feared for his life, he was forced to discharge multiple rounds into the upper body of the attacker. His colleague also fired at the man.

The witness said that the members of the police team did not enter the church compound via the gate at the front, but had to skilfully scale a wall, topped with barbed wire, at the back of the premises to gain access. The policeman said that it was while the members of the team were going over the wall, one after the other, that the man with the knife rushed to them.

“I was in the process of assisting members of the team to get past the barbed wires. He spoke to me, and I turned around and looked in the direction of the church.

“I looked to the left of a boardwalk where I saw a man of dark complexion, slim build, about 5 feet 7 inches in height. He was dressed in a red shirt and a pair of white and grey trousers. I saw this man with what appeared to be a silver-looking knife in his right hand and this man seemed to be disturbed by the presence of the police on the church compound,” the cop shared.

He said that the man was looking in the direction of the police who were coming over the wall and was pointing the knife furiously at them.

“It was as if he was trying to say something. He was agitated, moving from one side to the other. At the time when I saw this man, I did not see anyone else. I shouted out to the man, saying, ‘Police! Put down the knife!’ He did not put the knife down. The man then started to run towards me and shouted, ‘You must die!’ repeatedly,” the cop said.

He told the court that when he first shouted to the man, he was about 33 metres away from the him. The policeman said he made numerous attempts to get the man to stop advancing towards him.

“He did not obey the command. He continued to advance towards me with the knife and on reaching about three meters away, he put his right hand in the air with the knife in a stabbing position. I moved two steps backwards and then to the right. I then pointed my M16 rifle to the chest area of the man and I discharged three rounds because I was fearful for my life and the life of my colleagues who were beside me. I also heard loud explosions to my right. A constable was positioned to my right and the loud explosions sounded like gunshots. It came from the constable’s rifle. The man [the attacker] fell to the ground,” the witness testified.

He further said that following the shooting, all seven members of his team had got over the wall, through the barbed wire, after which the knife was removed from the man’s palm.

“We tried to assist him to the hospital but the front gate was locked and the service vehicle could not enter the premises. I saw a few people on the verandah section of the church and they went inside of the church. I then contacted the police emergency communications centre and I informed the monitor at the Area One control centre about the incident. I also requested from the monitor additional personnel to come to the scene,” he said.

The cop told the court that he then instructed two of his team members to cover the rear of the building and another set was sent to monitor the front.

“I, along with one member, went to the top of the church building to also give coverage. I walked towards the front of the building where I could see the gate and the roadway. I could see persons on the inside of the church premises. I saw someone close to the front gate, kneeling behind a column, covered with a white sheet and it seemed as if this person was hiding,” he said.

“Whilst on the top of the building I went to the right and I saw someone motionless lying face down and covered with white cloth. I also saw what appeared to be blood leaking from the neck area to the head. I saw more police arriving on the scene, as well as members of the Jamaica Defence Force. I shouted out to them and told them not to climb over the gate because I did not know if that person who was kneeling was armed,” he said, explaining that instructions were given to them on how to safely enter the compound.

World.title: ‘I have to balance the scale’
World.content:
Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Delroy Chuck (centre), in discussion with president of the Jamaican Bar Association Tenneshia Watkins (right), and executive member Jacqueline Cummings following Thursday’s meeting with defence attorneys regarding their concerns over the Firearms Act. (Photo: Ministry of Justice)

JUSTICE Minister Delroy Chuck on Friday continued pushing back at critics who say the Firearms Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation Act, 2022 is too harsh on the accused and needs to be amended, arguing that he has to “balance the scale”.

Speaking at the ministry’s Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) policy development and estate planning forum at Sandals Dunn’s River in St Ann, Chuck charged that he cannot only take into consideration the expectations of the accused but those of the victims as well.

“That is why I say, when I met with the Bar Association yesterday [Thursday] I told them, ‘Yes, we will look at those exceptional cases — we will look at imitation firearms, we will look at where the gun was not in play when it was found.’ But what about those cases where a man is caught having fired, having robbed, having raped? You think it is easy for a woman who has to surrender herself because a gun is at her head?” he said.

On Thursday Chuck called an emergency meeting with lawyers following a silent protest staged by defence attorneys outside the Supreme Court in downtown Kingston on Wednesday.

During the protest, attorneys called for a review of the mandatory sentencing provisions of the Act and and its impact on “justice, due process, and the rule of law”. They demanded that their concerns be taken on board for reform.

The demonstration follows mounting concerns within sections of the legal profession over the Act’s mandatory minimum sentencing provisions, particularly the restriction they place on judicial discretion.

However, Chuck argued on Friday that he has no doubt the judges have discretion and can always apply 15 years instead of 30, but maintained that offenders should be treated with the strongest possible penalty.

“Over the past couple weeks, including yesterday [Thursday], we’ve had to deal with this Firearms Act. The lawyers feel that the law is too harsh on gunmen and we must give the court more discretion, but those gunmen don’t deserve less than 30 years. Not 15 years. They should spend a long time in prison,” Chuck argued.

According to the defence attorneys, Thursday’s meeting failed to produce any meaningful plans to reform the Act, and as such attorneys have placed on alert to pull their services from the island’s courts for an entire week, starting next Monday — a move that will deal a significant blow to the Michaelmas Term which began just over a week ago.

Underscoring that since the passing of the legislation, less gun cases are going to the court, Chuck doubled down on his comments made on Sunday, September 13, 2026 at the annual Assize Service of the judiciary that the Act has resulted in the current reduction in crime.

According to Chuck, while the mandatory minimum sentences contained in the provision were being reviewed because of widespread concerns, “the security forces and a number of my colleagues feel that the Act is working and it is bringing down murders and shootings”.

On Friday, Chuck maintained he is confident the work of the police over the last few years is due to the fact that they not only have resources, but are supported by the the Firearms Act.

“We came into office with the murder rate climbing, and we decided that we need a new Firearms Act to deal with the guns and gangs within our country, and it took almost seven years before we were able to put in place the Firearms Act 2022,” he said.

“When you argue with the lawyers and say, ‘From 2022 I’ve quoted the reduction,’ they say, ‘But there’s no causation, there’s no correlation,’ [but] there’s coincidence though. And once there’s coincidence, and murders are going down, let murders go down some more. Let the coincidence continue,” Chuck said, adding that he advised lawyers that a law which has proven to be effective cannot be changed at present.

“There’s no doubt in my mind that the police feel morally justified and inspired to go and search for guns and capture gunmen because they know that when they do, and they take them to court, an appropriate penalty can be imposed. How do you think a police officer who finds a man, lock him up, take him to court, and the court pat him on the back and say, ‘You sound like you can be rehabilitated will feel?’ ” Chuck asked.

World.title: ‘Not a confrontation between lawyers and the State’
World.content:
President of the Advocates Association of Jamaica Tamika Harris (second right) shares her perspective during Thursday’s discussion with Justice Minister Delroy Chuck and the defence Bar over concerns relating to the Firearms Act. Also photographed are Sasha Kay Shaw (right); Tenneshia Watkins (third right); Jacqueline Cumming, King’s Counsel (second left); and Christopher Townsend. Photo: Ministry of Justice

Advocates’ Association of Jamaica President Tamika Harris on Friday rallied colleague attorneys to “remain resolute” ahead of next week’s planned withdrawal from courtrooms islandwide to press for changes to the 2022 Firearms Act while insisting that their protest “is not a confrontation between lawyers and the State”.

The week-long strike, which Harris on Friday confirmed will begin in earnest on Monday, September 28, comes after last Wednesday’s ‘silent protest’ outside the Supreme Court on King Street in downtown Kingston which was followed by an emergency meeting Thursday with Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs Delroy Chuck.

During that protest, placard-bearing members of the Jamaican Bar Association and the Advocates Association, in collaboration with Bar associations across the island, demanded that their concerns about the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022 and its impact on “justice, due process and the rule of law” be taken on board for reform.

After the meeting with Chuck failed to produce any commitments from the Government, Harris, in a statement issued Friday, stated, “A meeting is not an amendment. Engagement without a timeline is not reform. Discussion without action does not change the law. It is now September. The legislation remains unchanged. The consequences continue. We must not falter. I urge my colleagues to remain resolute. Momentum must not fade.”

Pointing to recent commentary by the prime minister, the national security minister and Minister Chuck which, she argued, demonstrated awareness that the provision needs to be amended, Harris said, “This is not a confrontation between lawyers and the State. The Government itself has acknowledged that amendments are needed. Minister Chang said there are things we have to change. Minister Chuck has confirmed that mandatory minimums are under review. There is substantial common ground. What is required now is urgency, a clear timeline, and action.

“Our call is for meaningful judicial discretion, proper recognition of early guilty pleas, a workable plea negotiation system [and] a mechanism to prevent injustice in exceptional cases. These objectives do not weaken public safety. They strengthen justice,” the Advocates’ Association of Jamaica president stated.

She emphasised that the stance of the attorneys should not be seen as support for criminals.

“Illegal firearms have caused immeasurable harm in Jamaica. Those who use guns to kill, rob, terrorise and intimidate must face serious consequences. Our call for reform must never be misrepresented as a call for weak gun laws. We are asking for a sentencing system that remains firm against serious firearm offending while allowing judges to distinguish between offenders, offences, and circumstances,” Harris declared.

The Act, which prescribes a mandatory 15-year sentence for specified violations, took effect in November 2022 and, among other things, provides penalties ranging from 15 years to life imprisonment for possession of illegal weapons. It establishes a dual regime — distinguishing between prohibited weapons or unregulated firearms and connected activities, and firearms that are duly authorised or registered.

Harris said Wednesday’s protest was not frivolous.

“Our protest was not undertaken lightly. For years the legal profession has raised concerns. In April, the Government indicated amendments were coming ‘in short order’. Yet months have passed. Those of us who practise in the criminal courts see the consequences daily. This is not theory, it is reality affecting real cases, real people, and the proper administration of justice. Further discussion alone was no longer sufficient,” Harris maintained.

“The Advocates Association of Jamaica is calling for urgent amendments to the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022. Our position is simple and should unite all Jamaicans: We need strong gun laws, but strong laws must also be fair laws… judicial discretion does not mean leniency, it means allowing judges to consider the offence, the offender, aggravating and mitigating factors, and the interests of justice. We are not asking for the abandonment of serious penalties. We are asking that judges be permitted to judge,” she stated.

World.title: Malie Donn, Merkz and top DJs to get SOAK’D at UWI
World.content:
Malie Donn

Aside from water and foam, patrons are in for a musical treat at this Saturday’s staging of SOAK’D, dubbed the ultimate water fete.

Set for UWI Mona Bowl on the campus of The University of the West Indies, it is hosted and promoted by Fabian “Fyahman” Morris, a recent law degree graduate, as part of his birthday celebration.

Since its 2023 inception it has grown into one of the most recognisable events held each year.

“Patrons can expect a full, high-energy experience built around music, water, foam, entertainment, and nonstop vibes. SOAK’D is more than just a party; it is an immersive experience where the crowd becomes part of the action… UWI Mona Bowl [gives] us more space to enhance production, water features, bar, activation and the overall atmosphere. We want people to come ready to get wet, have fun, and experience SOAK’D at another level,” Fyahman told the Jamaica Observer on Wednesday.

He is excited about the entertainment package, which will feature two of dancehall’s hottest names, the high-riding Van Cleef deejay Malie Donn and Merkz.

“The DJ and selector line-up is also packed, featuring the recent Caribbean Music Award winning DJ, Ricky Platinum, JJ Deadlock, DJ Spectre from Code Red, Zess from ZIP 103FM, Jubba Dem, DJ Deva Kidd, Selecta JB, DJ Rann, DJ Zacky, and others,” said Fyahman, who will also put on his DJ hat as he teams with Kryptic to blaze a musical inferno.

“Patrons can expect a mixture of dancehall, soca, hip hop, and the biggest party records, with the line-up designed to keep the energy building throughout the night,” he continued.

Fyahman spoke about the event’s growth of the past three stagings.

“The growth has been tremendous… but from the very beginning we saw the potential for it to become something much bigger. Over the years, the event has expanded in terms of production, attendance, partnerships, entertainment, and overall brand recognition. We have worked alongside major entertainment brands, including Yardmas Carnival, and the event has hosted several notable names within Jamaican entertainment. In 2025 SOAK’D incorporated a joint birthday celebration with Skippa, and in March 2026 we hosted Skeng and Showtime Services, with other major names including Jamal and Spice being part of that staging.” said Fyahman.

“Now the focus is on continuing that evolution. We are bringing in bigger entertainment packages, improving production and creating stronger brand partnerships while still maintaining what made SOAK’D special from the beginning: Great music, water, energy and an atmosphere where everybody comes to have a good time. This staging feels like another major step forward for the brand, and we’re excited for patrons to see what we’ve put together,” he explained.

World.title: Man accused of offering cop $2,000 ‘lunch money’ fined $30,000
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — A man who accused of offering a policeman $2,000 as “lunch money” after being stopped for a traffic violation was fined $30,000 for bribery in the St James Parish Court.

Pladger Magnus appeared before Judge Natiesha Fairclough-Hylton on Wednesday and was represented by attorney Kevon Johnson.

The court heard that on July 10, the arresting cop was conducting traffic duties along Rosehall Main Road when he stopped Magnus after observing that the fog lamps on his motor vehicle were on during the day.

The policeman informed Magnus that he would be issuing him a ticket, and the accused man allegedly responded, “Officer, give me a bly. Officer, you can’t give me a chance? Are you hungry? You want a lunch money?”

Magnus then reportedly walked back to his motor vehicle and returned, handing the cop his vehicle documents and $2,000.

When the policeman asked him what the money was for, Magnus allegedly said, “Buy a lunch with it because mi can’t afford that ticket.”

Magnus was subsequently arrested and charged. When cautioned, he allegedly responded, “Arrested fi wah?”

Johnson, in addressing the court on behalf of his client, stated, “The circumstances and my instructions are slightly different as to how this unfolded. We are not denying that the monies were handed, but my understanding from instructions is that on the pull-over he did ask for a chance.”

Johnson said, however, that Magnus would not have asked the policeman if he was hungry.

“What happened after was that the officer said he gave three blies already and he doesn’t give blies like that and my client assumed certain things,” he said.

Johnson added that he was opposing the allegation that Magnus had instigated the exchange, simply put the money there and handed it over, thinking he could just get away with it.

The attorney asked the court to be as lenient as possible, noting that it was his client’s first appearance before the judge and that he had not wasted the court’s time. He also asked the court to offer whatever discount it deemed appropriate in the circumstances.

Fairclough-Hylton subsequently fined Magnus $30,000 or 10 days’ imprisonment.

World.title: Samuda sounds alarm on climate financing shortfall
World.content:
Minister of Water, Environment and Climate Change Matthew Samuda speaking Tuesday at the United Nations’ Solutions Dialogue on Financing Adaptation in the Era of Overshoot in New York.

AS small island developing states, including Jamaica, bear the financial and environmental brunt of worsening weather conditions, Minister of Water, Environment and Climate Change Matthew Samuda has called for greater international financing for climate adaptation.

Speaking Tuesday at the United Nations’ Solutions Dialogue on Financing Adaptation in the Era of Overshoot, hosted in New York, Samuda argued that current global funds do not meet the scale of the threat faced by vulnerable countries.

He pointed out that the World Bank’s assessment is that Jamaica needs about US$5-billion to strengthen its water sector alone, against climate and development challenges.

The minister noted that in the last five years, Jamaica experienced four of its five worst droughts, and its hottest and wettest days on record, and the island’s western parishes were battered by Hurricane Melissa last October — the strongest storm to hit the country in history.

Additionally, Samuda pointed out that the onset of the El Niño climate phenomenon has contributed to worsening drought and heat conditions affecting the island.

Samuda argued that these extreme disruptions are undeniable proof of global climate overshoot and argued that developing countries lacked the funding required to fortify their resources against the environmental crisis.

“In the case of Hurricane Melissa last year, it was US$12.2 billion, 56 per cent of [Jamaica’s] GDP [gross domestic product]. When one compares that to something like Hurricane Katrina (2005), which was one per cent of US [United States of America] GDP, then you understand that the impact of overshoot affects us disproportionately, and that is of course a concern in the entire developing world,” said Samuda.

According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), climate overshoot occurs when global temperatures temporarily go past the Paris Agreement’s international goal of 1.5°C of warming, staying hot for several decades before potentially falling below it.

However, scientists warn that prolonged warming above that level could result in melting polar ice sheets, irreversible biodiversity loss and other long-term changes.

Currently, UNEP predicts that the Earth is on a trajectory to cross 1.5°C global warming within the next few years, with its report putting the best case scenario at 1.8°C; while other sources suggest a peak at 2°C.

“Now, adaptation is critical, because without…the right adaptation funds being allocated and deployed in the best way possible, you’re going to have a greater need for capitalisation of the Loss and Damage Fund. That is the reality. We can’t function with a fund that doesn’t have funds, so it already needs to be capitalised,” argued Samuda.

“The adaptation funds available to the developing world simply don’t scratch the surface. Then we have the issue of whether or not we’re deploying them as efficiently and as quickly as we absolutely need to, because every dollar not deployed, staying in a bank account not going into wider drains, better coastal development, [and] stronger housing infrastructure, will contribute to greater losses and loss of life,” he said.

While the water minister extended his gratitude to the Green Climate Fund (GCF), which recently approved a US$50-million investment to advance resilient agricultural practices in Jamaica, he noted that funding was still severely lacking.

He added that Jamaica has developed its Systemic Risk Assessment Tool, and is in the process of finalising its national adaptation plan but these strategies will require increased investments.

From a political perspective, Samuda maintained that a greater effort must be made to get other agencies to value resilience, pointing out that they have the capacity to action change by investing in adaptation-related financing.

“We simply need the political will to finance adaptation. That is a core of the issue, because we don’t need to be overly creative, the industries that will be affected, certainly the general insurance industry, has the capacity to significantly increase… [and] has the capacity to invest in adaptation-related financing,” he said.

“Another industry that creates collectible opportunities, it’s calculable and collectible, because of IATA (International Air Transport Association), is certainly the airline industry. There were five billion passenger trips last year. Certainly a dollar per passenger trip would not trigger global inflation. So the issue is an issue of political will,” charged Samuda.

World.title: CYCLE OF DOMINANCE
World.content:
From left: Oblique Seville of Jamaica, Kenneth Bednarek of the United States, and Kishane Thompson of Jamaica compete in the men’s 100m final during the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo, Japan, on September 14, 2025. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

RETIRED Jamaican-born 100m Olympic Games and World Champion Donovan Bailey remains confident in Jamaica’s sprint future, despite America’s recent dominance, but believes some local athletes will face some tough career decisions in the years ahead.

His comments come after the recently concluded World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest where Americans Melissa Jefferson-Wooden and Kenny Bednarek won the women’s and men’s sprint doubles, respectively.

It continued the USA’s impressive run in the sprints, with Jefferson-Wooden completing the 100m and 200m double at the Tokyo Championships last year, along with Noah Lyles who won the men’s 200m.

Four Americans, including Sha’Carri Richardson and Gabby Thomas, have now accounted for eight of the last 12 100m and 200m titles at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest, the 2024 Paris Olympics, and the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo.

Bailey, who won Olympic and World Championship gold for Canada in 1996 and 1995 respectively, believes the prospect of the 2028 Olympics on home soil is providing extra motivation for the American sprinters.

“There are cycles that happen all the time. Canadians, we had our own for a while; we dominated the Americans and then the Americans came back and they dominated. Then the Jamaicans came and just put the boots to them for such a long time. And right now the Americans are on an up cycle,” he said on Leighton Levy’s Mr. Analyst.

“[Year] 2028 is the LA Olympics. The last time the US hosted the Games was in 1996 so they are building towards [2028]. They’ve got some incredible young athletes, like Kenny and Melissa, but the Americans hate to not have two titles — heavyweight champion of the world and world’s fastest human beings. So, they are incredibly focused right now to make sure that 1996 never happens in 2028 in Los Angeles and so they are uber-focused now on making sure that these athletes are prepared.”

However, former 100m world record holder Bailey says Jamaica shouldn’t be overly concerned with the USA’s recent success.

Jamaica’s sprint star Oblique Seville broke America’s six-year World Championship streak across both sprints last year in Tokyo by winning the 100m. Kishane Thompson has also won consecutive silver medals at the 2024 Paris Games and the 2025 Tokyo Championships.

Shericka Jackson, Tina Clayton and Bryan Levell have also made the podium over the past three major championships.

Bailey, though, believes there needs to be a collective effort to maintain Jamaica’s successful sprint culture following the passing of legendary track coach, Stephen Francis.

“[Jamaica] has some really excellent veterans, some extremely talented young kids, and then you have others that are right on the cusp to making it to this level,” he said.

“I think that the consistency of the Jamaicans is going to continue. The loss of ‘Franno’ is a huge void, so I think that it’s probably a time where [the] politics of sport needs to be thrown out the window. Jamaica needs to be on top again, and for that, everyone’s got to come together.”

Bailey, though, says some athletes may need to look for training opportunities overseas to ensure they reach their full potential.

“I think that Glen [Mills] and Stephen proved that you can stay in Jamaica and become the very best on the planet, right, but as a business you have to look at all the options available to you. If there’s a coach that’s based somewhere else and that coach will invite you to his camp or you can negotiate a great deal where you can go and train with that coach, then you should,” he said.

“There are small, tiny windows in an athlete’s career where you can do significant things, where your body is healthy and your body is at its best. Whatever the window is for anybody — whether or not you’ve been to the podium, been to the top of the podium or not at some point — father time wins at some point.”

He added, “World Championships is next year, and then a year from that is the 2028 Olympics. So I think that, depending on who you are, where you’re going, what you can afford and your sponsorship and [so on], you have to go to a place where you’re going to get the very best right now to produce for right now.”

“If there’s a coach or coaching environment that’s based somewhere else other than Jamaica, go find it. But if you can get great coaching in a great environment that’s going to allow you to flourish and become really good or the best at what you do, and you can do that at home, then absolutely do that.”

The 2027 World Athletics Championships takes place in Beijing next September, with Jamaica’s trials set for June.

World.title: JWN Foundation scholars urged to build brands with purpose
World.content:
Former JWN Foundation scholar Rickardo Anderson during his “bro talk” break-out rap session with the male scholarship recipients. Photos: Mohic Ferguson

RECIPIENTS of the 2026 JWN Foundation Tertiary Scholarship have been challenged to think deliberately about the image they present, how they communicate and the story their personal brand tells about them.

The advice came during a professional development workshop led by author and media personality Dr Terri-Karelle Johnson on September 12, 2026.

Johnson urged the students to recognise that their personal brands are being shaped every day, both online and offline. She focused on personal branding strategies, effective verbal and written communication, social media presence and digital footprint management, telling the scholars that consistency and cohesion in how they present themselves can create opportunities.

“Cohesiveness and consistency open up pathways through non-verbal and verbal communication. It is important to intentionally learn how to use these platforms while upholding the integrity, morals and standards that you set for yourself,” Johnson said.

She encouraged the students to consider the story they are communicating through their appearance, speech, behaviour and digital activity.

“It is important to visualise what story you are presenting to other people. Can you willingly vouch for you?” Johnson asked.

One of the major areas of discussion was the relationship between personal identity and professional reputation, particularly in an era when employers and organisations can easily find information about prospective employees online.

Johnson warned the students that their social media activity can become part of their professional identity, whether they intend it to or not.

“In an ideal world, you would want to separate your personal social media accounts from your business accounts, but that is not the case,” she said. “What you post is what you tell your future employer about yourself. You cannot afford to compromise your professional brand because of your personal brand.”

The students were also encouraged to understand the importance of authenticity.

“You have to be authentic. The real, genuine you is showing up as your authentic self,” Johnson said. However, authenticity, she noted, does not mean ignoring context or professional standards.

“You also have to understand time and place. As a brand, people, companies and organisations deal with you accordingly. You have to ensure that you do not compromise your values and attitudes. Put yourself together regardless of what your personal brand is,” she said.

The workshop formed part of the activities of the JWN Foundation Scholarship Awards ceremony, which celebrated the achievements of students from the foundation’s focus communities in Kingston, Clarendon and St Elizabeth.

It delved into the requirements they would need not just for the world of work, but personal branding tips and social media etiquette to help on their life’s journey.

Close to 70 tertiary scholarship recipients participated in the workshop. They also had the opportunity to have their make-up professionally done by Le Champ Cosmetics and professional headshots by LH Multimedia.

JWN Foundation General Manager Garfene Grandison said the decision to incorporate professional development into the programme was informed by observations from the scholarship selection process over the years.

“Coming out of the interview process, many of the interviewees struggled to express themselves and had some level of difficulty in how they were groomed for the process. Having recognised this, we wanted to ensure that we equip them with the relevant tools that will help them to represent themselves,” said Grandison.

World.title: Eleven charged with murder aggravated by speech against ‘white race’ in France
World.content:
The killing later fueled far-right mobilization, including an attempted “punitive expedition” by identitarian militants in nearby Romans-sur-Isère.

French judges have sent 11 defendants to the juvenile assize court over the 2023 stabbing to death of 16-year-old Thomas Perotto, with the case involving a racial aggravating factor in the reference to “the white race and the French nation,” French media reported Friday.

The order sending them to trial, seen by POLITICO, accuses the defendants of murdering Perotto at a village fête in Crépol, attempting to kill three other people and violently attacking others. Judges seek to trial them as a group because the investigation hasn’t determined who is alleged to have delivered the fatal blow, AFP reported.

The judges’ order states the alleged killing was “preceded, accompanied or followed by words, writings, images, objects or acts of any kind” harming the honor of victims or a group because of their supposed race, ethnicity, nation or religion — “in this case, the white race and the French nation.”

Some defendants were minors when the attack took place. All are presumed innocent. The Valence prosecutor’s office had initially sought trial on murder and attempted murder charges without the aggravating factor, saying witness statements supporting it were “in the minority” and “imprecise.”

Denis Dreyfus, a lawyer representing a group of attendees claiming damages, told POLITICO that the charges matched arguments his side had made. “We welcome the considerable work carried out by the investigating judges,” he said, adding that the case should now proceed with “the dignity due to Thomas and the victims.”

The defense pushed back on the charges. “How can our client be sent to trial for murder aggravated by a racial circumstance when neither the fatal blow nor any racist remarks are personally attributed to him?” lawyers Seydi Ba and Diala Al-Shaman, who represent one of the defendants, said, according to AFP.

A trial date has not been set. Elise Rey-Jacquot, a lawyer representing another defendent, told RTL on Saturday she would appeal the charges, potentially delaying proceedings.

World.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz could reopen within seven days if US accepts deal
World.content:
Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Bandar Abbas, Iran on Sept. 5, 2026. | Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi Friday said his country is offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks on its nuclear program in exchange for concessions from Washington.

Those would include lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waiving sanctions on Iranian oil sales and a ceasefire that would include Lebanon, Araghchi told reporters on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, according to an AP report.

“The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan,” he said on Friday, adding that Iran had conveyed its offer to the U.S. through Qatar.



Although U.S. President Donald Trump has not formally responded to the proposal, he privately rejected the plan, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing U.S. officials. He is instead betting on renewed escalation including by raising the possibility of another bombing campaign on the country after the midterm elections in November, according to the same report.

Trump on Friday night shared a map of the region on Truth Social, renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the “Trump Strait.”

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global oil and natural gas supplies and has been a major flashpoint since the U.S. and Israel launched their war against Iran in February.

World.title: Trump’s G20 invite to Putin is an ‘opportunity,’ German foreign minister says
World.content:
But Germany’s Wadephul struck a more optimistic tone during a press conference with his Canadian counterpart in Ottawa.

The invitation “will be a litmus test really, also for Vladimir Putin to negotiate. So these kind of opportunities, one would have to take advantage of,” he said. “Repeatedly we have asked the Russian government and Vladimir Putin to come to the negotiation table. And if it is a possibility, then perhaps it would be at least a start to serious negotiations.”

He then added that the prerequisite for a meaningful conversation would be for a ceasefire to be in place during the talks.

Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said she was surprised by Trump’s invitation to Putin, but added that Canada would show up regardless because that would be “what diplomacy truly is.”

Wadephul’s remarks diverged from his government’s official position. Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s spokesperson, Stefan Kornelius, had said earlier this week that “the German government does not view relations with Russia as business as usual” and that it was coordinating a joint response with its partners.

The German foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The White House’s invitation is the latest U.S. effort to reintegrate Moscow into the international diplomatic fold and could lead to `Putin’s first in-person G20 appearance since 2019.

World.title: Ein Spaziergang mit Karl Lauterbach
World.content:
Ein politisches Beben rüttelt die Republik durch: Während die Linkspartei in Berlin an die Spitze stürmt, fliegt die CDU in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern komplett aus dem Landtag. Nach diesem historischen Wahlsonntag stellt sich die drängende Frage, wie handlungsfähig die Koalition bei künftigen Reformen überhaupt noch ist. Steht das deutsche Parteiensystem vor dem Kollaps oder gibt es noch einen Ausweg aus der Krise?

Gordon Repinski spricht mit dem früheren SPD-Gesundheitsminister Karl Lauterbach über die Verschiebungen und darüber, ob die Politik nun völlig neue, grundsätzliche Ideen braucht. Lauterbach warnt davor, alles schlecht zu reden und verteidigt die Koalition von Union und SPD, die stabiler sei als oft behauptet. Außerdem warnt er davor, zu glauben, dass Kürzungen bei den Sozialausgaben zu mehr Wirtschaftswachstum führen würden.

Dazu diskutiert Repinski mit Lauterbach über neue KI-Modelle, ihre Gefährlichkeit und das weltweite KI-Wettrennen, bei dem Deutschland droht, den Anschluss zu verlieren.

Das Berlin Playbook als Podcast gibt es jeden Morgen ab 5 Uhr. Rixa Fürsen, Maximilian Stascheit und das POLITICO-Team liefern Politik zum Hören – kompakt, international, hintergründig.

World.title: Burnham’s AI agenda is already in disarray thanks to Trump
World.content:
Within the space of a week, however, Trump trashed any hopes that America will participate in global agreements on AI and POLITICO revealed that AISI’s usually privileged access to new AI models is now being delayed by the White House – which told leading AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic not to share their models with the U.K. until U.S. testers have finished ascertaining that they don’t pose a threat to American systems.

So if Burnham wants to stick to his plan of making U.K. the center for brokering international AI harmony he has to figure out how to bring the U.S. onside, or else press on without the U.K.’s closest ally.

When approached by POLITICO, a U.K. government spokesperson said: “The U.K. is a world leader in AI security, and the AI Security Institute continues to work closely with the U.S. government, international partners and leading AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic.”

Special relationship problems

The U.K. already has a track record for convening global meetings on AI safety, but it has also tended to stick by the U.S. when deciding whether to sit out specific international agreements.

In 2023 the U.K. hosted the Bletchley Park Summit on AI safety, which produced an agreement on the opportunities and risks of AI signed by 28 countries, crucially including the U.S. and China.

However, at the Paris iteration of the summit in 2025 the U.K. declined to sign a new declaration on the ethical development of AI alongside the U.S.

World.title: Dutch opposition party votes to join European Socialist family
World.content:
“There are only three European political families represented at all three levels [of the

EU],” the advisory committee wrote in a report, adding that the PES has “prime ministers, the President of the European Council, European Commissioners, and leaders of national parties.”

“The Greens … have fewer ministers, no members of the European Commission, and no

heads of government; consequently, their preliminary consultations carry less weight,” the

report went on.

PRO leader Jesse Klaver joined a PES meeting ahead of the European Council summit in June, alongside Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen.

What about the MEPs?

European political parties and political groups in the European Parliament are closely

linked, but they are not the same thing.

A PRO spokesperson told POLITICO that the party’s eight MEPs are likely to remain in

their current parliamentary groups: four in the Socialists and Democrats and four

in the Greens/European Free Alliance.

The spokesperson said PRO would likely review the arrangement ahead of the next

European Parliament election in 2029.

World.title: Pope Leo calls for dialogue as France’s populist forces eye power
World.content:
The pope named no politician or party. But his defense of diversity and religious freedom lands as Le Pen’s National Rally campaigns against immigration ahead of a presidential election she hopes to win for the first time.

“This dialogue is all the more urgent in the context of present-day France, where the people of differing cultural and religious backgrounds are called to live together,” the pontiff continued.

Standing in front of French government members and church dignitaries, the pope also argued against pushing religion out of public life, weeks after the National Rally said it was in favor of banning the Muslim headscarf. “Righteous secularism doesn’t mean excluding religion from public spaces,” he said.

Macron said the pope brought “hope” to France and praised his work on artificial intelligence and human dignity.

The papal visit will take Leo from the Élysée to UNESCO, Notre-Dame Cathedral and a youth vigil at the Stade de France. He will celebrate Mass on Saturday, expected to gather 600,000 people on the Champs-Elysées in Paris.

French politics have become deeply polarized in recent years, with the far-right National Rally and the far-left France Unbowed gaining popularity, just as traditional parties struggle to attract voters after a decade of Macron’s presidency.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons
World.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky (R) and High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas (L) attend a joint press-conference following talks in Kyiv on October 13, 2025. | Sergei Supinsky/AFP via Getty Images

The president said he received a positive and constructive response from the EU during his diplomatic talks this week.

KYIV — Ukraine needs to secure $27 billion to plug a hole in its defense budget in the next two months or risk being unable to buy weapons early next year, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters in a WhatsApp chat Friday.

“Most of this money is for our drones, missiles, and supplies for our warriors. About a third of this money, perhaps even a little more, is for drones for January, February, and March. And if we do not order and pay for them in October and November, we will face serious challenges in January and February,” Zelenskyy said.

The president added that covering the deficit was a top topic of his negotiations with European partners: “I am urging the European Commission to provide the second tranche of the €90 billion [loan] sooner. Because, once again, we must have the necessary drones and missiles for January and February.”

World.title: Fat Bear Week returns as Alaska's biggest bears compete for the crown
World.content:
Sixteen bears are competing in this year's tournament, with last year's winner, Chunk, officially known as Bear 32, hoping to defend his title. Chunk reportedly weighed 544 kilograms when he won last year's contest.

 

Now in its 12th year, Fat Bear Week invites people around the world to vote for the bear they believe has been most successful at gaining weight ahead of hibernation.

Speaking to the Associated Press, Mike Fitz, a resident naturalist at Explore.org, explained that the competition highlights how crucial weight gain is to the bears' survival. Because they do not eat during hibernation, they must consume enough food in roughly six months to sustain themselves for the entire year.

But choosing a winner is not simply a matter of identifying the heaviest bear.

"This year, I think it's pretty tough to predict. I mean, there's a few bears that are larger than others, but it's not necessarily about body mass alone. We want people to consider the bears' stories as well, because getting fat means different for a big adult male who's maybe trying to dominate access to the best fishing spots at Brooks Falls," he explains.

Why getting fat is essential for survival

Katmai National Park and Preserve is home to approximately 2,200 brown bears. The competition, which began in 2014, was designed to raise public awareness of the animals and their remarkable preparations for winter.

Adult male brown bears typically weigh between 270 and 410 kilograms, although particularly large males can exceed 450 kilograms after feeding extensively on salmon. Females are generally about one-third smaller.

During hibernation, the bears neither eat nor drink and can lose around a third of their body weight.

Fitz also highlighted the importance of healthy salmon populations to the bears' survival. He pointed to the abundant sockeye salmon runs in Alaska's Bristol Bay region as an example of what healthy river ecosystems can support.

According to Fitz, the region demonstrates why protecting and restoring salmon populations elsewhere in North America is so important, particularly in areas where salmon numbers are declining.

Beyond celebrating the bears' impressive size, the competition also offers an insight into their daily lives.

Fitz said viewers can observe everything from bears enjoying a successful fishing session and playing with one another to the difficulties faced by mothers trying to feed their cubs or coping with the loss of their young.

"We get to see their their joys when they have a belly full of fish, we get to see them having fun when they're playing with another bear in a friendly manner and we get the see the real hardships that they experience the mother struggling to feed their cubs, the mothers who maybe lose cubs for instance".

The competition's final round is scheduled for Tuesday, 29 September, when the public will decide which bear takes this year's title.

And for those who can't get enough of Fat Bear Week, Google has added an interactive surprise: Searching for "Fat Bear Week" brings up a small bear on the screen that users can feed salmon, helping it gain enough weight to survive winter hibernation.

World.title: Trump reportedly rejects Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
US President Donald trump has reportedly rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway that has been at the heart of tensions between Washington and Tehran since late February.

 

The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported on Friday that Trump had refused a proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait, telling his aides that he expected to resume a bombing campaign against Iran after the US' midterm elections in November.

Trump later posted an image on Truth Social showing an image of the Strait of Hormuz rebranded as the "Trump Strait."

Donald Trump and the Strait of Hormuz https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump

On Friday, Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, said that "if the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime traffic can resume within seven days," adding that the "choice now rests with the United States."

Referring to the June memorandum of understanding between Iran and the US, he added: "The actions that the US needs to take are not new. All of them were previously outlined in the memorandum of understanding."

"If the American side is serious about reaching an agreement and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now ready," Araghchi went on.

According to the Associated Press, Tehran has proposed that if the US were to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, cancel sanctions on Iranian oil sales, and observe a ceasefire that includes Lebanon, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks regarding its nuclear program.

Araghchi noted that the seven-day timeline of the plan would begin as soon as the US agreed. He said that completing the initial steps would take four to five days and that the Strait would reopen on the sixth day.

Referring to the start of nuclear talks, Araghchi added: "On the seventh day, negotiations with the US will begin to reach a final agreement on issues agreed upon by both sides."

He also said it would be "better" if an agreement with Washington were reached before the US midterm elections.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the president of Iran, also emphasized during an interview with CBS on Friday evening that if the US accepted Iran’s seven-day proposal, then Tehran would honour everything to which it has committed.

Pezeshkian holds an image of late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at United Nations headquarters. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

According to AP, Iran’s proposed plan closely resembles the June memorandum of understanding, but its timeline is more condensed. The June MoU had given the two nations 60 days to reach a final deal.

An American official familiar with the talks between Tehran and Washington said that the US government was conducting positive and constructive discussions through mediators but that it would not rush to reach an agreement.

Additionally, a US official speaking to Reuters confirmed the continuation of "positive and constructive" talks with Iran, adding that discussions regarding "nuclear issues" were also ongoing.

Ali Vaez, Iran project director at the International Crisis Group, said: "This is a clever move. They know this proposal is very tempting for President Trump because it ends an unpopular war and lowers energy prices on the eve of the midterm elections."

"At the same time, it revives an agreement that was largely to Iran's benefit," Vaez continued. "The condensed timeline to reach the nuclear issue should also be attractive to a president who is in a hurry".

Diplomatic efforts and friction within Iran’s leadership

Pezeshkian stated during his speech at the UN General Assembly in New York on Wednesday that Iran was not afraid of continuing the war, yet Tehran remains ready for diplomacy.

In the latest diplomatic push, Pezeshkian hosted Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the prime minister and foreign minister of Qatar, on Friday morning. Qatar has acted as a mediator in talks between the US and Iran.

But signs of disagreement among the Iranian leadership have also been emerging, with some hardliners criticising diplomatic steps taken by Pezeshkian and Araghchi.

Before leaving US soil, Pezeshkian reiterated his country’s readiness to resume negotiations.

He also explained that foreign policy decisions were deliberated by a six-member team representing various institutions, including the security forces, parliament, and government bodies, with decisions reached through coordination among these members.

But Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, wrote on X: "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is an executor, not a policymaker."

"The foreign minister must explain under what authorisation and policy guidelines his meeting with the representative of the aggressor enemy took place. Iran's conditions have been communicated to the US, and illegal meetings under the pretext of conditions yield nothing but a sign of weakness," he continued, adding: "Do not beg for agreement and understanding."

"Instead of manufacturing authorisations, repent, apologize, and make amends. The message of weakness previously imposed a 40-day war on the people and the country; do not repeat the mistake."

World.title: Six dead after explosion causes building to collapse in central Athens
World.content:
Six people have been confirmed dead after a building where they were staying collapsed in Athens.

 

The building collapsed following an explosion on Friday morning in the Plaka district of the Greek capital.

Four US tourists had been staying on the first floor of the building while a couple - a 78-year-old British man and a 77-year-old Greek woman - lived on the second floor. The process of formally identifying the bodies is ongoing.

Fire crews are now winding down the operation after hours of searching through the rubble.

Around 30 firefighters, using six vehicles, took part in the search, with three specially trained dogs also deployed.

Rescue teams used geophones to try to detect possible sounds beneath the rubble, as well as specialist cameras to pinpoint locations where people might be trapped.

The explosion occurred shortly after 7:30 am on Friday and also caused damage to neighbouring properties and vehicles.

Two women were freed from a nearby building on Friday and transported to hospital. Another person suffered minor injuries from flying debris.

Authorities are meanwhile working to determine the cause of the blast.

The fire service, police, and medical crews remain at the scene, with a team from the Arson Crimes Division also investigating the incident.
