World.title: PM Al Zaidi meets UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi met with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Barham Salih, and his accompanying delegation in New York to evaluate the status of refugees and internally displaced persons (IDPs), alongside joint humanitarian relief programs.

The diplomatic discussions were held on the sidelines of Al-Zaidi’s active participation in the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The talks centered on deepening institutional coordination between the Iraqi Federal Government and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), with a particular focus on mobilizing technical resources and international assistance to support vulnerable displaced populations.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi underscored that Baghdad places human rights and humanitarian protection at the forefront of its national priorities, maintaining consistent cooperation with the UNHCR and relevant multilateral agencies to enhance living conditions, deliver targeted welfare services, and rebuild stability across liberated and crisis-impacted areas.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the necessity of tackling the root causes driving involuntary displacement and asylum seeking, calling for cohesive regional and international coordination frameworks to safeguard the fundamental rights of displaced groups in strict alignment with international conventions and statutory humanitarian laws.

In response, High Commissioner Salih confirmed the agency’s commitment to supporting Iraq through comprehensive relief and developmental operations, stressing that the UNHCR will continue working with Baghdad to fulfill all operational and financial benchmarks necessary to permanently resolve the internal displacement file.

World.title: PM Al-Zaidi asserts state monopoly on arms and outlines economic vision at UNGA81
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi delivered a wide-ranging policy address before the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, presenting Baghdad’s strategic vision for national sovereignty, economic restructuring, and regional stability.

Reaffirming Iraq’s adherence to the principles of the United Nations Charter, Al-Zaidi framed the nation as an ascending economic force and an essential bridge for multilateral dialogue and cooperative diplomacy. He declared that the country’s immediate priorities stem from a decisive national will to restore the prestige of the rule of law, consolidate constitutional governance, and rebuild public confidence in sovereign state institutions.

Addressing the nation’s security architecture, the Prime Minister emphasized that the federal government holds the exclusive authority to determine matters of peace and war, asserting that all arms and instruments of legitimate force must remain strictly confined to the command of constitutional institutions.

Al-Zaidi underscored that current executive and regulatory enforcement measures are rooted in statutory mandates and supreme national interest, aimed at defending territorial integrity, consolidating security gains, and establishing the stable environment required to support sustainable socio-economic development and incoming international investments.

Highlighting a pivotal sovereign transition, Al-Zaidi noted that the conclusion of the U.S.-led International Coalition’s mission in Iraq marks a strategic evolution in Baghdad’s foreign partnerships, pivoting defense-centric alignments toward multifaceted economic and developmental cooperation.

He stressed that Iraqi forces have built the requisite autonomous military and intelligence capabilities to defend the nation’s borders, land, and people in the post-defeat era of terrorism. To sustain this regional equilibrium, the Prime Minister called on international partners and neighboring states to enforce rigorous border management, eliminate security gaps, and maintain constant counter-extremism coordination.

Turning to economic governance, Al-Zaidi outlined Iraq’s ongoing campaign against administrative and financial corruption, identifying the recovery and safeguarding of public funds as an indispensable pillar of institutional reform. He articulated an ambitious modernization agenda designed to transition Iraq away from the vulnerabilities of a rentier economy toward a dynamic, open-market framework integrated with global digital and technological systems.

To realize this transition, the federal government has established legal, tax, and customs incentives aimed at empowering private enterprises, attracting foreign direct investment, and leveraging Iraq’s strategic geographical crossroads to expand commercial flows.

In the energy sector, the Prime Minister reaffirmed comprehensive plans to boost crude oil production, capture and process natural gas reserves, and scale up refining capacities alongside downstream petrochemical industries, aiming to cement Iraq’s standing as a dependable global energy supplier.

Al-Zaidi voiced grave concern regarding disruptions to freedom of navigation and commercial shipping routes that have triggered sharp increases in global energy prices. To insulate national revenues and reinforce global market stability, he confirmed that Baghdad is actively advancing strategic pipeline corridors linking Iraq with Turkey, Jordan, and Syria to diversify crude export outlets away from maritime chokepoints.

Concluding his address, the Prime Minister presented Iraq’s multibillion-dollar Development Road project as an overarching blueprint for regional integration, characterizing the multimodal transit corridor as a vital artery connecting East and West through trade, logistics, industry, and energy networks.

Finally, Al-Zaidi invited neighboring states and global investment partners to participate directly in the transit corridor, reiterating Iraq’s conviction that shared economic interests, reciprocal trade ties, and cross-border infrastructure constitute the most durable foundation for lasting regional peace and prosperity.

World.title: Basra tribesmen liberate hijacked oil tanker in Gulf of Aden
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A tribal dignitary from Basra Governorate revealed on Friday, September 25, 2026, that approximately 40 members of the Al-Shaghanba tribe from the Abu Al-Khaseeb district successfully liberated a hijacked crude oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden, freeing the crew and capturing seven armed pirates.

Sheikh Ali Al-Shaghanbi stated that the commercial vessel, owned by an Iraqi businessman belonging to the Al-Shaghanba tribe, was intercepted and boarded by maritime pirates while transiting strategic maritime lanes off the southern Arabian Peninsula.

According to the tribal leader, the pirates seized control of the tanker, took the crew hostage, and issued ransom demands as a condition for their release.

In response, an expeditionary group of roughly 40 armed tribesmen from Abu Al-Khaseeb and the village of Jaykoor mobilized to mount a direct recovery operation, coordinating logistics and tracking through international contacts positioned outside Iraq.

The intervention concluded with the tribal forces successfully storming the vessel, regaining full command of the tanker, and securing the safe release of all detained crew members unharmed.

Sheikh Al-Shaghanbi confirmed that the clash resulted in the capture and detention of seven armed pirates found aboard the vessel, while remaining members of the pirate group managed to flee the maritime perimeter.

World.title: Al Zaidi courts US banks in New York targeting 10M bpd oil capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Under the auspices and in the presence of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Iraq to the United Nations in New York hosted a high-level roundtable meeting bringing together representatives from premier American commercial banks and financial institutions, Iraqi banking delegates, senior government officials, and economic analysts.

Held late Thursday evening Baghdad time on September 24, 2026, the diplomatic engagement was convened to re-establish institutional communication between Iraq’s financial sector and the international banking architecture, with a particular focus on direct correspondent relationships with major U.S. lenders.

In his address to the executive gathering, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi stressed that Iraq has embarked on an irreversible trajectory of structural economic transformation and banking sector modernization. He acknowledged that past vulnerabilities within Iraq’s domestic banking ecosystem were partly rooted in institutional isolation and restricted interaction with global financial hubs, particularly American banking conglomerates.

Al-Zaidi extended an open invitation to U.S. financial institutions to establish direct operational footprints in the Iraqi market, emphasizing that their market entry would represent a qualitative leap toward elevating local banking practices, adopting international compliance standards, and deepening Iraq’s integration into global capital networks.

Highlighting Iraq’s macroeconomic foundations, the Prime Minister noted that the country currently produces approximately 4.5 million barrels of crude oil per day, with federal energy policies actively targeting an expansion toward 10 million barrels per day over the long term.

This hydrocarbon expansion strategy is designed to maximize sovereign revenues and channel critical liquidity into national development, industrial manufacturing, and cross-sector economic diversification. Al-Zaidi assured participants that the government is actively engineering an investor-friendly environment with streamlined regulatory, customs, and fiscal frameworks, underscoring that American banks hold vast opportunities to structure project financing, issue commercial credit, and underwrite major capital ventures across energy, logistics, and real estate.

Detailing administrative reforms underway, Al-Zaidi outlined the government’s clear operational blueprint for comprehensive institutional restructuring across state-owned commercial banks. The initiative aims to enforce corporate governance benchmarks, upgrade anti-money laundering and know-your-customer compliance mechanisms, and build an agile banking framework capable of supporting modern commercial activities.

The Prime Minister affirmed that statutory anti-corruption proceedings, asset recovery drives, and fiscal protection measures are advancing effectively, reiterating Baghdad’s commitment to institutional transparency and the safeguarding of public and private investment funds.

World.title: Iraq and US sign accord handing over diplomatic center at Baghdad Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Government and the United States signed a formal agreement on Thursday, September 24, 2026, transferring full control of the Baghdad Diplomatic Support Center (BDSC) at Baghdad International Airport to the Iraqi side, marking a significant step in the systematic restructuring of bilateral ties between both nations.

The signing ceremony, hosted at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs headquarters in Baghdad, brought together Iraq’s Undersecretary for Bilateral Relations, Muhammad Hussein Bahr Al-Uloom, and the Chargé d’Affaires ad interim at the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Steven Fagin.

The foreign ministry stated that the handover forms an integral milestone in federal efforts to fulfill the technical and sovereign prerequisites for concluding the mission of the U.S.-led International Coalition and drawing down foreign military presence across Iraq, aligned with the established September 30, 2026, deadline.

By transferring authority over the high-profile logistical installation at the capital’s international gateway, the sovereign transition moves forward on schedule toward the formal cessation of coalition combat missions.

Undersecretary Bahr Al-Uloom emphasized the strategic weight of the agreement, framing the handover as an operational pivot toward an expanded bilateral era centered on mutual economic partnerships, energy infrastructure modernization, and broad-based development projects.

In response, Fagin reaffirmed Washington’s support for advancing bilateral collaboration within agreed strategic frameworks that uphold mutual sovereignty, with both diplomatic delegations concluding the ceremony by noting that the handover establishes practical foundations for deeper institutional cooperation and coordinated regional security frameworks.

World.title: Iraq targets first Gulf Cup win against Kuwait
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq will take on Kuwait on Saturday, looking for their first victory in the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup, after drawing 1-1 with Oman in Jeddah.

The Group A match will take place at Prince Abdullah Al Faisal Stadium in Baghdad at 6:55 p.m. local time, with Iraq starting the second round with one point and Kuwait aiming to rebound from a 1-0 loss to Saudi Arabia.

Iraq started quickly against Oman on Wednesday, with Mohammed Qasim scoring in the sixth minute with a strong left-footed finish.

Oman answered in the second half with Nasser Al-Rawahi, who equalized in the 67th minute to give both sides a draw.

News from Iraq’s Coach Graham Arnold said that preparations for the first match had been restricted, with his group having little time together before playing an Oman team that had been in camp for many days.

Arnold mentioned that Iraq’s players are physically, tactically, and emotionally ready for Kuwait. Arnold may make changes to his team for the match against Kuwait due to exhaustion and the hot weather in Saudi Arabia.

Half of Iraq’s Gulf Cup roster had competed in the 2026 World Cup, with the remaining being younger players given a chance with the national team.

Arnold said that Mustafa Saadoun and Mohammed Qasim are available for the match, while defender Akam Hashim’s fitness is being examined.

Saturday’s encounter is crucial after Iraq’s two-point loss to Oman. Saudi Arabia leads Group A with three points, Iraq and Oman have one apiece, while Kuwait has no points after the first round.

The top two teams advanced to the semifinals.

Iraq’s last group encounter is against Saudi Arabia on September 29, making it crucial to win against Kuwait before facing the current group leaders.

World.title: Iraqi PM calls on US firms to seize investment opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on US companies on Wednesday to seize investment opportunities available in Iraq, particularly in the petrochemicals, glass, and phosphate industries, as well as the gas and clean energy sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in New York with a delegation from the US Chamber of Commerce, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stated that Iraq has considerable natural resources, human resources, and a key geographical position, all of which serve as necessary foundations for successful partnerships. He explained that the government is seeking to use these resources to promote economic development and increase investment possibilities.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the government’s commitment to providing support for businesses and investors, such as granting ownership of land for investment projects in accordance with Iraqi laws, as well as access to tax and customs exemptions for up to ten years.

Iraq is working on infrastructure and transportation projects, notably the strategic project of the Development Road, which will improve Iraq’s position as a corridor connecting the East and West, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister affirmed that the government looks forward to establishing factories and setting up projects to diversify the economy and create job opportunities.

Al-Zaidi also asked members of the US Chamber of Commerce and specialized firms to attend the Baghdad Energy Conference and capitalize on the prospects offered in the country. He added that Iraq aspires to establish economic partnerships based on collaboration, mutual interest, and long-term investment.

World.title: Iraqi PM, US president discuss partnerships, regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in New York on Tuesday on the sideline of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and approaches to strengthen cooperation and partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and investment sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two sides also reviewed the latest developments in the region, as well as the joint efforts undertaken by Iraq and the United States to enhance regional and international security and stability.

The discussion takes place ahead of a crucial September 30 milestone, which marks a shift in Washington-Baghdad ties toward long-term economic collaboration as the US prepares to end its coalition military mission in Iraq.

Amid continuing negotiations between Iraq and US officials, including a recent meeting between al-Zaidi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Washington pressured Baghdad on its obligations to place weapons possessed by armed factions under state supervision.

In addition to their exclusive bilateral discussion, al-Zaidi attended President Trump’s larger gathering that included leaders from important regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations.

The larger gathering addressed strategies to coordinate post-war arrangements, protect global commerce supply lines, and develop diplomatic frameworks for Middle Eastern stability.

World.title: As Trump hugs Xi and plugs Sharif, India feels the squeeze
World.content:
TOI correspondent from Washington:

The clearest sign yet of a widening US-India diplomatic rift came this weekend from the White House and the United Nations, where India was denouncing Pakistan for what it called a litany of âfalsehoodsâ and âdeceit,â even as US President Donald Trump appeared to give those very claims a presidential imprimatur.

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had used his UN General Assembly address to revive Islamabadâs account of the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, crediting Trump with a âtimely interventionâ that, he said, prevented a wider war. On Friday night, shortly after Chinaâs President Xi Jinping had departed for Beijing, Trump posted an 87-second excerpt of Sharifâs speech on Truth Social without comment. The clip included Sharifâs praise of Trump and Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir.

The timing was striking. India had just exercised its Right of Reply, with First Secretary Petal Gahlot accusing Islamabad of peddling âfalsehoodsâ and âdeceitâ and describing Pakistan as a âpuppetâ regime. New Delhi has also rejected Trumpâs repeated assertion that he mediated the cessation of hostilities in May 2025, saying the fighting was halted after direct military-to-military communication between India and Pakistan.





For India, however, the larger concern may be less about one Truth Social post than about a pattern. The Xi visit to Washington this week appeared to underscore how dramatically the strategic geometry of US foreign policy has shifted. Rather than organizing its Asia policy principally around building India as a counterweight to China â a two-decade old Washington objective that resulting in an âIndo-Pacificâ focused QUAD â the Trump White House increasingly appears willing to deal with Beijing as a peer whose cooperation is indispensable, and whose confrontation carries costs Trump is reluctant to incur.

Following the Xi visit, Washington and Beijing extended their trade truce and agreed on tariff reductions covering $30 billion of less-sensitive goods in each direction, according reports in the Chinese media. They also operationalized bilateral boards on trade and investment and agreed to pursue an artificial-intelligence dialogue.

Analysts say none of this amounts to a formal US-China condominium, and deep disagreements over Taiwan, technology, trade and strategic competition remain.

But the emerging arrangement has prompted comparisons with a de facto G-2: Washington and Beijing managing their rivalry directly while other powers, including India, find themselves having to adjust to decisions made in a room in which they are not present.

âOne totally unsurprising consequence of this US-China trade truce is that Trump is not even thinking about implementing the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions legislation he just signed, which would have required penalizing China's support for Russia's war machine,â Tom Malinowski a former New Jersey lawmaker noted, even as Republicans close to Trump have been champing at the bit to punish New Delhi.

The Graham bill, signed by Trump on Sept.

18, gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue buying Russian crude or natural gas under specified conditions. The law specifically covers countries among the five largest Russian oil or gas importers that make new purchases, as well as countries identified among the top facilitators of sanctions evasion.

India is plainly exposed to that provision, as is China. Yet the contrast in Trumpâs handling of the two relationships has become difficult for New Delhi to ignore: Beijing is being courted into a new economic accommodation even as India faces the prospect of punitive trade action.

The message was reinforced this week by a senior State Department official who said the Graham law gives Trump âa new tool in his toolbox,â while emphasizing that its use is not automatic. The official pointed to a broad national-security waiver but added that Washington expects India to help the US end the Ukraine war.

More revealing was the official's description of what Washington now wants from India: not necessarily strategic alignment against China, but access to the enormous Indian energy market.

âWe are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs,â the official was quoted as saying, pointing to expanding US hydrocarbon exports and urging faster diversification away from Russian supplies.

All this is consequential because for two decades the bipartisan American strategy had been to help India acquire the economic, military and technological heft to balance China's rise. As recently as May, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who will be back in New Delhi in October, was describing India as one of America's most important strategic partners, while US officials continued to characterize New Delhi as a critical Indo-Pacific counterweight.

The language now coming from Washington is noticeably more transactional.

For New Delhi, the resulting unease is not simply about tariffs or Pakistan. It is about whether a strategic partnership painstakingly built across successive administrations is being replaced by a transactional relationship in which China is too powerful to punish, Pakistan is useful to cultivate, and India is expected to accommodate. And as New Delhi watched Washington kiss up to Beijing as an indispensable peer and embrace a country New Delhi views as a terrorism sponsor, the strategic space India once occupied in the American imagination appeared to be shrinking.

World.title: 'Avoids issue of Gen Z voters': Congress attacks EC's 'wishy-washy' press note, seeks pause in SIR
World.content:
"The CEC thinks he can hide behind âbureaucratiseâ and protocol. He stands exposed and is now petrified," claimed Jairam Ramesh

First, the Press note does not directly deny the story or its findings. It makes a defensive attempt to downplay the same in paragraph 3(i) and 3(ii) but does not say that the allegations are baseless.

Second, in the case of Goa, after having been caught out the ECI has sheepishly stated that Form 6 has already been filled out for inclusion by 81 of the 97 deleted voters. To put this another way, you disenfranchise voters through a broken and corrupt system, and when caught say that they are being added back.

Third, it seeks to justify the Commissions actions by appealing to the Order of the Supreme Court dated May 27th, 2026. The Order which was pronounced well before the recent revelations will not save the CEC for the malicious deletion of targeted voters, for the incompetence that has resulted in citizens being wiped off the roles, for the crores lost in both expenses and man-hours due to the confusion and harassment caused to entire families.

Fourth, it extends the deadlines for voter registration in Delhi and Maharashtra. But what happens to the voters of Karnataka and Telangana? What happens to the voters disenfranchised in Bihar and West Bengal? Do the voters of these and other states who were deleted due to one manâs corruption not deserve answers?

Fifth, the Press Release also states the ECI will now involve experts from IIT/IIIT to review the ECINET portal and submit a report to ensure it complies with rules. Aside from being a meaningless safeguard (since the concern is not about the technical soundness but rather the centralization which prevents voter addition at ground level) this confirms the concerns attributed to the two other Election Commissioners per the reportage.

Sixth, the Press Note avoids answering the questions regarding the deliberate targeting of Gen Z voters. The ECI has no answer for its targeted disenfranchisement, beginning mid-July 2026 through wholly illegal changes made to Form 6 (unseen and unapproved by Parliament) which placed an unfair burden on them to find and disclose their parents and/or grandparentsâ details.

World.title: Evening newswrap: EC holds key meeting amid SIR row; 11 killed in Pak suicide blast & more
World.content:
Election Commission said SIR decisions were unanimous and eased notice procedures, allowing BLO home visits and online hearings. It also extended claims deadlines in Delhi and Maharashtra.

At least 11 people were killed and around 30 injured after a suicide bomber targeted a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. TTP claimed responsibility.

India completed a golden double at the Asian Games as the men defeated Iran 40-34 in the final, hours after the women beat Iran 37-34 to retain gold.

World.title: 'Political parties can't but CJP can force Gyanesh Kumar to resign': Mamata faction MP on EC-SIR row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Only the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) can force Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to resign, senior

(TMC) MP Kalyan Banerjee said on Saturday.

According to Kalyan Banerjee, who is from the Mamata Banerjee faction of the TMC, no political party can force Kumar to step down.

âIf the CJP gives a real challenge, they can remove Kumar; no other political party can. If the CJP does it, there will be quick disposal. They stick to one issue and pursue it with all their heart and soul,â he told a vernacular news channel.

The CJP, a youth pressure group that led student protests that resulted in Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation as Union education minister over the NEET paper leak issue, has warned that it will launch a nationwide agitation in Mumbai from October 2, Mahatma Gandhiâs birth anniversary, if the CEC does not resign by Saturday.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday demanded Kumarâs resignation and threatened to launch a âJantar Mantar 2.0â agitation if the poll body chief does not step down, referring to the designated protest venue in Delhi where the group held its sit-in demanding Pradhanâs resignation.

Dipkeâs remarks came a day after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders of the Election Commission, including those concerning the addition, deletion and restoration of voters and changes to the voter registration process.





Following the report, poll panel officials said the two commissioners had raised objections to decisions taken during the electoral roll clean-up and the handling of voter databases in various states.

Election Commission sources, however, maintained that all decisions of the commission, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), had been unanimous and approved by both election commissioners and the chief election commissioner.

World.title: SIR row: EC says final decisions unanimous, clarifies officer’s role, voter inclusion process
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Saturday said all decisions taken on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously, while announcing measures to simplify the process for voters facing notices over discrepancies.

The clarification comes amid row over report that claimed differences within the EC over SIR of electoral rolls.

Also Read |

"In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country. The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission.

The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026. The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission.

The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the poll body said in a statement.

At a meeting held on Saturday, the Commission decided that voters who receive notices during the ongoing SIR over being unmapped or having logical discrepancies will not ordinarily have to appear before the electoral registration officer (ERO).





Booth-level officers (BLOs) will visit their homes to collect documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to decide.

Also Read |

Hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online. An adult family member can also attend a hearing on behalf of the elector if authorised. The Commission said facilities for online hearings would be strengthened.

The Commission also directed district election officers to set up help desks and special camps for people living in night shelters, labourers, poor people and homeless persons, depending on local requirements.

The EC said SIR has been completed in 20 states and Union territories, including Bihar and West Bengal. It said voters whose names were left out during or after the exercise, as well as young and first-time voters, can apply to the concerned ERO for inclusion through continuous updation. Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs), DEOs and EROs have been directed to launch a special enrolment drive.

EC clarifies officer, IT division row

The Commission also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary was not related to any policy decision concerning the Commission or its IT division, but concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation to the EC.

It said work redistribution orders issued by the officer were not implemented after directions from two Commissioners, and oversight of the IT division by the Deputy Election Commissioner was never withdrawn.

The EC said field officers have role-based access to the ECINet system based on their statutory powers. A committee headed by a senior Deputy Election Commissioner and including an independent IIT/IIIT expert will review the system for compliance with relevant laws and rules.

The Commission also said future initiatives involving IT modules and portals would be discussed by the Committee of Officers before being placed for approval.

Claims deadline extended in Delhi, Maharashtra

The Commission extended the deadline for filing claims and objections in Delhi till October 30, following a request from the Delhi CEO. The deadline for disposal of notices and claims and objections has been extended till November 30.

In Maharashtra, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended till October 12, while their disposal will continue till November 10.

The Commission further said the SIR order issued on June 24, 2025, covering all states and UTs and subsequently implemented in phases, had received unanimous approval. It added that the Supreme Court upheld the order on May 27, 2026.

In Goa, the EC said BLOs had been directed to visit voters left out of the rolls and collect their forms. Of 97 such voters, 81 have already filled Form 6 for inclusion.

The Commission also directed that agendas for its meetings be circulated in advance and minutes issued, while requiring officers' annual performance reports to be completed by December 31 each year. World.title: 'Not talking on behalf of EC': Union minister says 'no proof' of EC-SIR row, slams opposition
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Prahlad Joshi on Saturday hit out at the opposition over its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid the ongoing controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying there was no âconcrete proofâ to support the allegations being raised against the Election Commission.

Reacting to the opposition's claims, Joshi said the protest was an expression of the âpainâ caused by its electoral defeat. He said the SIR issue was being used to voice that distress.

âThe pain in their hearts caused by their defeat... they are trying to express that distress through the SIR issue,â Joshi said.

His remarks came in response to questions about a report published by The Indian Express, which cited concerns allegedly raised within the Election Commission over the SIR exercise.

The report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period.

The reports led the opposition to seek action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demand a halt to the SIR, while the ECI said internal notes, queries and differences of view are part of its functioning and maintained that all final decisions on the exercise were unanimous.





Joshi said that even if the report was taken into consideration, it did not amount to conclusive evidence of wrongdoing.

âWhatever has appeared in The Indian Express... if you even believe that, I am not saying they have no right, but I am also saying that it is not concrete proof for that. It is not at all concrete proof,â he said.

Joshi also disputed the opposition's suggestion that decisions related to the SIR were taken unilaterally.

Referring to the Election Commission's own press release, he said decisions of the poll panel had been unanimous.

âAnd whatever has been written in The Indian Express, even that never states that a unilateral decision was taken. All the decisionsâall, I am not saying almostâall the decisions of the Election Commission have been taken unanimously,â Joshi said.

The Union minister, however, clarified that he was not speaking on behalf of the poll panel.

âI am not talking on behalf of the Election Commission, but I am speaking based on the press release issued by the Election Commission,â Joshi said.

The opposition has been protesting against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and has raised questions about the manner in which the electoral-roll revision is being conducted.

World.title: AI should complement radiologists, says AIIMS-Mangalagiri chief at AP IRIA conference
World.content:
More than 800 radiologists and imaging professionals from across the country are attending the 12th annual State conference of the Andhra Pradesh Indian Radiological and Imaging Association (AP IRIA)-2026 at AIIMS-Mangalagiri. The conference began on September 25 and will continue till September 27.

Executive Director of AIIMS-Mangalagiri Ahanthem Santa Singh, who attended the inaugural ceremony as the guest of honour on Saturday (September 26), highlighted the growing role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in radiology. He said AI should not replace radiologists but serve as a companion, supporting clinical decision-making and improving patient care.

Prudhvinatha Reddy, Additional Professor and Head of the Department of Radio-Diagnosis at AIIMS-Mangalagiri, was awarded a gold medal by AP IRIA for his academic excellence and contribution to the field of radiology.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Reddy said more conferences should be organised, particularly for young radiologists, to provide opportunities for knowledge sharing, professional interaction and learning about advances in radiology.

Organised by the AP IRIA Vijayawada subchapter in association with the Department of Radio-Diagnosis, AIIMS-Mangalagiri, the conference features scientific sessions, lectures, panel discussions and academic presentations on diagnostic and interventional radiology, AI and emerging imaging technologies.

Members of AP IRIA are participating in the conference.

World.title: Minister urges police constables to stay disciplined, technically aware
World.content:
As many as 142 police constable trainees belonging to Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts passed out of the District Training Centre (DTC) in Chittoor on Saturday after completing nine months of training. The passing-out-parade of the SCT PC-2025 batch was held at the DTC grounds here.

Minister for Transport and district in-charge Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy, who was the chief guest, said it was heartening to see highly educated youth joining the police force. He said the government was giving top priority to filling vacant posts in the police department.

“The State government issued a notification for 5,000 constable posts at one go and completed the recruitment process. The stipend for trainees has been increased from ₹4,500 to ₹12,000,” the Minister said.

Calling on the trainees to uphold discipline and honesty, the Minister urged them to be technically aware in an era of artificial intelligence and rising cybercrimes.

District Collector Sumit Kumar said that for many people, a constable would be the first and most visible face of the government. “People expect justice, safety and good service from you. You have to be lawful, impartial and responsible while dealing with vulnerable sections and victims,” he said.

Superintendent of Police (SP) Tushar Dudi said the trainees should continue the discipline and efficiency they displayed today in the field as well. “Work with integrity and bring a good name to your families, DTC Chittoor and the State police,” he said.

World.title: Two Naga civilians killed in Manipur’s Senapati district
World.content:
Suspected extremists killed two Naga civilians in Manipur’s Senapati district on Saturday (September 26, 2026), barely 48 hours after Myanmar-based assailants gunned down four people in Kamjong district.

District officials could not confirm how the two Naga men, identified as Rocky Mao of Chowainamei village and Kumar Poumai of Laii Shirafii village, were killed or what led to the incident.

Naga-dominated district

Senapati is a Naga-dominated district. One of the deceased is a Mao Naga and the other is a Poumai Naga. Two others injured — Ashiho Sani and Adani Manio — belong to the Mao Naga community.

The injured were rushed to a private hospital for treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were taken to Senapati District Hospital for autopsy and other legal formalities.

Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh was in Senapati district on an official visit when reports of the killing came in. He attended the silver jubilee celebration of a missionary school in Mao, which borders Nagaland.

World.title: TDP leader alleges ₹500-crore scam in Sachivalayam jobs during YSRCP term
World.content:
Telugu Desam Party MLC Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy has accused the previous YSRCP regime led by the former Chief Minister, Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, of having indulged in a ₹500 crore scam by selling jobs in Sachivalayam (ward and village secretariats).

Addressing the media in Kadapa on Saturday, he said each job was sold for anything between ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh by the YSRCP leaders at various levels.

“Names of the candidates written on paper chits were sent to the district Collectors, recommending them for the jobs,” the TDP leader charged.

Mr. Reddy also pointed out that as many as 3,437 jobs were given under sports quota, with 801 ‘selected’ for merely participating in school games.

“Any candidate who had played, not won any medal or prize, any game in the neighbourhood school and produced a certificate to this effect got a job,” he remarked.

The MLC also blamed the previous government for giving jobs to those who had participated in rural games, folk festivals and countryside celebrations like ‘Sankranti Sambaralu’.

With such a shabby track record, Mr. Jagan was blaming our sports quota policy, Mr. Reddy said, demanding that the State government probe the case and unearth the scam.

World.title: Annual Credit Plan envisions a credit outlay of ₹54,438 crore for Krishnagiri
World.content:
The Annual Credit Plan (ACP) for Krishnagiri district was released by Collector C. Dinesh Kumar at the Collectorate on Saturday (September 26).

The ACP envisions a total credit outlay of ₹54,438.99 crore for 2026-27. Of this, ₹30,906.64 crore (56.8%) has been earmarked for the priority sector and ₹23,532.34 crore (43.2%) for the non-priority sector.

The sector-wise allocation entails ₹20,539.36 crore towards agriculture, earmarking the largest share, reflecting the predominantly agrarian nature of the district. MSMEs have been allocated ₹8,345.82 crore to support the auto cluster in Hosur and the granite cluster in Jagadevi/Bargur. Other priority sectors such as education, housing, renewable energy, social infrastructure, and export credit entail an allocation of ₹2,021.46 crore .

As far as the performance assessment under the previous year’s plan, against a target of ₹42,484.32 crore for financial year 2025-26, banks in the district achieved a credit flow of ₹48,726.20 crore, registering an achievement of 114.69%, reflecting the sustained efforts of the banking network in the district, according to the banks. Releasing the Annual Credit Plan, Collector and the District Consultative Committee Chairperson Dinesh Kumar appealed to all banks in the district to to extend credit support to farmers, MSMEs and other eligible beneficiaries under various Government-sponsored schemes, so as to further the district’s economic growth.

The Plan was jointly released in the presence of Sowndari M., Deputy Zonal Manager, Indian Bank, and M. Sasikumar, Lead District Manager, Krishnagiri. The Plan was prepared by Indian Bank, the Lead Bank for the district.

World.title: At least 13 killed in bomb blast in northwest Pakistan
World.content:
At least 13 people, including two women and two children, were killed and 30 others injured when an explosives-laden vehicle rammed into a police checkpost in northwest Pakistan on Saturday (September 26, 2026), an official said.

According to Pakistan’s national emergency response service Rescue 1122, the incident occurred in Darazinda tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan district, near the border between the restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces.

The banned terror outfit Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has claimed responsibility for the attack.

A suicide bomber rammed a tractor-trolley loaded with explosives into a joint police and customs checkpost in the Aman Mela area, Regional Police Officer Khan Mubashir Malik said.

The checkpost had been set up to curb smuggling and check the illegal movement of goods along the Dera Ismail Khan-Quetta road.

The blast destroyed a large portion of the checkpost and completely demolished a nearby house, killing four.

Overall, 13 people were killed, including the suicide bomber, six excise and customs department officials, two policemen, two women and two children, a security officer said, adding that 30 sustained injuries.

The injured were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital for treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were also taken there.

Bomb disposal teams were dispatched to the site to determine the nature of the explosives used in the attack, police said. Security forces cordoned off the area and launched a search operation following the attack, while further investigation was under way.

President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the blast in a statement issued by his office and expressed grief over the casualties.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the attack and sought a report from the concerned officials, while Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi expressed condolences to the bereaved families. “The cowardly acts of khwarjis cannot weaken the nation’s firm resolve against terrorism,” he said. The federal government uses the term Fitna al Khwarij for the TTP.

The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province has faced recurring unrest over the years driven by militant violence, cross-border movement of fighters from Afghanistan and repeated military operations.

The federal government has accused the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan of carrying out attacks in the province since the militant group ended its ceasefire with the government in November 2022.

World.title: 48-hour Ganesh immersion procession concludes in Hyderabad
World.content:
The Ganesh immersion procession in Hyderabad concluded on Saturday afternoon, bringing to an end a 48-hour operation that saw lakhs of devotees throng the city’s central stretches and more than 28,000 police personnel deployed for security and crowd management.

City Police Commissioner V. C. Sajjanar said the immersion festivities concluded peacefully, with the final phase stretching well into Saturday after the heavy turnout of devotees slowed the movement of idols towards Hussainsagar.

The immersion process had been slightly delayed as lakhs of people, many accompanied by their families, gathered around Tank Bund, NTR Marg, Necklace Road, Liberty and Moazzam Jahi Market. Traffic restrictions consequently remained in place along the main procession routes on Saturday until the remaining idols were cleared.

The Commissioner said preparations for the festival had begun three months in advance, while coordination with various government departments and other stakeholders had been underway for the past two months.

According to the officer, approximately 30 lakh devotees visited the Khairatabad Bada Ganesh during the festival, while about 15 lakh offered prayers at the Balapur Ganesh. He said there had been an increase in both the number of idols and the turnout of devotees this year.

The Khairatabad and Balapur Ganesh idols were immersed ahead of time with the cooperation of their respective festival committees. However, some other pandal organisers began their journeys late, contributing to the procession stretching into Saturday.

Joint inspections of the procession route from Balapur to Hussainsagar had been conducted with festival committees and officials from different government departments. Police also used technology to monitor the procession, while officials worked from the TGICCC Multi-Agency War Room to address problems arising on the ground.

The Commissioner said coordination among the police, GHMC, Revenue, Electricity, RTA, HMDA and other agencies was crucial to managing the event. Cranes deployed along Tank Bund, NTR Marg and Necklace Road and traffic diversions across the procession stretches formed part of the final 48-hour operation.

Over the two days, the Commissioner travelled on a motorcycle along several procession stretches, including Tank Bund, Basheerbagh, Liberty, Ambedkar Statue, Telugu Talli Flyover, M.J. Market, Nampally, Gandhi Bhavan and Nizam College Junction, inspecting arrangements and interacting with personnel deployed on the ground.

While describing the immersion as peaceful, the Commissioner also flagged several issues that police intend to address before next year’s festival.

The use of paper shower cannons during processions had left large quantities of paper on roads, creating a skidding hazard for two-wheelers when it rained, he said. Police would bring the issue to the government’s notice and seek a ban on such devices from next year.

Waste left behind after food distribution during the festivities would also be regulated, he said. He also expressed concern over instances of drunk driving and what he described as obscene dancing by a few individuals. Police plan to hold advance meetings with festival committees and idol makers ahead of the 2027 festivities to create awareness about idol height restrictions, security standards and discipline.

“A detailed debriefing of this year’s operation will now be conducted, with police planning to use lessons from the exercise to begin preparations for the 2027 Ganesh festival,” concluded the officer.

World.title: Illegal pole installation by solar power firm along roads, waterbodies cause concern at Radhapuram
World.content:
The installation of over 100 electric poles inside water bodies, irrigation channels and along roads by an upcoming private solar power generation unit without obtaining mandatory permission has caused concern among residents of a few villages at Radhapuram taluk in Tirunelveli distrct.

The villagers are annoyed because any possible collapse of the unauthorised electric poles may pose a serious threat to them, their families, houses, livestock and other properties.

According to them, a private solar power company that is coming up at Mudavankulam near Radhapuram for generating 25 MW electricity is establishing its unit on 108 acres for generating 5 MW power in the first phase. Even as work is under way, the company is installing 120 electric poles for a distance of 12 km to transmit power generated in the unit to a nearby sub-station to be subsequently connected to the grid.

“Barring 20 poles installed on private patta lands, all others have been erected along the road, inside the Public Works Department’s water bodies and irrigation channels and on panchayat union roads and HR and CE lands. But none of the departments has given any permission for the work,” said a villager from Ramakrishnaperi.

E. Bharathiraja, a farmer from Mudavankulam, has submitted a complaint with the Assistant Engineer of Kothaiyar Basin Sub-Division, Vadakkankulam, seeking removal of the electric poles installed in irrigation tanks and water channels.

R. Saravanakumar of Thalavaipuram has submitted a complaint with the Joint Commissioner of HR and CE, Tirunelveli, on September 24, accusing the solar power company of putting up electric poles along the land belonging to Sri Nithyakalyani Amman Temple, Radhapuram.

In his complaint with the Inspector of Police, Radhapuram, on September 22, Junior Engineer of Department of Highways, Radhapuram, L. Murugalingam has prayed for legal action against the solar unit for installing 14 electric poles in the night without permission on land belonging to the Department of Highways.

When the Highways officials found out about the illegal installation of electric poles, they detained a lorry, it is said.

Anand, who supervises the installations for the company, says they have applied for permission and ‘no objection certificates’ from various government departments.

Superintendent of Police Vishwesh Balasubramaniam Shastri said the issue was not brought to his knowledge. “We received a complaint only from the solar company on reported blocking of access to its premises following a land dispute, for which we have registered a case.”

He added that he would check on the complaint given by the Department of Highways about the unlawful installation of electric poles.

When contacted, Collector Anand Mohan said, ”the company had applied for regularisation of electric poles erected inside the water body as per extant rules. At the same time, we have received complaints from the public as well.. Both the application for regularisation and the complaints from the public are under examination.”

World.title: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30
World.content:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said.

Separately, a rescue worker was killed and two others were injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast.

DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast. He clarified that no law enforcement or security personnel were among the deceased, which included a Customs official and civilians.

The deceased comprised nine men, two women and a minor.

According to police and Rescue 1122 officials, an unidentified attacker rammed the explosives-laden tractor trolley into the checkpost. DI Khan District Police Officer (DPO) Ziauddin Ahmed confirmed that it was a suicide blast.

The blast destroyed a large portion of the checkpost and completely demolished a house adjacent to the post. The intensity of the explosion was such that it was heard over a considerable distance, according to local officials and residents. Heavy firing was also heard following the blast.

The Aman Mela checkpost, located near Mughal Kot and Darazinda on the DI Khan-Quetta Road, is used by police for security and checking along the route. It is situated close to the border between Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

According to RPO Maken, 25 of the injured were being taken to the district headquarters (DHQ) hospital. Meanwhile, District Excise Officer Faheem Wazir said Excise personnel present at the checkpost remained safe.

A bomb disposal team was also sent to the site to determine the nature of the explosion and examine the scene, police said.

DPO Ahmed and the superintendent of police for the Saddar area had reached the site soon after the explosion and supervised the rescue operation. A Rescue 1122 spokesperson noted that their teams were on the site for relief operations, but mobile phone services were unavailable in the area.

More than 25 personnel, six ambulances and a fire vehicle took part in the relief operations, according to the rescue service. On the directions of District Emergency Officer (DEO) Mohammad Arif Khan, four additional ambulances with staff were dispatched from DI Khan to assist in evacuating the injured.

1 killed as ambulance comes under fire

Rescue 1122 officials said a rescue worker was killed while two others were seriously injured when an ambulance transporting some bodies recovered from the blast site was targeted by gunfire.

The deceased was identified as Rescue 1122 worker Shareefullah, while Anees and Imtiaz sustained serious injuries.

Rescue personnel provided immediate medical assistance to the injured and took them to hospital for further treatment.

Despite the firing incident, rescue teams continued the operation to transport the bodies and assist those affected by the blast.

Governor seeks report

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi sought a report from senior officials on the incident and directed that every possible medical facility be provided to those injured.

“The attack is a nefarious conspiracy by Fitna al-Hindustan Khawarij,” the governor said.

The state refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan, and uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

President Asif Ali Zardari strongly condemned the blast in a statement issued by the Presidency and expressed grief over the lives lost.

The president ordered that the best medical facilities be provided to the injured, and that relief operations be made “more effective”.

“Making innocent citizens and law enforcement personnel a target of terrorism is highly condemnable,” he was quoted as saying.

“Operations against terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan and Fitna al Khawarij, who perpetrate heinous acts with foreign support, must be made more effective.”

In a statement issued by his ministry, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the “suicide blast at the anti-smuggling Aman Mela police checkpost” and expressed his condolences to the bereaved families.

“The cowardly acts of kharjis cannot weaken the nation’s firm resolve against terrorism,” he was quoted as saying, using a term the state employs to designate terrorists.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is on the front lines of the fight against terrorism.”

Naqvi noted that people from all walks of life have made sacrifices against terrorism, adding that the state deeply values the sacrifices of martyrs.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said that the “terrorist attack” in DI Khan, following the recent bloodshed in Kohat, was “another painful reminder of the terrorism threat Pakistan continues to confront”.

“My deepest condolences to the families of our martyrs and prayers for the injured. The nation stands firmly with our courageous police, law-enforcement agencies and security forces,” he said.

“Pakistan has defeated terrorism before, and we will defeat it again. Terrorists, their facilitators, financiers and sponsors will be held accountable and no territory beyond our borders will be allowed to serve as a sanctuary for terrorism against Pakistan,” he said.

“We will neither be intimidated nor divided. Pakistan will prevail,” Bilawal said.

Rise in terrorism

KP has witnessed an increase in terrorist activity in recent months, with law enforcement agencies and security forces being targeted, prompting authorities to intensify counterterrorism operations.

Earlier this month, police said they foiled an attack by TTP terrorists on a checkpost in DI Khan’s Daraban area. No casualties were reported among the police personnel.

On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation .

In response to that and other terrorist incidents, Pakistan days later conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying over 28 terrorists were eliminated.

Mainland KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

World.title: Makkah alliance military chiefs vow to ‘immediately’ translate commitments into effective military cooperation: ISPR
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have expressed a shared determination to “immediately translate” their commitments under the Makkah Defence Alliance into effective military cooperation, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Saturday.

The commitment was made at a meeting of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir and the chiefs of general staff of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Riyadh on Friday.

The meeting took place against the backdrop of heightened security concerns in the kingdom, with the Houthis and the Yemeni government engaged in renewed fighting . The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia and attacked ships in the Red Sea, while also carrying out attacks in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks.

Earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) had said the three countries were considering a meeting of their military chiefs to discuss ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance.

According to the ISPR, the participants discussed measures to advance cooperation among their armed forces, including enhanced intelligence sharing, military coordination and integration of capabilities.

The measures would help strengthen deterrence and collective defence, the military’s media wing said.

The participants also reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and strongly “resented” attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as civilian and economic infrastructure.

They appreciated the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces in ensuring the safety of the people and security of the kingdom, according to the ISPR.

The military chiefs further affirmed their commitment to collective defence, which, the ISPR said, demonstrated the resolve of the three countries to defend Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The ISPR added that the Riyadh meeting reflected the strength of the defence partnership among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, as well as their shared determination to implement the commitments under the tripartite defence agreement.

The participants also commended the longstanding relations and mutual trust between the three countries and their armed forces.

Kingdom ‘welcomed’ outcomes of meeting

Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, in a post on X, said that he and CDF Field Marshal Munir “welcomed the outcomes” of the chiefs of staff meeting held under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

Prince Khalid said they discussed the “heinous attacks” targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as on the kingdom’s civilian and economic infrastructure.

He said the two sides affirmed their continued joint efforts to confront the attacks in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

The Makkah alliance was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Makkah on Aug 7 and the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee was subsequently held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where the three countries agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Riyadh and decided that Pakistan would provide the secretary general for its first three-year term.

Pakistan appointed retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as the alliance’s first secretary general, taking another step towards putting the institutional structure of the pact in place.

The earlier New York ministerial meeting indicated that the three governments wanted the military chiefs to examine practical options. Therefore, the Riyadh meeting was expected to begin that process, although any decision on specific deployments or military assistance would depend on the Saudi requirement and the agreement reached by the three sides.

Turkiye has already signalled its willingness to address Saudi military requirements, with Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan saying last week that Ankara was ready to help with “military needs, especially on some technical issues”. Pakistan has also repeatedly affirmed its commitment to the agreement.

World.title: Naqvi assails PTI's 'version of equality before law' after KP IG told to ensure speaker's approval for any MPA's arrest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday took strong exception to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government’s attempt to further solidify legislation mandating the assembly speaker’s prior permission for an MPA’s arrest or detention.

In a post on X, Naqvi shared a KP Assembly Secretariat’s letter addressed to the KP inspector general (IG) on Friday, a day after the provincial cabinet approved the KP Police Act 2026. The proposed law, yet to be passed by the assembly, links the IG’s decisions to the chief minister or the government’s approval.

In his letter to IG Zulfiqar Hameed, KP Assembly Deputy Secretary (Admin) Ibrahim Khan reminded him of Section 11 of the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026, which made the speaker’s approval mandatory to arrest or detain an MPA.

The Act was among multiple pieces of legislation enacted in April by the KP government. A few of those provisions about lifetime blue passports and arms licences were withdrawn in August after facing criticism from the media and public.

Commenting on the letter on Saturday, Naqvi said: “Now in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, even if an MPA is accused of a criminal offence, the police must first seek the speaker’s permission before arresting him.

“What next?” the minister asked, detesting that in case an MPA killed a person, would the police “first wait for the speaker’s permission to arrest him?”

“What an extraordinary version of ‘equality before law’. Well done. Keep it up! And this is Riyasat-i-Madina?“ Naqvi wrote, referring to PTI founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s motto of transforming Pakistan into Riyasat-i-Madina (the State of Madina).

In the letter, the KP Assembly Secretariat had directed the IG to ensure strict compliance with Section 11 of the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 2026.

The letter reproduced the section, titled “permission of speaker before arrest, detention etc of a member”, which provides:

“(1) When a member has to be arrested on a criminal charge or for a criminal offence or has to be detained under an executive order, the magistrate or the executive authority, as the case may be, shall seek prior permission of the speaker, indicating the reasons for the arrest or detention of the member in the appropriate form set out in the Second Schedule.

“(2) Where the speaker deems it necessary in the public interest, he may require the relevant police officer to submit the police report or challan, as the case may be, to ascertain the facts of the matter. The speaker may, in his discretion, call up such inquiry before submission of challan in the court, as he may deem appropriate.”

The KP Assembly Secretariat directed the IGP to ensure strict compliance with Section 11 and adopt the prescribed procedure before arresting or detaining any provincial lawmaker, whenever such action becomes necessary.

The development comes amid an already heated debate over the new KP Police Act, with the interior ministry arguing that the provincial legislation violates the constitutional framework and weakens the police command structure at a time when KP remains on the frontline of the fight against terrorism.

The approval comes as the PTI claims dozens of its leaders and workers have been detained ahead of the party’s nationwide protest, now rescheduled for Oct 4. It has also said KP cabinet members were being targeted by unidentified individuals.

During a cabinet meeting that approved the Police Act, CM Sohail Afridi said if his government was forcing the local bureaucracy, police, district commissioners or others to do anything wrong, then they should not obey those orders.

World.title: ATC issues contempt notice to Adiala superintendent over failure to facilitate Imaan, Hadi’s powers of attorney
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday issued a contempt of court notice to the Adiala jail superintendent for allegedly failing to facilitate the signing and transmission of powers of attorney (vakalatnamas) required to file bail petitions for Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.

On Tuesday, the court returned bail petitions filed by human rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi in the Kohsar police station protest case over the absence of signed powers of attorney.

During the proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra directed the jail superintendent to explain why he should not be sentenced to six months in prison for allegedly disobeying the court’s orders.

No representative of Adiala jail appeared before the court, while the two accused could also not be produced through video link despite a previous direction.

Dr Shireen Mazari, Imaan’s mother, and a large number of lawyers appeared before the court during the proceedings.

The judge expressed displeasure over the failure of the jail authorities to obtain Imaan and Hadi’s signatures on the powers of attorney, which are required to authorise lawyers to represent them in the bail proceedings.

Judge Sipra remarked that the jail superintendent should not push the court — or himself — into a corner.

He asked whether the deputy superintendent had collected the powers of attorneys from the sessions court on the relevant day.

Advocate Riasat Ali Azad told the court that he was not certain whether the documents had been collected from the court. He said the lawyers had submitted the powers of attorneys there for onward transmission to Adiala jail in compliance with the court’s order.

The serial numbers of the powers of attorneys submitted to the sessions court were subsequently presented before the bench.

The court staff informed Judge Sipra that Imaan and Hadi were not being produced through video link because the jail authorities had cited internet connectivity problems.

The judge expressed dissatisfaction with the explanation, observing that the Adiala jail authorities had also repeatedly cited internet connectivity issues in an earlier case.

He recalled that he had previously directed experts from PTCL and NTC to visit Adiala jail to resolve the connectivity problem, specifically instructing that experts be sent from Haripur.

Judge Sipra observed that obtaining and signing the vakalatnama was a fundamental right of an accused and could not be denied on account of administrative hurdles.

The court subsequently issued a show-cause notice for contempt of court to the Adiala jail superintendent and sought an explanation as to why he should not be sentenced to six months’ imprisonment.

The ATC adjourned further proceedings until Tuesday.

On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

However, on September 17, the Supreme Court suspended the couple’s sentences in the controversial social media posts case. The SC granted the couple bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000 and ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict.

Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the Kohsar police station protest case. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night. However, the ATC rejected the police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand.

World.title: India's election commission orders review of voter-roll changes
World.content:
The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters.

Opposition parties have claimed the lists have been manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission of India has said differences are normal in any institution, and that all its actions were lawful.

The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating voters’ lists that began last year.

Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have demanded Kumar’s resignation.

The CJP said it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if he did not quit by Saturday.

The Commission said on Saturday that a committee led by a senior election official and including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules.

It also said local officials would visit voters flagged for discrepancies instead of routinely requiring them to appear at government offices.

World.title: 'Largest hypocrisy in the world': Pakistan tells UNGA India’s 'terrorist exports' have gone global
World.content:
Pakistan on Saturday accused India of having “elevated propaganda into statecraft”, embraced disinformation as diplomacy and “exported terrorism as an instrument of policy”, as Islamabad hit back at remarks made by the Indian representative at the UN General Assembly.

In a reply to the Indian representative’s statement during the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Counsellor Saima Saleem termed India a state “that has elevated propaganda into statecraft, embraced disinformation as diplomacy, exports terrorism as an instrument of policy, pursues hegemony as a regional strategy, mainstreamed Islamophobia and institutionalised Hindutva ideology”.

“The extraordinary balance sheet of today’s incredibly intolerant India. It exports terrorism and violence while trying to import victimhood and sympathy,” she said.

“Pakistan knows the cost of Indian-sponsored terrorism all too well,” she said, adding that since the turn of the century, Pakistan had lost nearly 100,000 lives to terrorism, generations had been scarred and billions of dollars had been drained from the country’s economy.

She said Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts and sacrifices had been well recognised internationally.

“We have also presented to the international community extensive evidence of India’s financing, aiding and abetting of terrorist groups targeting Pakistanis, including the TTP, BLA and Majeed Brigade,” she said.

“Yet, despite its endless lectures to others on terrorism, we are still waiting to hear India unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks that kill innocent Pakistani civilians. But how can we expect India to condemn its proxies?” she stated.

She said India’s “terrorist exports have gone from regional to global”, citing former Indian naval commander Kulbhushan Jadhav, convicted in Pakistan on terrorism and espionage charges, and Nikhil Gupta, who pleaded guilty in the United States for plotting the murder of a Sikh leader at the direction of the Indian government.

She also referred to “others implicated in assassinations carried out in Canada”.

Kashmir dispute

Turning to the Kashmir dispute, the counsellor said: “Jammu and Kashmir never was, neither is, nor will ever be an integral part of India. It is an internationally recognised disputed territory, a huge part of which is under India’s forcible and illegal occupation for nearly eight decades against the wishes of the Kashmiri people, and in gross violation of international law and numerous resolutions of the Security Council.”

“The contrast between AJK and Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir could not be more stark,” she said.

“In AJK, Kashmiris enjoy rights, participate in political life and have the freedom to express their opinions, while the people of Indian-occupied Kashmir endure decades of occupation, repression and denial of their fundamental rights and freedoms, including the inalienable right to self-determination. Rights exercised cannot be equated with rights denied,” she said.

‘Largest hypocrisy in the world’

Saima said the ruling RSS-BJP dispensation in India had “institutionalised Hindutva ideology in state policy and practice, and unleashed a reign of terror against minorities”.

“Muslims are demonised; Christians persecuted; Dalits dehumanised; and Sikhs disenfranchised in the largest hypocrisy in the world,” she said.

She said massacres of Muslims in Gujarat and Delhi under state patronage, calls for the genocide of Muslims, Islamophobic rhetoric by politicians and discriminatory citizenship laws were part of the “Hindutva project”.

Indus Waters Treaty

On the Indus Waters Treaty, Saima said that by the “so-called holding in abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and blatantly disregarding its international legal obligations, including the sanctity of treaties”, India had “stooped to a new low of weaponising water, a lifeline for the 240 million people of Pakistan”.

She said India’s “false narratives and disinformation could not hide the crushing defeat it suffered at Pakistan’s hands during Marka-i-Haq in May 2025”.

“It is well recognised by the international community that India lost more than a military conflict; it lost its credibility. Today, India can no longer import sympathy as it stands exposed in front of the world,” she said.

“As stated by my prime minister, Pakistan remains steadfast in its pursuit of peace, mutual respect, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes in our region and beyond — a commitment reflected in our consistent role as a peacemaker, mediator and bridge-builder,” she stated.

“We will defend ourselves whenever aggression is imposed upon us, but we will never abandon the path to peace; for lasting strength lies not in the wars a nation can fight, but in the peace it has the courage to build and defend.”

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”.

Addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, he said India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis, adding that the country’s position had been rejected by UN experts and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

World.title: Pakistan open FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign with 4-0 defeat against Thailand
World.content:
Pakistan opened their FIFA Asean Cup campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Thailand at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung, Indonesia, on Saturday, as Teerasak Poeiphimai struck twice and an own goal compounded the Green Shirts’ chastening introduction to the tournament.

Pakistan, ranked 198th in the world and competing as a guest side, defended in numbers during a cagey opening half hour.

Mohibullah produced a brilliant interception, and Ali Raza made a superb sliding tackle as Nolberto Solano’s men restricted Thailand to long-range efforts, with goalkeeper Yousuf Butt making a fine save on the half-hour mark.

Yousuf was powerless moments later, however, when he saved a header from Jude Soonsup-Bell only for Teerasak to tuck in the rebound and open the scoring in the 31st minute.

Thailand’s second arrived ten minutes later after captain Abdullah Iqbal’s misplaced pass led to a quick burst that ended with Soonsup-Bell slamming home from close range.

Thailand had the ball in the net again three minutes later, but the effort was ruled offside.

Pakistan needed inspiration, and coach Nolberto Solano made three substitutions at halftime, with Shayek Dost, Hayyan Khattak and Alamgir Ghazi coming on for Ali Raza, Ali Agha and Abdullah Shah.

The changes brought more enterprise, with full-backs Mohammad Fazal and Haris Zeb making forward runs, and Pakistan started the second half brightly, keeping possession and threatening without making a decisive move.

Thailand slowly grew back into the half and scored their third on the hour mark. Teerasak played a one-two with Supachai Chaided before his left-footed volley deflected off Haris Zeb and looped over goalkeeper Yousuf into the net.
